Schwerpunktland ist in diesem Jahr Norwegen, dessen Verlage mit einem eigens gestalteten Pavillon im Herzen der Halle 3 vertreten sein werden. Die Messe läuft bis zum 19. Oktober.

The Reykjavík Art Museum opens its long-awaited retrospective of Icelandic sculptor Sigríður Ólafsdóttir this Friday, drawing together more than ninety pieces spanning four decades of her career — from the monumental basalt columns of her early work to the gossamer wire installations she has produced in recent years. The exhibition, titled "Tides and Thresholds," runs through March 9th and is curated by the museum's own Benedikt Karlsson, who spent three years negotiating loans from private collections across Europe and North America.

Die Hamburger Hochbahn AG hat ab dem kommenden Montag eine Fahrpreiserhöhung von durchschnittlich 4,9 Prozent angekündigt, die sämtliche U-Bahn- und Buslinien im Hamburger Verkehrsverbund betrifft. Hintergrund sind gestiegene Energie- und Personalkosten, wie Unternehmenssprecherin Carolin Westergaard in einer Pressemitteilung erläuterte. Einzeltickets im Innenstadtbereich kosten künftig 2,60 Euro statt bisher 2,48 Euro, während Monatskarten um rund 7 Euro teurer werden. Der HVV geht davon aus, dass täglich etwa 1,3 Millionen Fahrgäste von der Anpassung betroffen sein werden.

Elspeth Morrow delivered a masterclass in the dying minutes of Saturday's Women's Championship clash at Tynecastle Park, converting a 94th-minute penalty to seal a 2–1 victory for Heart of Midlothian Women over Hibernian Women and send the Edinburgh derby crowd of 4,812 home in raptures. The result keeps Hearts four points clear at the top of the SWPL 2 table with six fixtures remaining.

A weekend of sold-out jazz performances at the Barbican Centre in London is set to coincide with severe disruptions on the Elizabeth line, after Transport for London announced that engineering works between Paddington and Liverpool Street will suspend services on both Saturday and Sunday. The Barbican's two-night residency, headlined by saxophonist Léa Fontaine and her quartet, forms the centrepiece of this year's London Jazz Festival and is expected to draw around 3,400 concertgoers across the two evenings; TfL is urging ticket-holders to allow extra travel time and consider the Central line or bus routes as alternatives. Works are scheduled to begin at 11 p.m. on Friday, 14 November and run through until 6 a.m. on Monday, 17 November, with an estimated 85,000 passengers affected over the closure period.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstag mit 54 zu 38 Stimmen bei vier Enthaltungen einen umstrittenen Beschluss zur Aufstockung des städtischen Wohnbaufonds um 280 Millionen Euro verabschiedet. SPÖ und Grüne stimmten geschlossen dafür, während ÖVP und FPÖ den Antrag als „budgetär unverantwortlich" ablehnten. Bürgermeister Michael Ludwig hatte den Vorstoß in der Vorwoche persönlich angekündigt; die tatsächliche Debatte im Rathaus dauerte knapp fünf Stunden. Stadtrat für Wohnen, Tomas Vedral, sprach nach der Abstimmung von einem „historischen Signal für leistbares Wohnen in Wien".

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, October 15, drawing publishers, agents, and literary enthusiasts from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for what organisers are billing as a landmark 76th edition. This year's guest of honour is Italy, and a programme of readings, panel discussions, and rights-trading sessions will run through Sunday, October 19. The fair's director, Katharina Reuter, said attendance was expected to surpass 285,000 visitors over the five-day event.

The Flemish parliament in Brussels passed a contentious housing reform bill on Thursday by a razor-thin margin, with 71 votes in favour and 68 against, as the governing coalition of N-VA and Vooruit overcame stiff resistance from opposition benches led by Vlaams Belang. Finance minister Lieselotte Raemdonck, who steered the legislation through three months of fractious committee hearings, called the result "a generational step toward affordable renting," while Vlaams Belang floor leader Pieter Deschamps denounced it as "a bureaucratic overreach that will throttle private landlords." The bill caps annual rent increases at 2.5 per cent and creates a new arbitration body to handle tenant disputes across the region.

Austria's parliament voted on Thursday to approve a landmark cultural funding bill, directing an additional €45 million toward regional arts institutions — a decision that prompted immediate celebration from the Wiener Festwochen, which announced the same afternoon that it would expand its 2025 programme to include a new outdoor theatre residency at the Burgtheater, featuring productions by the acclaimed director Nora Blumenstein and ensemble work from the Volksoper Wien.

Die Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe (BVG) haben angekündigt, dass ab dem 1. März 2026 die U-Bahn-Linie U5 zwischen den Stationen Hauptbahnhof und Hönow für voraussichtlich vier Wochen vollständig gesperrt wird, um dringend notwendige Gleissanierungsarbeiten durchzuführen. Rund 74.000 Fahrgäste täglich sind von der Sperrung betroffen; Ersatzbusse der Linie U5E sollen den Betrieb aufrechterhalten. Die BVG bat alle Pendlerinnen und Pendler, auf die S-Bahn Berlin oder den Regionalverkehr auszuweichen.

Commuters on the S-Bahn network in Munich faced significant delays on Monday morning after a points failure near Ostbahnhof brought services on lines S2, S4, and S6 to a near-standstill for more than three hours, leaving an estimated 47,000 passengers stranded or redirected onto replacement bus services. Deutsche Bahn, which operates the network, said engineers restored full functionality by midday but warned that residual disruptions could persist into the evening peak.

Commuters on the East Rail Line faced severe disruptions on Monday morning after a points failure near Hung Hom station forced MTR Corporation to suspend services between Hung Hom and Lo Wu for nearly four hours, with engineers working to restore full operations before the evening peak. Transport officials estimated that approximately 340,000 passengers were affected, with replacement bus services laid on along the corridor, though long queues formed at several interchange stations. MTR said repairs were completed by 1:30 p.m. and a full timetable resumed shortly after.

Der Stadtrat von Freiburg im Breisgau hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit für die Einführung einer kommunalen Klimaschutzabgabe auf gewerbliche Parkflächen gestimmt. 34 Ratsmitglieder votierten dafür, 29 dagegen, bei zwei Enthaltungen. Die Grünen und die SPD hatten den Antrag gemeinsam eingebracht, während CDU und FDP geschlossen dagegen stimmten. Bürgermeisterin Sonja Kleinhans zeigte sich erleichtert: „Das ist ein wichtiges Signal, dass Freiburg seinen Kurs in der Klimapolitik ernsthaft verfolgt."

For decades, the Frankfurter Buchmesse has served as a barometer of the publishing industry's anxieties and ambitions alike, yet few observers pause to consider the unglamorous logistics that underpin it: the freight corridors, the temporary signage, the loading bays wedged beneath Messe Frankfurt's vast exhibition halls. Tobias Wenderoth, a logistics consultant who has worked the fair since 2007, describes the operation as "a small city assembled and dismantled in under a fortnight." Whether any of that invisible infrastructure will be modernised before the fair's centenary remains, for now, an open question.

Beim packenden Kellerduell in der 3. Liga besiegte der FSV Zwickau am Samstagabend den VfB Oldenburg mit 3:1 vor ausverkauftem Haus im GGZ Arena. Die Tore für die Gastgeber erzielten Marek Vondráček (14.), Tobias Prill (58.) und Lukas Schwermann (82.), während Jonas Heitkamp in der 67. Minute für Oldenburg traf. Mit dem Sieg klettert Zwickau auf den zwölften Tabellenplatz und verlässt vorerst die Abstiegszone.

A last-gasp header from Nadia Veltri sealed a 2–1 victory for FC Lugano Women over Servette FC Chênois Féminin in front of 4,320 passionate supporters at the Cornaredo Stadium on Sunday evening, extending Lugano's lead at the top of the Nationalliga A Women's table to six points with just three rounds remaining.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run at Messe Frankfurt, drawing publishers, agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to what remains the largest trade fair for books and media in the world. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, with a programme curated by Isabella Moretti that spans literary readings, film screenings, and panel discussions on contemporary Italian fiction. Admission for the public weekend starts at €18 per person.

Am Wochenende verwandelte sich Linz in eine Doppelbühne für Kunst und Sport: Während der Österreichische Kunstverein am Samstagabend im Brucknerhaus die Vernissage der Ausstellung „Stille Landschaften" des Malers Tobias Werngruber eröffnete – rund 1.400 Besucher drängten sich durch die lichtdurchfluteten Säle –, trafen keine zwei Kilometer entfernt der LASK und Sturm Graz im Raiffeisen Arena vor 12.350 Zuschauern im Rahmen der österreichischen Bundesliga aufeinander. Das Spiel endete 2:1 für den LASK, dessen Mittelfeldspieler Florian Haindl mit einem Doppelpack die Partie entschied.

Malmö FF held off a resilient Djurgårdens IF to claim a narrow 2–1 victory at Eleda Stadion on Saturday evening, extending their unbeaten run at home to eleven matches in the Allsvenskan. Tobias Renström opened the scoring in the twenty-third minute before Djurgårdens levelled through a clinical finish by Axel Söderberg just after the interval, only for Marcus Lindvall to restore the hosts' lead with a thumping header eight minutes from time. An attendance of 19,450 witnessed one of the tighter contests of this Swedish top-flight season.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe in der Messe Frankfurt und erwartet in diesem Jahr erstmals seit der Pandemie wieder mehr als 300.000 Besucher. Gastland ist Slowenien, dessen Verleger und Autoren — darunter die Lyrikerin Vesna Radovanović und der Romanschriftsteller Andrej Kogoj — mit einem breit gefächerten Programm vertreten sein werden. Messedirektorin Lena Pfeiffer sprach von einem „Zeichen der Erneuerung für den gesamten Buchhandel".

A long-running saga of bureaucratic delay and crumbling infrastructure came to a head this week in Edinburgh, where Transport Scotland announced that the Waverley Line extension to Galashiels will be closed for emergency track repairs from Monday, 14 July through Sunday, 27 July, affecting an estimated 18,000 daily commuters on the ScotRail service. The closure is directly threatening attendance at the Borders Book Festival, which opens on Wednesday, 16 July at Harmony House in Melrose and runs for six days; festival director Catriona Meldrum confirmed that rail disruption had already prompted organisers to arrange a fleet of 12 shuttle buses from Edinburgh Waverley station, urging ticket-holders — who paid between £8 and £24 for individual events — not to cancel plans.

The Swedish Riksdag narrowly approved a sweeping overhaul of the country's housing subsidy framework on Thursday, with 176 votes in favour and 173 against, after nearly nine hours of fractious debate in which Social Democrats accused the governing coalition of "dismantling the welfare state brick by brick." Moderaterna and its junior partners — the Sweden Democrats and the Christian Democrats — held the line just barely, though two Moderate MPs broke ranks to vote with the opposition. Housing minister Britta Söderholm hailed the result as "a long-overdue correction," while Social Democrat floor leader Mikael Rantanen vowed an immediate legal challenge before the Constitutional Committee.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opened its doors on Wednesday to a record 4,312 exhibitors from 95 countries, with this year's guest of honour being Slovenia — a designation that brought a wave of Slovenian novelists, poets, and translators to the Frankfurt fairgrounds for the first time in such numbers. Curator Maja Vreš, who has championed Central European literature for over a decade, assembled a programme of readings, panel debates, and live translation workshops spread across Hall 3.1 and the newly refurbished Agora stage. Tickets for the public weekend are priced at €18 per day.

The Galway City Council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a controversial rezoning plan that would open 340 hectares of greenbelt land on the city's eastern fringe to mixed-use development, with 17 councillors in favour, 14 against, and 3 abstentions. The measure, championed by Fine Gael and Fianna Fáil representatives on the council, was fiercely opposed by the Green Party and Sinn Féin, who argued that the move would irreparably damage wetland habitats and undermine the city's climate commitments. Council Chairwoman Aoife Ní Fhaoláin told reporters the decision had been "neither easy nor unanimous" but insisted that housing supply pressures left the council with few alternatives.

Rowan Szymański delivered a masterclass in clinical finishing on Saturday as his brace powered FC Wrocław Athletic to a 3-1 victory over Górnik Zabrze at the Stadion Miejski, pulling the hosts clear of the relegation zone and deepening the visitors' mid-table anxieties in the Ekstraklasa. A crowd of 18,400 watched Szymański open the scoring inside seven minutes before setting up Dominika Wierzbicka for the second, with Jakub Ostrowski completing the rout from the penalty spot in the 78th minute.

The Vienna Philharmonic's long-awaited three-night residency at the Musikverein, headlined by conductor Lieselotte Brandauer and featuring tenor Maksym Chornovil, opens on Friday 18 April — but festivalgoers travelling by U-Bahn should plan ahead: Wiener Linien has announced that the U4 line will be suspended between Karlsplatz and Hütteldorf from Thursday 17 April through Sunday 20 April for emergency track-bed repairs, with replacement buses running every eight minutes throughout the closure.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, literary agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds — a sprawling assembly of halls that this year devotes a landmark pavilion to Slovenian literature, the designated Guest of Honour. Chief organiser Jürgen Boos described the programme as "the most internationally ambitious in a decade," with headline appearances by novelists Mareta Kowalczyk and Dragan Šešić scheduled across the opening weekend.

The Salzburg regional parliament narrowly approved a controversial housing affordability package on Thursday, with 23 votes in favour and 19 against, after nearly four hours of fractious debate during which ÖVP floor leader Markus Eberharter accused the opposition Grüne of "stalling tactics designed to serve urban landlords rather than working families." The SPÖ, whose support proved decisive, said it had extracted written commitments on rent caps before crossing the aisle.

Wegen des Bundesliga-Heimspiels des FC St. Pauli gegen Bayer 04 Leverkusen am Samstag, den 18. Januar, sperrt die Hamburger Hochbahn von 14 bis 22 Uhr die U3-Haltestelle Feldstraße und richtet Pendelbusse zwischen Schlump und Messehallen ein. Erwartet werden rund 29.500 Zuschauer im Millerntor-Stadion, wo die Partie um 15:30 Uhr angepfiffen wird; Fahrgäste werden gebeten, frühzeitig auf S-Bahn-Verbindungen auszuweichen.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect to draw more than 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with this year's guest of honour nation being Italy — represented by a delegation of over 200 authors, including the celebrated novelist Chiara Dentale, whose latest work appears in English translation for the first time. Literary agents, publishers and readers from some 100 countries will converge on Hall 3 for a slate of readings, panel discussions and rights negotiations that stretch from dawn to dusk, making it once again the largest trade fair for books in the world.

Beim packenden Stadtderby in der Regionalliga Südwest setzte sich der SV Waldhof Mannheim am Samstagabend mit 3:1 gegen den FC-Astoria Walldorf durch. Vor 8.200 Zuschauern im Carl-Benz-Stadion war der überragende Mittelfeldmann Lukas Drenkhahn mit einem Doppelpack der entscheidende Faktor für die Hausherren. Für den Anschlusstreffer der Gäste sorgte Miroslav Čapek per Freistoß in der 67. Minute – ein Aufbäumen, das letztlich ohne Wirkung blieb.

Chicago's transit authority confirmed Thursday that planned track maintenance on the Red Line will force full service suspensions between Belmont and Howard stations from the night of January 31 through February 3, affecting an estimated 47,000 daily commuters. The Chicago Transit Authority said replacement bus services will run every six minutes along the corridor, though riders should expect journey times roughly double those of the express rail service. The $28 million upgrade, which includes rail grinding and signal cabinet replacements at three stations, has been in the works since mid-2023.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to reject a proposed amendment to the Housing (Emergency Provisions) Bill that would have capped private rent increases at two percent annually, with 63 members voting against and 58 in favour, after a fractious three-hour debate in which Scottish Labour and the Scottish Conservatives united in opposition to the SNP-backed measure. "This is a missed opportunity for hundreds of thousands of renters," said Catriona Drummond, the SNP's housing spokeswoman, who had championed the clause since its introduction in February.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to extend free bus travel to asylum seekers currently housed in temporary accommodation across the country, with 67 members backing the measure, 59 opposing it, and four abstaining. The bill, championed by Transport Minister Catriona Dunbar of the SNP and fiercely contested by Scottish Conservative leader Alasdair Muir, passed despite last-minute lobbying from business groups who warned of budgetary strain on regional operators. "This is about dignity and basic mobility," Dunbar told Holyrood, "not a political gesture."

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect to draw more than 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, where roughly 4,200 exhibitors from over 100 countries will present new titles spanning fiction, academic publishing, and children's literature. This year's guest of honour is Italy, and the Italian Publishers Association has curated a sprawling pavilion tracing the country's contemporary literary scene from Milan to Palermo. "No other fair concentrates this much creative energy in one place," said fair director Klara Seifenbach at Tuesday's press briefing.

The Wiener Konzerthaus will open its winter season on 4 November with a sold-out performance by the Mahler Chamber Orchestra under the baton of conductor Lena Vaskevičiūtė, whose programme pairs Sibelius's Seventh Symphony with a world première of a string concerto by the Icelandic composer Árni Þórðarson. Ticket prices ranged from €18 to €95, and all 1,840 seats were claimed within forty-eight hours of going on sale.

The Wiener Festwochen announced Thursday that Algerian-French director Nadia Boussalem will helm the opening production of this year's festival, a sprawling adaptation of Ibn Battuta's travel chronicles staged at the Burgtheater beginning on May 16 and running through June 1. Organisers expect the eight-hour work — performed in Arabic, Darija, and French with German surtitles — to draw audiences from across Europe, with tickets priced at €45 for general admission.

The Flemish parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a sweeping package of childcare subsidies, with 72 members in favour and 63 opposed, after nearly six hours of fractious debate in which the N-VA and Vooruit clashed repeatedly over means-testing provisions. The bill's sponsor, junior minister Lotte Verstraeten, called the result "a hard-won step forward for working families across Flanders," while opposition leader Dries Claes of the Vlaams Belang dismissed it as "a fig-leaf compromise that will help almost nobody."

The Scottish Parliament voted on Thursday to approve a sweeping package of rent-control measures for the private housing sector, with the Scottish National Party and the Scottish Greens combining to secure a majority of 72 votes to 51, with four abstentions. The bill, championed by Housing Minister Catriona Dunbar, had faced fierce opposition from Conservative MSPs, who warned the legislation would deter investment in new residential construction. Labour abstained, with its deputy leader Ewan Murchie calling the measures "well-intentioned but structurally flawed." The result marks the first time Holyrood has passed binding rent controls since devolution.

The Reykjavik City Council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a controversial rezoning plan that would open several protected green corridors along the Elliðaár river to mixed-use development, with 13 councillors in favour, 9 against, and 2 abstentions — a result that drew immediate condemnation from the opposition Vinstrihreyfingin–grænt framboð, whose spokeswoman Þórunn Sigríður Gestsdóttir warned that the decision "sets a precedent we will spend a generation undoing."

Galatasaray came from behind to defeat Fenerbahçe 3–2 in a ferocious Istanbul derby at RAMS Park on Sunday, with midfielder Kerem Sarıoğlu netting the decisive goal in the 87th minute to send the home faithful into raptures. The victory, watched by a sell-out crowd of 52,400, extends Galatasaray's lead at the top of the Süper Lig to seven points with nine rounds remaining.

Commuters on Oslo's T-bane network faced significant delays on Monday morning after a signalling fault between Stortinget and Nationaltheatret stations brought all five lines to a standstill for nearly three hours, stranding an estimated 47,000 passengers during the morning peak. Ruter, the regional transit authority, deployed additional bus services along Karl Johans gate as a temporary workaround, but queues stretched well beyond Jernbanetorget. Engineers confirmed the fault was repaired by 10:45 a.m., and full service on lines T1 through T5 was restored shortly afterwards.

Die Münchner Philharmoniker eröffnen am 14. März ihre neue Konzertreihe „Klang der Kontinente" im Gasteig HP8 mit einem Programm, das Werke von Arvo Pärt, Camille Saint-Saëns und der zeitgenössischen Komponistin Leilani Akana vereint. Chefdirigent Marek Vyšný übernimmt dabei das Pult, unterstützt von der Mezzosopranistin Theodora Brandt als Solistin. Karten sind ab 22 Euro erhältlich; die Reihe läuft bis zum 28. Juni.

Beim packenden Halbfinale der Deutschen Meisterschaft im Fechten setzte sich die Fechterin Lena Vorderwülbecke aus Heidelberg am Samstag in der Stuttgarter Hanns-Martin-Schleyer-Halle mit 15:11 gegen die Favoritin Sonja Grabowski durch und zog damit souverän ins Finale ein. Vor rund 2.400 Zuschauern bewies Vorderwülbecke eine bemerkenswerte taktische Reife, während Grabowski trotz zahlreicher Angriffskombinationen nie wirklich ins Spiel fand.

The Austrian capital braced for severe traffic disruption on Saturday as the Vienna Marathon drew an estimated 42,000 runners through the city centre, prompting Wiener Linien to suspend tram services on lines 1, 2, and D between Schwedenplatz and the Burgring from 7 a.m. until approximately 2 p.m. Race director Marta Hofer confirmed that Ethiopian favourite Dawit Gebre crossed the finish line at Heldenplatz in a course-record time of 2:04:38, edging out Kenya's Samuel Rotich by just eleven seconds in what officials called one of the closest elite finishes in the event's history.

The Reykjavík City Council narrowly approved a sweeping housing affordability motion on Thursday evening, with councillors voting 11 to 8 in favour after nearly four hours of heated debate. The measure, championed by councillor Sigríður Ólafsdóttir of the Left-Green Movement, would cap annual rent increases at two per cent and oblige the municipality to build at least 400 new social housing units by 2027. Conservative coalition partners Independence Party voiced fierce opposition, calling the caps "economically illiterate," though they failed to muster enough votes to block the motion. Mayor Gunnar Benediktsson, who had remained conspicuously neutral throughout the proceedings, signed the resolution into the record shortly before midnight.

Die Berliner S-Bahn wird in der Nacht vom 14. auf den 15. März wegen dringender Gleiserneuerungsarbeiten im Abschnitt zwischen Ostbahnhof und Erkner vollständig gesperrt; Reisende werden gebeten, auf die parallel verkehrenden RB-Linien der Deutschen Bahn auszuweichen. Nach Angaben der S-Bahn Berlin GmbH sind rund 38.000 Fahrgäste von der Maßnahme betroffen. Die Sperrung dauert voraussichtlich sieben Stunden.

Denmark's Folketing narrowly approved a landmark climate bill on Thursday, with 91 votes in favour and 84 against, after weeks of fractious debate that had threatened to collapse the ruling coalition. The legislation, championed by Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen's Social Democrats and backed reluctantly by the Danish Social Liberal Party, commits Copenhagen to reducing carbon emissions by 70 percent ahead of the 2030 deadline. Opposition leader Søren Dalgaard of the Danish People's Party condemned the bill as "economically reckless," warning that rural constituencies would bear a disproportionate burden of the transition costs.

Beim packenden Abendspiel im Weserstadion setzte sich Werder Bremen am Freitagabend mit 3:1 gegen den FC Schalke 04 durch und kletterte damit auf den dritten Tabellenplatz der 2. Bundesliga. Torschütze Lennart Böhme traf doppelt in der zweiten Halbzeit, während Nico Pasveer den Ehrentreffer für die Gäste erzielte. Vor ausverkauftem Haus verfolgten 42.100 Zuschauer das Duell, das Werder-Trainer Mateusz Górski als „verdienten Schritt in die richtige Richtung" bezeichnete.

Wegen des Halbfinals im DFB-Pokal zwischen dem FC Kaiserslautern und Bayer 04 Leverkusen im Fritz Walter Stadion am Dienstagabend hat die Verkehrsgesellschaft Kaiserslautern (VKU) für die Nacht von Dienstag auf Mittwoch Sonderbusse auf den Linien 101, 103 und 115 eingesetzt, um die rund 42.000 Zuschauer nach dem Abpfiff geordnet in die Innenstadt und die umliegenden Stadtteile zu befördern. Das Spiel endete nach Verlängerung mit 3:2 für Leverkusen, wobei der eingewechselte Stürmer Tomáš Vrábel mit einem Doppelpack in der Nachspielzeit für die Entscheidung sorgte.

Leinster edged out Glasgow Warriors 27–24 in a tense United Rugby Championship encounter at the Aviva Stadium on Saturday evening, with fly-half Ciarán Doherty slotting a late penalty to seal the win in front of a crowd of 48,300. Glasgow, who had led by six points entering the final quarter, will rue a string of handling errors that gifted the hosts two crucial turnovers. The result keeps Leinster firmly atop the URC standings with six wins from seven outings this season.

Tens of thousands of cycling fans descended on Innsbruck on Saturday for the final stage of the Tour of the Alps, where Italian climber Marco Selvaggi sealed a dramatic overall victory at the Bergisel finish line — only to face a chaotic journey home as ÖBB suspended all regional rail services between Innsbruck and Brenner Pass for the remainder of the weekend, citing emergency track repairs following a subsidence detected south of Matrei am Brenner. The rail operator estimated that roughly 28,000 passengers would be affected and advised travellers to use replacement bus services laid on along the A13 motorway corridor.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect to draw upwards of 300,000 visitors, with Norwegian literature taking centre stage as the guest-of-honour theme. Among the highlights, debut novelist Ingrid Solberg-Naastad will read from her debut collection at the Festhalle on Thursday evening, while the Norwegian Publishers Association has assembled a pavilion spanning nearly 2,000 square metres in Hall 4.2. Ticket prices for public days start at €18.

Beim packenden Stadtderby in der 2. Bundesliga trennten sich der VfL Bochum und Borussia Dortmund II am Freitagabend im Ruhrstadion mit einem 2:2-Unentschieden vor 23.400 Zuschauern. Tor-Schützen für die Gastgeber waren Marek Svoboda und Lennart Kühne, während auf Dortmunder Seite Adrián Fuentes beide Treffer erzielte. Mit diesem Ergebnis verpasste Bochum die Chance, den zweiten Tabellenplatz zu festigen.

Wegen eines Signalschadens zwischen den Stationen Ostbahnhof und Rosenheimer Platz ist die S-Bahn-Linie S3 in München seit dem frühen Dienstagmorgen teilweise unterbrochen. Die S-Bahn München teilte mit, dass Züge zwischen Pasing und Ostbahnhof im 20-Minuten-Takt verkehren, während Fahrgäste für den östlichen Abschnitt auf die U-Bahn-Linien U4 und U5 ausweichen sollen. Nach Schätzungen der Betreiberin sind rund 38.000 Pendler von den Beeinträchtigungen betroffen. Eine Wiederherstellung des regulären Betriebs wird frühestens bis Mittwochnachmittag erwartet.

Mit einer ausverkauften Uraufführung im Wiener Konzerthaus hat die Komponistin Sofía Brenntner am Freitagabend ihr erstes Streichquartett einem begeisterten Publikum präsentiert. Das Ensemble Resonanz aus Hamburg übernahm die Interpretation des knapp vierzigminütigen Werks, das Brenntner als „einen Dialog zwischen Stille und Klang" bezeichnete. Karten für die Veranstaltung waren bereits drei Wochen im Voraus zu Preisen zwischen 18 und 45 Euro vergriffen.

Der Regionalverkehr zwischen Salzburg und Freilassing wird in der Nacht vom 14. auf den 15. März vollständig eingestellt, nachdem ÖBB-Techniker bei Routinekontrollen schwere Schäden an der Weichenanlage im Bahnhof Salzburg Hauptbahnhof festgestellt haben. Rund 4.200 Pendlerinnen und Pendler sind von der Sperrung betroffen. Als Ersatz richtet die ÖBB einen Schienenersatzverkehr mit Bussen ein, der laut Unternehmenssprecherin Veronika Haslinger jedoch deutlich längere Fahrzeiten mit sich bringt. Die Reparaturarbeiten sollen bis zum 17. März abgeschlossen sein.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to pass the Renewable Heat Transition Bill, with 68 members in favour, 55 against, and 4 abstentions, marking what the SNP's energy spokesperson Catriona Gilfillan called "a generational shift in how Scotland heats its homes." The Scottish Conservatives, who led the opposition to the measure, argued that the timeline for phasing out gas boilers by 2032 was reckless and would burden lower-income households. Labour MSPs were split, with several breaking ranks to support the government.

Copenhagen's city council approved a landmark €2.3 billion expansion of the Metro network by 34 votes to 11 on Thursday, with the governing Social Democrats and their Green allies overcoming fierce resistance from the Liberal Alliance, which had argued the project would saddle taxpayers with unsustainable debt. The approved plan, championed by transport councillor Astrid Nørgaard, will add seven new stations along a southern harbour loop and is expected to carry an estimated 85,000 additional passengers daily once the line enters service in 2031. Construction firm Ørsted Rail Consortium was awarded the primary contract, and the city's transit operator Movia confirmed it would coordinate interim bus services across the affected corridors from as early as March 2026.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to pass the Housing Affordability (Emergency Measures) Bill, with 68 members backing the legislation and 55 voting against, following a bruising three-hour debate in which opposition MSPs from the Scottish Conservatives accused the SNP-led government of overreaching landlord regulation powers. First Minister Catriona Llewellyn-Ross, who staked considerable personal authority on the bill's passage, hailed the result as "a landmark moment for renters across Scotland," while Scottish Conservative leader Alistair Dunbar condemned it as an assault on the private rental market. Holyrood observers noted that three Labour members broke ranks to support the government, providing the decisive votes that pushed the bill over the threshold.

Kristoffer Haugen delivered a masterclass in front of a sold-out Ullevaal Stadion on Saturday, scoring twice as Vålerenga dismantled visiting Brann 3–1 to move to the summit of the Eliteserien table. Midfielder Tone Fjeldberg added the third in stoppage time, extinguishing any hope of a late Bergen comeback. Attendance was recorded at 27,412.

Beim packenden Halbfinale der Deutschen Volleyball-Meisterschaft bezwang der VfB Friedrichshafen am Samstag den Berliner SC mit 3:1 in der ZF Arena und zog damit souverän ins Endspiel ein. Vor 4.200 Zuschauern ragte Außenangreifer Tobias Wernecke mit insgesamt 22 Punkten heraus und ließ dem Gegner kaum eine Chance im dritten und vierten Satz.

The Finnish parliament narrowly passed a sweeping austerity budget on Thursday, with 104 votes in favour and 95 against, after a bruising overnight debate that exposed deep fault lines between the ruling National Coalition Party and its junior partner, the Finns Party. Finance Minister Kaarina Mäkelä, who steered the bill through committee last month, called the outcome "a painful but necessary step," while opposition leader Petri Sundqvist of the Social Democrats warned that cuts to housing subsidies would hollow out the welfare state within a decade.

The city of Salzburg celebrated a memorable weekend as the Mozarteum Foundation unveiled a sold-out chamber music festival, "Resonanz," at the Großes Festspielhaus on Saturday, featuring violinist Lena Broschek and cellist Tomáš Červenka in a programme spanning Schubert and Shostakovich — while across town, Red Bull Salzburg dismantled Wolfsberger AC 4–1 at the Red Bull Arena in an Austrian Bundesliga fixture before a crowd of 28,500, with forward Miloš Petrović scoring a hat-trick to cement his side's lead at the top of the table.

Fußball-Zweitligist FC Erzgebirge Aue hat am Samstagabend im Erzgebirgsstadion einen hart erkämpften 2:1-Heimsieg gegen den SV Wehen Wiesbaden eingefahren. Vor 8.450 Zuschauern traf Mittelfeldspieler Jonas Przybylski in der 78. Minute zum entscheidenden Tor, nachdem Stürmer Marek Holub Aue kurz nach der Halbzeit in Führung gebracht hatte. Mit diesem Erfolg klettert Aue auf den fünften Tabellenplatz der 2. Bundesliga.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to reject a proposed bill that would have granted local councils expanded powers over short-term letting platforms, with 64 members voting against the measure and 59 in favour, amid fierce opposition from the Scottish Conservative Party and a handful of dissident SNP backbenchers. Deputy First Minister Catriona Lyle, who had championed the legislation, called the result "a missed opportunity for communities blighted by the holiday-let market," while Scottish Conservative housing spokesperson Alistair Dunmore argued that the bill would have placed an undue burden on small property owners. The bill's failure is expected to reignite debate within the SNP about internal party discipline ahead of the 2026 Holyrood elections.

The Scottish Parliament passed a landmark housing affordability bill on Thursday by a margin of 73 votes to 44, with 6 abstentions, after a fractious three-hour debate in which SNP ministers clashed sharply with Conservative backbenchers over proposed rent controls in Edinburgh and Glasgow. The bill, championed by Housing Secretary Catriona Dunbar, would cap annual private rent increases at 3 percent across all local authority areas — a measure the Scottish Conservatives' leader, Alasdair Pryce, condemned as "economically reckless." Scottish Labour voted alongside the SNP to secure the majority.

Tens of thousands of supporters descending on Dortmund for Saturday's Bundesliga derby between Borussia Dortmund and Schalke 04 at Signal Iduna Park caused severe overcrowding on U-Bahn lines U45 and U46, prompting Deutsche Bahn and the Dortmund transit authority DSW21 to deploy twelve additional trains and suspend private vehicle access along Strobelallee from 14:00 until well after the final whistle. The match itself ended 3–1 to the hosts, with midfielder Luca Brandt netting a brace, before a crowd of 81,365.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organizers expect to draw upward of 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with Norwegian literature taking centre stage as the guest-of-honour theme this year. Publisher Ingrid Solberg-Haugen, whose debut novel "Saltwater Roads" has already sold briskly in translation across fourteen countries, will deliver the opening keynote, while the Norwegian Publishers Association is co-hosting a series of panel discussions on Nordic noir and climate fiction throughout the week.

Der Stadtrat von Erfurt hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einen umstrittenen Haushaltsentwurf für das kommende Jahr verabschiedet: 27 Ratsmitglieder stimmten dafür, 21 dagegen, bei vier Enthaltungen. Bürgermeisterin Karoline Wendt von der SPD bezeichnete das Ergebnis als „schmerzhaften, aber notwendigen Kompromiss", während die CDU-Fraktion unter Fraktionschef Tobias Irmler das Votum als „verantwortungslos" kritisierte. Besonders umstritten war der geplante Stellenabbau im öffentlichen Dienst sowie die Erhöhung der Grundsteuer um zwölf Prozent.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to reject a proposed amendment to the Housing (Scotland) Bill that would have capped private rent increases at two per cent annually, with 63 members voting against and 58 in favour, after a heated debate in which Scottish Labour MSPs broke ranks with the SNP-led government and sided with Conservative opposition benches. Housing minister Fionnuala Drennan insisted the administration would bring forward a revised framework before the end of the parliamentary term, while Conservative housing spokesperson Callum Raeburn called the outcome "a long-overdue correction of course."

ÖBB has confirmed that engineering works on the Westbahn corridor between Salzburg and Linz will force a complete suspension of intercity rail services for eleven days beginning 14 March, with replacement coaches laid on at all affected stations. The Austrian federal railway estimates that around 47,000 passengers per day will face significantly extended journey times during the closure, which is required to install new overhead line equipment as part of the broader Westring electrification upgrade. Travellers are advised to allow an additional ninety minutes for any connection through the corridor.

Copenhagen's much-anticipated Øresund Sound Festival will open at the Royal Danish Playhouse on 14 June, drawing chamber ensembles and electroacoustic composers from across Scandinavia for a five-day programme curated by festival director Maja Thorsbjerg. The timing coincides with a significant expansion of the Metro Cityringen line, with operator Metroselskabet set to inaugurate three new stations — Sydhavn, Mozarts Plads, and Sluseholmen — on the same date, a move expected to bring an additional 28,000 commuters daily into the city centre and ease access to the waterfront venue.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to pass the Renewable Heating Transition Bill, with 67 members in favour and 59 against, after a bruising three-hour chamber debate in which Scottish National Party backbenchers broke ranks to side with Scottish Labour and the Scottish Greens. Deputy First Minister Catriona Elphinstone, who had staked considerable political capital on the legislation, called the result "a generational step toward a warmer, fairer Scotland," while Conservative MSP Alasdair Drummond-Ross condemned the bill as "a ruinous imposition on rural households already struggling with energy costs."

Rostock Seagulls edged out Hannover Wanderers 2–1 in a tense third-round cup tie at the DKB Arena on Saturday evening, with a late penalty from midfielder Tomasz Wierzbicki sealing the result in front of 14,200 spectators. Hannover's Erol Şimşek had briefly levelled matters just before the hour mark, but the hosts ultimately held firm to advance to the quarterfinals of the DFB-Pokal.

The Scottish Parliament voted on Thursday to approve a landmark arts-funding bill that will earmark £40 million annually for community cultural programmes, with 89 votes in favour and 31 against — a result hailed by Culture Secretary Fiona Glenross as "a turning point for grassroots creativity." The legislation clears the way for the Edinburgh International Festival to expand its free public programming, and organisers have already confirmed that the festival's 2025 edition will open on 1 August at the Ross Bandstand with a commission from Glasgow-based composer Alasdair Muir.

The Wiener Konzerthaus will host a two-night retrospective of works by the Icelandic composer Sigríður Magnúsdóttir on 14 and 15 March, featuring the Vienna Radio Symphony Orchestra under the baton of conductor Pétur Halldórsson. The programme spans three decades of Magnúsdóttir's output, from austere early chamber pieces to her sprawling 2019 orchestral suite "Vetrarljós," and tickets are priced at €28 for gallery seats. Organizers at the Nordic Sound Initiative have described the event as the most comprehensive survey of her music ever staged in continental Europe.

Commuters on the Øresund cross-border rail corridor faced severe disruptions Monday after Banedanmark engineers discovered a fractured overhead wire between Malmö Central and Copenhagen Airport, forcing Øresundståg to suspend all services on the line for what officials said could stretch to three days. An estimated 47,000 daily passengers were affected, with Skånetrafiken advising travellers to board replacement coaches running every twenty minutes from Hyllie station. "Repair crews are working around the clock," a spokesperson for Banedanmark told reporters, adding that a full inspection of the catenary system along the entire corridor had been ordered.

Beim packenden Halbfinale der Deutschen Meisterschaft im Ringen am Samstag in der Messehalle Dortmund besiegte der AC Ringen Freiburg den KSV Kölnstadion mit 5:3 und zog damit souverän ins Finale ein. Vor 2.400 Zuschauern war es vor allem Jonas Wehrheim, der mit zwei entscheidenden Schultersiegen die Weichen stellte und zum Matchwinner avancierte.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to reject a proposed reform to the country's land ownership laws, with 64 members voting against the bill and 59 in favour, dealing a significant blow to First Minister Catriona Dunbar and her Scottish Green-backed administration. The measure, championed by Rural Affairs Secretary Alasdair Muir, would have imposed stricter caps on the size of private estates and compelled large landowners to offer right-of-first-refusal to local communities. Opposition was led by the Scottish Conservatives, whose spokesman Euan Forsyth argued the legislation amounted to "an assault on property rights that would chill rural investment for a generation."

Commuters on the Merseyrail network faced severe disruption on Thursday after a signalling fault near Lime Street Station brought services on both the Northern and Wirral lines to a near-standstill for close to five hours, stranding an estimated 34,000 passengers across Merseyside. Merseyrail said replacement bus services were deployed along key corridors but warned that journey times would remain significantly extended well into the evening peak. The operator attributed the fault to ageing track-side infrastructure and said a full engineering assessment was under way.

A last-gasp header from striker Tomáš Bednář sealed a dramatic 2–1 victory for FK Hradec Králové over Zbrojovka Brno at Malšovická aréna on Saturday, keeping the hosts three points clear at the top of the Fortuna:Liga table with just four rounds remaining. Bednář, who had been largely anonymous for the first hour of play, met a deep Ondřej Fišer cross in the 89th minute to send the sold-out crowd of 7,200 into raptures.

The Flemish parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to adopt a sweeping housing reform package championed by the centre-right N-VA, with 71 members backing the bill against 64 opposed and 5 abstaining. The legislation, which caps rent increases at 2.5 percent annually and mandates energy-efficiency upgrades for all rental properties by 2031, had been fiercely contested by the Greens and the socialist Vooruit, whose spokeswoman Liesbet Claes accused the governing coalition of "handing landlords a shield while tenants freeze." N-VA housing minister Wouter Desmedt called the vote "a generational step forward for Flemish families."

Borussia Dortmund edged out Bayer Leverkusen 2–1 in a tense Saturday evening Bundesliga clash at Signal Iduna Park, with striker Tomáš Vrábel netting a stoppage-time winner to send the 81,365-strong crowd into raptures. Leverkusen had levelled through a penalty just after the hour, threatening to deny the hosts all three points until Vrábel's decisive header in the fourth minute of added time.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, literary agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. Among this year's headliners are novelist Adaeze Nwofor, whose debut in German translation arrives just in time for the fair, and veteran Swiss essayist Lorenz Huguenin-Virchaux, who will deliver the opening lecture on Thursday morning. The Guest of Honour pavilion this year belongs to Norway, with a programme curated by Oslo-based arts foundation Kulturrådet stretching across all five days of the fair.

Der Stadtrat von Graz hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einem umstrittenen Wohnbauprogramm zugestimmt, das den Bau von 1.200 geförderten Mietwohnungen in den nächsten fünf Jahren vorsieht. Mit 28 Stimmen dafür, 19 dagegen und drei Enthaltungen setzte sich die Koalition aus ÖVP und SPÖ gegen die Oppositionsparteien FPÖ und Grüne durch. Stadtrat Benedikt Harrer (ÖVP), der das Programm federführend ausgearbeitet hatte, sprach von einem „historischen Schritt für leistbares Wohnen in Graz". Die Grünen kritisierten hingegen, das Programm vernachlässige ökologische Baustandards vollständig.

Wegen des Bundesliga-Derbys zwischen dem FC St. Pauli und dem Hamburger SV am Samstag, dem 18. Januar 2025, im Volksparkstadion rechnet die Hamburger Hochbahn AG mit erheblichen Beeinträchtigungen auf den U-Bahn-Linien U2 und U3 rund um den Stadionbereich. Die Behörde kündigte an, ab 16 Uhr zusätzliche Züge im Fünf-Minuten-Takt einzusetzen, um die erwarteten 57.000 Zuschauer zu bewältigen; dennoch müssen Fahrgäste zwischen 15 und 23 Uhr mit Verspätungen von bis zu 20 Minuten rechnen. Das Hinspiel hatte der HSV mit 2:1 für sich entschieden, doch St.-Pauli-Stürmer Luca Brandt schwor nach dem Abpfiff, das Blatt diesmal zu wenden.

Die Ausstellung „Zwischenräume – Fotografie der Stille" wird ab dem 14. März im Münchner Stadtmuseum zu sehen sein und versammelt Arbeiten von zwölf internationalen Künstlerinnen und Künstlern, die sich mit verlassenen Industriegebieten im Ruhrgebiet auseinandersetzen. Kuratorin Lena Varosević hat die Schau über drei Jahre hinweg zusammengetragen; Eintritt kostet 9 Euro. Bis zum 1. Juni bleibt die Ausstellung geöffnet.

Commuters in Mannheim faced significant disruption on Monday after RNV, the Rhine-Neckar transit authority, suspended tram services on lines 1, 3, and 5 through the city centre following an overnight water main burst near Paradeplatz that left sections of the track bed unstable. Engineers estimated repairs would take at least four days, during which an estimated 47,000 daily passengers will be diverted onto replacement bus services. RNV said it was coordinating with the city of Mannheim to waive bus surcharges for affected tram ticket holders throughout the closure period.

Reigning champions Dynamo Brno edged out Spartak Olomouc 3–2 in a breathless Czech First League clash at the Městský stadion on Saturday evening, with midfielder Tomáš Vrábel sealing the victory with a curling strike in the 87th minute before a crowd of 11,400.

Die Kunstmesse art Karlsruhe eröffnet am 20. Februar ihre einundzwanzigste Ausgabe in der Messe Karlsruhe und versammelt bis zum 23. Februar rund 200 Galerien aus achtzehn Ländern unter einem Dach. Kuratorisch verantwortet wird die diesjährige Sonderschau „Figur und Raum" von der Münchener Kunsthistorikerin Petra Vogelmann, die dabei einen thematischen Bogen von klassischer Skulptur bis zu zeitgenössischer Rauminstallation spannt. Der Eintritt für Tagesbesucher beträgt 18 Euro.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to pass a motion of no confidence in the devolved government's housing minister, Catriona Belhaven, after a damaging week in which two separate inquiries found her department had misallocated nearly £4.2 million in affordable-housing grants — a result that opposition parties, led by Scottish Labour and the Scottish Conservatives, described as long overdue and that now forces First Minister Alasdair Munro to consider a cabinet reshuffle before the new year.

The Scottish Parliament approved a sweeping new housing affordability bill on Thursday by a margin of 73 votes to 44, with 6 abstentions, after a fractious three-hour debate in which SNP backbenchers clashed openly with Labour and Conservative members over proposed rent caps for Edinburgh and Glasgow. Deputy First Minister Catriona Mhairi Dunbar, who steered the legislation through committee, called the result "a historic step for tenants across Scotland," while opposition spokesperson Reuben Aldcroft described the caps as "economically reckless." The Scottish Greens, whose 7 votes proved decisive, had extracted a last-minute concession extending protections to short-term let properties before lending their support.

Beim diesjährigen Alpenklang-Festival in Innsbruck, das am Samstag im Tiroler Landestheater eröffnet wurde, sorgte das Ensemble Resonanz mit einem mitreißenden Programm aus alpiner Volksmusik und zeitgenössischer Komposition für stehende Ovationen vor rund 1.200 Besuchern. Nur wenige Stunden später, ebenfalls am Samstag, errang der FC Wacker Innsbruck in der Tivoli-Arena einen knappen 2:1-Sieg gegen den FC Lustenau im Rahmen der 2. Bundesliga und festigte damit seinen zweiten Tabellenplatz.

Die Hamburger Kunsthalle eröffnet am kommenden Freitag eine großangelegte Retrospektive der norwegischen Malerin Astrid Veum, die rund 140 Werke aus vier Jahrzehnten ihres Schaffens vereint und damit erstmals in Deutschland einen umfassenden Überblick über ihr von skandinavischer Landschaft und Licht geprägtes Werk bietet. Kuratorin der Ausstellung ist Dr. Marlene Brückfeld; die Schau ist bis zum 18. Mai 2025 zu sehen, der Eintritt beträgt 16 Euro.

Benedikt Haugen's composed finish in the 83rd minute sealed a hard-fought 2–1 victory for Rosenborg BK over Vålerenga at Lerkendal Stadion on Saturday, keeping the Trondheim club atop the Eliteserien table with four matches to play. Haugen's match-winning strike, set up by a deft through-ball from Simen Aabø, sparked jubilant scenes among the 17,420 supporters packed into the ground.

A weekend of clashing schedules threatens to test Edinburgh's transport network this Saturday, as ÖBB's Scottish rail partner ScotRail has warned of severe disruptions on the Waverley Line due to emergency track repairs between Galashiels and Edinburgh Waverley, leaving an estimated 18,000 passengers to seek alternative travel — an inconvenient coincidence for the Edinburgh International Festival, which opens its 78th edition at the Usher Hall on the same day, with Latvian conductor Līva Kalniņa leading the Scottish Chamber Orchestra in a programme of Shostakovich and Pärt before packed houses expected to number 2,200 nightly.

The Flemish parliament narrowly approved a new language-in-the-workplace directive on Thursday, with 72 votes in favour, 58 against, and 4 abstentions, after a fractious overnight debate in which the N-VA and Vlaams Belang pushed the measure through over sustained objections from Vooruit and the Greens. The policy would require all employers in the Brussels Capital Region with more than twenty staff to conduct formal internal communications exclusively in Dutch, a provision that critics labelled discriminatory and legally precarious. Flemish Minister-President Pieter Vanderschaaf — a fictional name standing in for the chair of the government — called the vote "a historic step toward protecting our language and our identity."

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to extend free bus travel to all residents under the age of 25, with 68 members backing the measure against 55 opposed and 4 abstaining — a policy championed by Transport Minister Fiona Glenross, who called the expansion "a generational shift in how young Scots move through their country." The Scottish National Party and the Scottish Greens combined to push the bill through, while Scottish Labour and the Scottish Conservatives argued that funding for the scheme remained dangerously vague. The legislation will now pass to Holyrood for royal assent before coming into force on 1 March 2026.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to advance a bill tightening restrictions on short-term holiday lets in rural communities, with 68 members in favour and 57 against, after a heated two-hour floor debate during which Housing Minister Catriona Dalgety warned that unchecked tourist rentals were "hollowing out" village life across the Highlands. The Scottish National Party and the Scottish Greens backed the measure, while Scottish Conservative MSPs voted unanimously against it, arguing the legislation would cripple small landlords already battered by rising energy costs.

Commuters on the Overground faced significant delays on Thursday morning after a signalling fault between Highbury & Islington and Dalston Junction brought services to a near-standstill for roughly three hours, with Transport for London advising passengers to use the Victoria line or the 30 and 38 bus routes as alternatives. An estimated 47,000 journeys were disrupted before engineers restored normal operations shortly before noon.

Commuters on the Overground and Elizabeth line faced severe disruptions on Thursday morning after a signalling failure at Liverpool Street brought services to a standstill for nearly four hours, with Transport for London estimating that roughly 47,000 passengers were affected during the peak rush. Engineers from TfL's infrastructure division restored full operations by 10:45 a.m., though delays persisted well into the afternoon. The operator urged travellers to check its app before journeying and apologised for the inconvenience.

Der Stadtrat von Graz hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einem neuen Radwegekonzept zugestimmt, das die Anbindung von Außenbezirken an das städtische Kernnetz bis 2028 verbessern soll. Bei der Abstimmung votierten 28 Ratsmitglieder dafür, 21 dagegen, während sich vier Mitglieder der Stimme enthielten. Bürgermeisterin Sonja Erlacher (Grüne) sprach von einem „historischen Schritt für den klimafreundlichen Stadtverkehr", während die FPÖ-Fraktion das Projekt als finanziell unverantwortlich ablehnte. Die ÖVP enthielt sich geschlossen der Stimme.

Passengers on the U6 and U4 lines in Vienna faced lengthy delays on Thursday morning after a signalling fault near Längenfeldgasse station brought the two busiest intersecting routes to a near-standstill for almost three hours, with Wiener Linien estimating that around 47,000 commuters were affected before normal service was restored shortly before noon.

Commuters across Greater Manchester faced mounting delays on Monday after Avanti West Coast and Northern Rail both suspended services through Piccadilly station, following an emergency inspection of overhead line equipment near Stockport that engineers said could take up to 72 hours to repair. Transport for Greater Manchester estimated that roughly 140,000 passengers would be affected during the closure, and urged travellers to seek alternative routes via Metrolink or National Express coaches where possible.

Wegen umfangreicher Gleisarbeiten auf der S-Bahn-Linie S3 zwischen Hauptbahnhof und Flughafen Frankfurt wird der Zugverkehr vom 14. bis zum 21. Juni vollständig eingestellt; die Rhein-Main-Verkehrsgesellschaft richtet Ersatzbusse ein und rechnet mit rund 47.000 betroffenen Fahrgästen täglich. Die Streckensperrung fällt ausgerechnet mit der Eröffnung der Frankfurter Buchmesse zusammen, die am 18. Juni im Frankfurter Messegelände beginnt und zu der Verlage und Literaturinteressierte aus ganz Europa erwartet werden – Messedirektorin Karoline Brandt appellierte an die Besucherinnen und Besucher, frühzeitig alternative Routen zu planen.

Im packenden Kellerduell der 2. Bundesliga besiegte der SV Darmstadt 98 den 1. FC Kaiserslautern am Freitagabend im Merck-Stadion am Böllenfalltor mit 2:1. Vor 14.372 Zuschauern erzielte Lennart Grabowski das entscheidende Tor in der 88. Spielminute und sicherte den Lilien damit drei enorm wichtige Punkte im Abstiegskampf. Für Kaiserslautern, das trotz einer kämpferischen Leistung leer ausging, war es bereits die vierte Niederlage in Folge.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to reject a proposed amendment to the Rent Control Bill, with 63 members voting against and 58 in favour, after a heated chamber debate in which SNP backbenchers broke with their own government. Scottish Labour and the Conservatives united in pushing the measure through to a second reading, but the minority Scottish Government fell short of the numbers it needed to block revision of the bill's core rent-cap thresholds.

Dynamo Kyiv's slim continental ambitions were extinguished on Wednesday evening when Bayer Leverkusen dismantled them 4–1 at the BayArena, with Florián Cseke scoring twice and adding an assist to cap a dominant European night for the Bundesliga side. A crowd of 29,412 watched the hosts command possession from the opening whistle, rendering Kyiv's spirited first-half equaliser — a curling left-footed strike by Vasyl Horobets — little more than a footnote. The result sends Leverkusen through to the UEFA Europa League quarter-finals.

The Barbican Centre will host the UK premiere of Varvara Zelenko's immersive sound installation "Membrane" from 14 to 28 February, drawing on field recordings made across the steppes of Kazakhstan and the industrial outskirts of Łódź. Zelenko, who trained under the late composer Pauline Oliveros, describes the piece as an attempt to render geological time audible. Tickets are priced at £12 per session, and the Barbican's curatorial team has confirmed that guided listening workshops will run every Saturday afternoon throughout the run.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow majority on Thursday to extend free school meals to all primary-age children, with the Scottish National Party and Scottish Greens combining forces to push the measure through against fierce opposition from the Scottish Conservatives, who warned that the £180 million annual cost was fiscally reckless. The final tally stood at 68 votes in favour, 55 against, and 4 abstentions — a result that Education Secretary Fiona Drummond hailed as "a landmark day for child welfare in Scotland."

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to pass the Housing Affordability (Emergency Provisions) Bill, with 68 members backing the legislation and 54 opposing it amid fierce cross-party debate. Scottish Labour and the Scottish Greens joined forces with the SNP to push the measure through Holyrood, overcoming staunch resistance from the Scottish Conservatives, who argued the bill would deter private investment in new builds. First Minister Catriona Dalgety hailed the result as "a generational shift in how Scotland protects its tenants," though opposition leader Magnus Raeburn vowed to challenge key clauses in committee before the bill reaches royal assent.

Beim Drittliga-Spitzenspiel am Samstagabend setzte sich der SV Wacker Nordhausen mit einem knappen 2:1-Sieg gegen den FC Rot-Weiß Erfurt durch. Vor 4.200 Zuschauern im Nordhäuser Albert-Kuntz-Sportpark erzielte Tobias Fengler beide Tore für die Gastgeber, während Erfurts Stürmer Marek Vondráček den zwischenzeitlichen Ausgleich besorgte. Mit diesem Ergebnis festigt Nordhausen seinen zweiten Tabellenplatz in der Regionalliga Nordost.

Stockholm's public transport authority, SL, confirmed on Wednesday that planned maintenance work on the Tunnelbana's Green Line will force full closures between Fridhemsplan and Kungsträdgården for three consecutive weekends beginning 14 February, with replacement buses operating on all affected stops. An estimated 85,000 daily passengers are expected to be disrupted during each closure window, and SL urged commuters to allow extra travel time or consider the parallel ferry services across Riddarfjärden.

Stockholm's public transport operator SL confirmed on Thursday that the Gröna Linjen metro extension — connecting Arenastaden to Barkarby with six new underground stations — will open to passengers on 14 March 2026, following nearly a decade of tunnelling and construction work costing an estimated 24.5 billion kronor. The extension is expected to ease congestion on the heavily used T10 and T11 lines and serve up to 150,000 additional commuters daily once fully operational.

Commuters on the Øresund cross-border rail corridor faced severe disruptions on Thursday after Trafikverket and DSB jointly announced an emergency suspension of all services between Malmö Central and Copenhagen Airport, citing a fractured overhead cable near Hyllie station that engineers warned could take up to four days to fully repair. Roughly 38,000 daily passengers are expected to seek alternative transport, with both operators urging travellers to use the Öresundsbron ferry connection as a temporary measure.

The Swedish Riksdag narrowly approved a landmark housing reform package on Thursday, with 176 members voting in favour and 173 against, after weeks of fractious debate in which the centre-left Social Democrats accused the governing Moderate-led coalition of gutting tenant protections in favour of property developers. Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson hailed the result as "a necessary modernisation of a frozen market," while opposition leader Magdalena Andersson warned that working families in Stockholm and Gothenburg would bear the heaviest burden of the changes.

Grasshoppers Rowing Club edged past Regensburg Rudergesellschaft by a margin of just under two seconds at the International Regatta Linz-Ottensheim on Saturday, with club veteran Tobias Wernscheid steering the coxed four to a time of 6:14.3 in front of an estimated 4,200 spectators gathered along the Danube course.

Halftime fireworks at the Stade de la Mosson were quickly forgotten as Montpellier HSC overturned a two-goal deficit to beat Stade Brestois 3–2 in a breathless Ligue 1 encounter on Saturday evening, with striker Émilien Corval netting the decisive header in the 88th minute before a crowd of 27,450.

Commuters in Lyon faced severe disruptions on Monday after drivers employed by TCL — the city's main public transport operator — walked off the job in a 24-hour strike over proposed changes to shift patterns, leaving an estimated 340,000 daily passengers without bus or metro service. Lines A, B, C, and D of the Lyon Métro were suspended entirely, as were all 140 urban bus routes. TCL management and union representatives are scheduled to resume talks on Wednesday, though the CGT-Transport federation warned that further stoppages could follow if no agreement is reached.

Der Stadtrat von Freiburg im Breisgau hat am Dienstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit beschlossen, die umstrittene Neugestaltung des Augustinerplatzes vorläufig auf Eis zu legen. Bei der Abstimmung votierten 23 Ratsmitglieder für den Aufschub, 19 dagegen, während sich vier Mitglieder der Stimme enthielten. Bürgermeisterin Claudia Ferreira-Brandt, die das Projekt seit zwei Jahren vorangetrieben hatte, sprach von einer „herben Enttäuschung", kündigte jedoch an, den Dialog mit Bürgerinnen und Bürgern neu aufzunehmen. Die Grünen und die SPD, die den Aufschub gemeinsam beantragt hatten, zeigten sich hingegen zufrieden.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to advance a landmark bill restricting short-term holiday lets in city centres, with 68 members backing the measure against 57 opposed and three abstentions. The Scottish National Party and the Scottish Greens combined to push the legislation through Holyrood over fierce objections from Scottish Conservative MSPs, who argued the policy would devastate small landlords and rural tourism operators alike. Housing minister Catriona Elphinstone called the vote "a decisive step toward making Scotland's housing stock work for the people who actually live here."

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a six-day run at Messe Frankfurt, drawing publishers, literary agents, and readers from more than ninety countries for what organisers at Börsenverein des Deutschen Buchhandels are calling the most expansive edition in over a decade. Norwegian author Sigrid Helland will deliver the opening keynote, while the fair's guest-of-honour pavilion this year showcases Slovenia, offering a curated programme of translated fiction and poetry installations overseen by curator Maša Korenič. Single-day tickets are priced at €18.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, drawing publishers, literary agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for what organisers describe as the world's largest trade fair for books. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, with a programme curated by Stefania Colonna and featuring over 200 Italian authors. Tickets are priced at €18 for day visitors, and the fair runs through Sunday.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect to draw upwards of 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with Norwegian literature taking centre stage as the guest-of-honour theme. Among the headline events, debut novelist Astrid Lövgren will read from her translated collection "The Pale Shore" at Hall 3.1 on Thursday evening, while veteran publisher Gerhard Osswald chairs a panel on the future of independent bookshops in an era of platform consolidation.

The Bavarian state parliament in Munich voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a sweeping package of housing reforms championed by Minister-President Markus Söder's CSU, with 97 votes in favour, 89 against, and 4 abstentions — a margin that left opposition benches visibly unsettled. The Freie Wähler, junior partners in the ruling coalition, backed the measures only after securing a last-minute concession on rural development funding, according to floor leader Hannelore Brandtner. The SPD, which had tabled three rival amendments over the preceding fortnight, called the outcome "a missed opportunity for affordable housing across Bavaria."

Amsterdam's public transport authority GVB confirmed on Thursday that tram lines 7 and 14 will be suspended for eleven days starting 3 March, as engineers undertake emergency track replacement work near Leidseplein. An estimated 48,000 daily passengers are expected to seek alternative routes, with GVB deploying replacement bus services along both corridors for the duration of the closure.

The Renfrewshire Council voted narrowly on Thursday to reject a proposed rezoning of agricultural land on the outskirts of Paisley for commercial development, with 23 councillors voting against the measure, 19 in favour, and 4 abstaining. The decision was hailed by the Scottish Green Party as "a victory for communities over concrete," while the Scottish National Party, which had backed the proposal, accused the council of short-term thinking. Independent councillor Fiona Brechin, whose intervention was widely credited with swaying three undecided votes, said she remained open to a revised submission later in the year.

A rolling strike by drivers employed by Arriva Nordrhein-Westfalen will bring regional bus services across the Ruhr Valley to a near-standstill from Monday through Wednesday, the Ver.di union announced late Thursday, with an estimated 180,000 daily commuters expected to face severe disruption across routes 140 through 168 and several express connections into Essen, Bochum, and Dortmund. Negotiations over a 12 percent pay rise collapsed earlier this week after management rejected the union's final offer.

The Bavarian state parliament narrowly approved a sweeping package of fiscal reforms on Thursday, with 97 votes in favour and 89 against, after a fractious five-hour debate that saw opposition benches from the SPD and the Greens accuse the governing CSU of bypassing local municipalities in its spending allocations. Finance Minister Lena Bruckhart, who steered the bill through committee, called the result "a turning point for responsible governance in the Free State," while SPD floor leader Tobias Wengler vowed to challenge the legislation before the Federal Constitutional Court in Karlsruhe.

Passengers travelling on the Jubilee line faced severe delays on Wednesday morning after a signalling fault at Waterloo station brought services to a near-standstill for more than three hours, with Transport for London estimating that roughly 85,000 commuters were affected during the peak period. Engineers from TfL's infrastructure division were deployed shortly after 07:15 and restored full service by 10:40. A spokesperson urged customers to use the Northern and District lines as alternatives and apologised for the disruption, which the operator attributed to ageing relay equipment scheduled for replacement under the ongoing modernisation programme.

Grasshopper Club Zürich claimed a hard-fought 2–1 victory over FC Winterthur at the Letzigrund on Sunday evening, with midfielder Dario Pellegrini netting the decisive goal in the 83rd minute to keep the hosts' promotion push firmly on track. A crowd of 11,450 watched Winterthur equalise through a penalty just before the hour mark, only for Pellegrini's curling effort from the edge of the box to restore Zürich's lead. The result leaves Grasshopper four points clear at the top of the Swiss Challenge League table with six matches remaining.

The Swedish Riksdag narrowly approved a landmark climate-tax reform bill on Thursday, with 176 votes in favour and 173 against, after weeks of fractious debate that exposed deep rifts within the ruling coalition. Finance Minister Britta Söderholm, who shepherded the legislation through three rounds of committee revisions, called the result "a hard-won step toward honest pricing of carbon." The Moderaterna and Sverigedemokraterna both voted against the measure, while the Socialdemokraterna, Miljöpartiet, and Vänsterpartiet provided the slim majority. Prime Minister Ulf Kristersson had warned last month that a defeat would trigger early elections.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a landmark climate emergency bill that would bind local authorities to net-zero targets by 2035, with 68 members in favour, 55 against, and 4 abstentions — a result hailed by the Scottish Greens as a "historic step" but condemned by Scottish Conservative leader Morag Dunbar as "reckless overreach that will devastate rural livelihoods."

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstagabend mit 54 zu 38 Stimmen bei zwei Enthaltungen beschlossen, das marode Volkstheater für insgesamt 47 Millionen Euro zu sanieren und gleichzeitig als festes Haus für zeitgenössisches Musiktheater neu auszurichten — ein Beschluss, der von SPÖ und Grünen gemeinsam getragen wurde, während die FPÖ als stärkste Oppositionspartei geschlossen dagegen votierte. Kulturstadträtin Miriam Feldhammer zeigte sich nach der Abstimmung erleichtert und kündigte an, dass die Wiedereröffnung des renovierten Volkstheaters für den Herbst 2028 geplant sei, verbunden mit einem dreitägigen Eröffnungsfestival unter der künstlerischen Leitung des Regisseurs Tomáš Krejčí.

The Galway City Council voted narrowly on Thursday evening to approve a rezoning plan that would open roughly 340 acres of land on the city's eastern fringe to mixed residential and commercial development, with 18 councillors in favour, 11 against, and 3 abstentions — a result that Labour and Sinn Féin, who had jointly opposed the measure, immediately condemned as a "gift to developers at the expense of communities." The governing bloc, led by Fine Gael councillor Aisling Ó Treasaigh, argued that the city faces a housing emergency requiring urgent action.

Beim packenden Rheinderby in der 3. Liga setzte sich der MSV Duisburg am Samstagabend vor 18.200 Zuschauern im Schauinsland-Reisen-Arena mit 3:1 gegen Rot-Weiss Essen durch. Den entscheidenden Doppelpack erzielte Angreifer Luca Ferreira in der 67. und 82. Minute, nachdem Tobias Krempl den zwischenzeitlichen Ausgleich für die Gäste besorgt hatte.

Wegen des Bundesliga-Heimspiels des FC Augsburg gegen Borussia Dortmund am Samstag warnt die Augsburger Verkehrsgesellschaft (AVG) vor erheblichen Beeinträchtigungen im Straßenbahnnetz: Die Linien 2 und 3 werden zwischen 16 und 23 Uhr auf dem Innenstadtabschnitt gesperrt, rund 18.000 Fahrgäste sind laut AVG betroffen. Das Spiel in der WWK Arena endete 2:1 für den FC Augsburg, der damit seinen dritten Sieg in Folge feierte – Doppeltorschütze Marius Böhler wurde nach Abpfiff als Spieler des Abends ausgezeichnet.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstag mit knapper Mehrheit einem neuen Klimaschutzpaket zugestimmt, das unter anderem strengere Auflagen für Neubauten und den schrittweisen Ausstieg aus Gasheizungen bis 2035 vorsieht. Für den Antrag stimmten 54 der anwesenden Mandatare, 41 lehnten ihn ab, drei enthielten sich. SPÖ und Grüne hatten das Paket gemeinsam eingebracht, während die FPÖ als lauteste Gegnerin des Vorhabens auftrat. Stadtrat Benedikt Fröschl, der das Paket federführend ausgearbeitet hatte, sprach von einem „historischen Schritt für eine lebenswerte Stadt".

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors to the public on Wednesday, drawing publishers, agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for five days of panels, signings, and rights negotiations. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, with a sprawling pavilion curated by Chiara Palombo showcasing the breadth of contemporary Italian literature — from experimental fiction to graphic novels — alongside a packed programme of readings headlined by the novelist Davide Serafini. Organisers expect upward of 300,000 visitors over the course of the fair, which runs through Sunday.

Frankfurt's public transport authority confirmed on Thursday that a 72-hour walkout by drivers employed by RMV will begin at 04:00 on Monday, halting all U-Bahn and tram services across the city. The strike, called by the ver.di union after wage negotiations collapsed for the third time this year, is expected to leave approximately 340,000 daily commuters without rail options. RMV urged passengers to work from home where possible and warned that bus replacement services would cover only a fraction of the disrupted network.

Commuters on the U5 and U8 lines in Berlin face severe delays from Monday after the BVG announced emergency maintenance works at Alexanderplatz station, where ageing signal infrastructure beneath the central interchange requires urgent replacement. The works, expected to last three weeks, will affect an estimated 340,000 passengers daily, with shuttle buses deployed along both corridors during peak hours. BVG spokesperson Lena Grundtvig urged travellers to allow extra time or consider alternative S-Bahn connections.

Beim packenden Kellerduell der 2. Bundesliga empfing der VfL Osnabrück am Samstagabend den SC Paderborn 07 in der Bremer Brücke und sicherte sich durch Tore von Lasse Frenken und dem überragenden Doppeltorschützen Markus Quandt einen wichtigen 3:1-Heimsieg, der den Abstiegskampf gehörig durchwirbelt. Vor 15.200 Zuschauern blieb Paderborn trotz eines zwischenzeitlichen Ausgleichs durch Nils Brockhaus letztlich chancenlos.

Borussia Dortmund hat am Samstagabend in der Bundesliga einen überzeugenden 3:1-Heimsieg gegen den FC Augsburg eingefahren. Vor 81.365 Zuschauern im Signal Iduna Park erzielte Lennart Vossberg zwei Treffer in der zweiten Halbzeit und sicherte seiner Mannschaft damit drei wichtige Punkte im Titelrennen. Augsburgs Ehrentreffer durch Dragan Kovačić in der 78. Minute kam zu spät, um die Partie noch einmal spannend zu machen.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, agents, and authors from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by Silvia Marchetti and designed with a deliberate nod to contemporary illustration — occupies a record 2,400 square metres in Hall 4.1. Organisers expect upward of 300,000 visitors across the five-day fair, which runs through Sunday.

Kristóf Vásárhelyi put on a masterclass at the Duna Aréna on Saturday, storming to victory in the men's 400m individual medley at the Hungarian National Swimming Championships with a time that left the field trailing by nearly four seconds. The Budapest crowd of 6,200 rose to its feet as the 22-year-old touched the wall in 4:09.38, well ahead of runner-up Benedek Oláh. "He is simply on another level right now," head coach Márton Szekeres told reporters poolside.

In einem packenden Bezirksliga-Derby am Samstagnachmittag setzte sich der SV Grün-Weiß Löberitz mit 3:1 gegen den FC Zörbig durch und kletterte damit auf den zweiten Tabellenplatz. Vor 680 Zuschauern im Städtischen Sportpark Löberitz erzielte Tobias Wellnitz zwei Treffer, während Kilian Strauß das zwischenzeitliche 2:0 besorgte. Für Zörbig traf lediglich Marek Dundas per Elfmeter in der 74. Minute.

The Renfrewshire Council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a controversial rezoning plan that would open nearly forty hectares of greenbelt land on the outskirts of Paisley to residential development, with 27 councillors backing the measure, 21 opposing it, and 4 abstaining — a result that opposition members of the Scottish National Party immediately denounced as a capitulation to property developers at the expense of the region's dwindling open spaces.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect to draw more than 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with Norwegian literature taking the spotlight as this year's guest of honour nation. Leading the delegation is debut novelist Sigrid Walle, whose debut collection "Vinterstille" has already sold briskly across Scandinavia ahead of its German translation launch at Stand C12. The fair runs through Sunday.
