This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose national pavilion — designed by Rome-based architect Silvia Pratesi — sprawls across three interconnected halls in a tribute to contemporary Italian writing. Organizers expect upwards of 300,000 visitors over the five-day fair, with keynote readings by novelists Carla Menegatti and Dragan Vuković scheduled for the evening programme. Single-day admission is priced at €18 for adults.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstagabend mit 54 zu 38 Stimmen bei vier Enthaltungen einem umfangreichen Wohnbauprogramm zugestimmt, das bis 2030 rund 12.000 neue Gemeindewohnungen schaffen soll. Die regierende Koalition aus SPÖ und NEOS setzte sich damit gegen den Widerstand von FPÖ und ÖVP durch. Bürgermeister Michael Ludwig zeigte sich nach der Abstimmung erleichtert und sprach von einem „historischen Schritt für leistbares Wohnen in Wien".

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opened its doors on Wednesday to a record 4,312 exhibitors from 95 countries, with Nigerian novelist Adaeze Okonkwo delivering a celebrated keynote address at the Festhalle before a crowd of nearly 8,000. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — a sprawling, luminous installation curated by Rossella Fantini — has drawn long queues since the fair's morning launch. The event runs through Sunday.

Oslo's city council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a €340 million contract for the extension of the Holmenkollbanen metro line northward to Røa, with 32 councillors in favour and 27 against — a result hailed by the governing Arbeiderpartiet as a long-overdue investment in the city's northern suburbs but condemned by the opposition Høyre as fiscally reckless. Work on the new stretch, which will add four stations and is expected to carry an estimated 28,000 additional passengers daily, is set to begin in March 2025 under operator Ruter, with full service projected to open by late 2028.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to pass the Highlands Rural Infrastructure Bill, with 67 members backing the measure against 59 opponents and 3 abstentions — a result that SNP backbencher Catriona Dunbar hailed as "a turning point for communities left behind by successive Westminster governments," while Scottish Conservative leader Alistair Rhind warned that the funding formula embedded in the legislation would prove "unworkable within eighteen months."

Die Österreichischen Bundesbahnen haben angekündigt, dass auf der Weststrecke zwischen Wien Hauptbahnhof und Salzburg Hauptbahnhof ab dem 14. April 2025 für voraussichtlich drei Wochen umfangreiche Gleiserneuerungsarbeiten stattfinden werden, die zu erheblichen Verspätungen und teilweisen Streckensperrungen führen. Betroffen sind die Fernverkehrslinien RJ 61, RJ 63 sowie mehrere Railjet-Verbindungen in Richtung München. Fahrgäste werden gebeten, auf Schienenersatzverkehr oder alternative Verbindungen über Linz auszuweichen; die ÖBB schätzt, dass täglich rund 42.000 Reisende von den Maßnahmen betroffen sein werden.

Defending champions Randers FC were held to a grim 1–1 draw by Viborg FF at the Cepheus Park on Sunday, a result that leaves them four points adrift of league leaders FC Nordsjælland with just six rounds remaining in the Danish Superliga season. Midfielder Tobias Engholm-Svensson broke the deadlock in the 34th minute, only for Viborg substitute Kristján Óskarsson to equalise with a towering header deep into second-half stoppage time, silencing a crowd of 8,400 inside the stadium.

Commuters across Greater Manchester faced significant disruption on Monday after Avanti West Coast and Northern Rail both suspended services on the Liverpool–Manchester corridor, citing a fractured overhead line near Warrington Bank Quay station. Network Rail engineers worked through the night to restore power, with full services not expected to resume until Wednesday at the earliest. Transport for Greater Manchester estimated that roughly 47,000 passengers would be affected over the two-day outage, and urged travellers to use the replacement bus services laid on between Liverpool Lime Street and Manchester Piccadilly.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnete am Mittwoch ihre 76. Ausgabe mit einem Festakt in der Festhalle Frankfurt, an dem nach Angaben der Veranstalter rund 10.500 Gäste aus aller Welt teilnahmen. Als Gastland des Jahres präsentierte sich Norwegen mit einem breit angelegten Programm aus Lesungen, Podiumsgesprächen und Ausstellungen zeitgenössischer norwegischer Literatur. Messedirektorin Klara Sundtvedt sprach von einem „Signal der Offenheit in unruhigen Zeiten" und betonte die Rolle des gedruckten Buches als verbindendes Medium. Die Messe läuft bis zum Sonntag.

Riding a thunderous second-half performance, FC Midtjylland dismantled Brøndby IF 4–1 at MCH Arena on Saturday evening to move five points clear at the top of the Danish Superliga, with midfielder Søren Elgaard scoring twice and winger Piotr Nawrocki adding a spectacular late volley that drew a standing ovation from the 9,800 in attendance.

Leyton Orient came from behind to claim a dramatic 3–2 victory over Exeter City at the Brisbane Road on Saturday evening, with striker Tomasz Kwaśniewski netting the winner deep into stoppage time to send the home crowd of 6,841 into raptures. The result lifts Orient to fourth in League One with seven matches remaining.

Commuters across the Scottish central belt faced significant disruption on Monday after ScotRail announced the suspension of services on the Glasgow–Edinburgh Queen Street via Falkirk High corridor, citing emergency track repairs near Polmont necessitated by overnight subsidence. An estimated 34,000 passengers were affected during the morning peak alone, with replacement bus services running between Glasgow Queen Street and Linlithgow unable to keep pace with demand. ScotRail said it expected full services to resume by Wednesday evening at the earliest.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run at Messe Frankfurt, drawing publishers, literary agents, and readers from more than ninety countries — with Norwegian author Ingrid Halvorsrud delivering the opening address and the Spanish stand, curated by cultural editor Beatriz Montaner Solís, showcasing a landmark anthology of contemporary Iberian voices translated into eleven languages. This year's edition marks the fair's 75th anniversary.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, welcoming publishers, agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by Chiara Vellutini and designed around themes of memory and landscape — is expected to draw considerable crowds. Organisers anticipate attendance of roughly 285,000 visitors over the five-day run, with single-day tickets priced at €18.

Commuters on the S-Bahn München network faced severe delays on Monday morning after a signalling fault near Ostbahnhof brought three lines to a standstill for nearly four hours, with Deutsche Bahn estimating that roughly 87,000 passengers were affected during the disruption. Engineering crews worked through the rush hour to isolate the fault, and full services on the S2, S4, and S6 were not restored until shortly before midday. Deutsche Bahn said it would review the ageing relay infrastructure at the Ostbahnhof junction and could not rule out further short-term outages.

Grasshopper Club Zürich came from behind to beat Servette FC 3–2 in a fiercely contested Swiss Super League derby at Letzigrund on Saturday evening, with midfielder Tobias Fehr netting the decisive goal in the 88th minute before a crowd of 14,200 roaring supporters.

Commuters on the S-Bahn München network faced severe delays on Monday morning after a signalling fault near Ostbahnhof brought the central tunnel section to a near-standstill for almost four hours, affecting an estimated 340,000 passengers. Deutsche Bahn engineers worked to restore normal operations by midday, though services on lines S1 through S8 remained subject to cancellations and extended headways well into the afternoon rush. The operator urged travellers to use U-Bahn and bus alternatives wherever possible.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse has long occupied a peculiar place in the cultural imagination of continental Europe — part trade fair, part literary pilgrimage, part geopolitical barometer — and scholars at Goethe-Universität Frankfurt have spent the better part of a decade debating whether its influence on publishing trends is waning in the face of digital disruption. Meanwhile, the city's transport authority, RMV, has been quietly studying whether a dedicated shuttle service between Frankfurt Hauptbahnhof and the Messe Frankfurt grounds would ease the perennial congestion that grips the Sachsenhausen district each October.

Crestwood United edged Halton Borough 2–1 in a tense Central Counties League fixture at Brindley Park on Saturday evening, with midfielder Søren Almvik netting the decisive goal in the seventy-eighth minute to send the travelling supporters into raptures. A crowd of 1,340 witnessed Halton Borough's Yemi Odukoya equalise just before the interval, only for Almvik's curling left-foot effort to ultimately settle the contest in United's favour.

The Städel Museum in Frankfurt opens its long-anticipated retrospective on Dutch Golden Age still-life painting this Friday, drawing together more than 140 canvases from collections across Europe and North America in an exhibition that will run through 15 March next year. Curated by Dr. Hannelore Voss and her colleague Pieter Schrijvers of the Rijksmuseum, the show is expected to attract some 95,000 visitors over its four-month run — a figure the museum's director, Kaspar Moldenhauer, described as "cautiously optimistic" at yesterday's press preview.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its 76th edition on Wednesday, welcoming publishers, agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for five days of panels, rights negotiations, and headline author appearances. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, with a sprawling programme curated by the Istituto per il Commercio Estero and anchored by readings from novelists including the invented Giulia Ferrante and poet Marco Selvini. Organisers expect upwards of 300,000 visitors over the course of the fair, which runs through Sunday.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt und erwartet in diesem Jahr rund 95.000 Fachbesucher sowie mehr als 4.000 Aussteller aus aller Welt. Als Gastland des Jahres tritt Slowenien auf, dessen Verlage und Autoren — darunter die Lyrikerin Maja Vidmar und der Romancier Aleš Šteger — im Zentrum des Ehrengastpavillons stehen werden. Messedirektorin Klara Sonnenschein kündigte an, dass der Schwerpunkt in diesem Jahr auf dem Verhältnis von Literatur und künstlicher Intelligenz liege, ein Thema, das sämtliche Podiumsdiskussionen durchziehen werde. Die Messe läuft bis zum 19. Oktober.

Der Wiener Architekt Maximilian Drexler gilt seit Jahren als einer der schärfsten Kritiker des öffentlichen Nahverkehrs in der österreichischen Hauptstadt: In einem langen Essay für die Wochenzeitung „Der Falter" argumentiert er, dass die Wiener Linien zwar formal gut ausgebaut seien, es aber an einer kohärenten Kulturpolitik fehle, die Kunst und Mobilität miteinander verknüpfe – ein Befund, der in Fachkreisen lebhaft diskutiert wird, ohne dass konkrete Maßnahmen in Sicht wären.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt, wo über 4.000 Aussteller aus mehr als 100 Ländern erwartet werden. Ehrengast in diesem Jahr ist Slowenien. Die Schriftstellerin Maja Blažič-Hartl, die als Gesicht der slowenischen Literaturszene gilt, wird am Eröffnungsabend aus ihrem jüngsten Roman lesen. Laut Messedirektorin Renate Söllner sollen insgesamt rund 300.000 Besucher die fünftägige Veranstaltung besuchen.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opened its doors on Wednesday to an estimated 93,000 visitors on the first public day alone, with Norwegian author Lena Vikstrøm drawing the longest queues at the signing table after her debut novel — a multigenerational saga set in the fjords of Troms — was named the fair's literary discovery of the year. This year's guest of honour is Slovenia, whose pavilion in Hall 4.1 has been designed by Ljubljana-based architect Maja Zupančič and features the work of more than forty Slovenian writers and illustrators. The fair runs through Sunday.

Olympique de Marseille claimed a hard-fought 2–1 victory over Stade Rennais at the Vélodrome on Saturday evening, with midfielder Théo Caussade netting the decisive goal in the 84th minute to keep Marseille's Ligue 1 title challenge firmly alive. An attendance of 63,400 roared the home side home as Rennes, despite a spirited second-half showing, were unable to find an equaliser.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstagabend mit 54 zu 38 Stimmen bei vier Enthaltungen einem umstrittenen Klimaschutzpaket zugestimmt, das unter anderem eine schrittweise Anhebung der städtischen Parkgebühren sowie verbindliche Energiestandards für Neubauten vorsieht. Die Koalition aus SPÖ und NEOS hatte das Paket über Monate verhandelt, während FPÖ und ÖVP geschlossen dagegen stimmten. Bürgermeister Michael Ludwig sprach im Anschluss von einem „historischen Schritt für eine lebenswerte Stadt", wenngleich Kritiker aus der Wirtschaftskammer Wien eine Belastung für kleine Unternehmen befürchten.

Die Österreichischen Bundesbahnen haben angekündigt, dass die Weststrecke zwischen Salzburg und Wien ab dem 14. März für voraussichtlich drei Wochen vollständig gesperrt wird, um dringend notwendige Erneuerungsarbeiten an den Gleisanlagen durchzuführen. Reisende werden gebeten, auf Fernbusse oder den Flugverkehr auszuweichen, da ein vollständiger Schienenersatzverkehr aufgrund der Streckenlänge nicht eingerichtet werden kann. Die ÖBB schätzt, dass täglich rund 28.000 Fahrgäste von der Sperrung betroffen sein werden.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to extend free prescriptions to undocumented migrants, with the Scottish National Party and the Scottish Greens combining to push the measure through by 68 votes to 55, despite fierce resistance from the Scottish Conservatives, who accused the SNP government of prioritising gesture politics over fiscal discipline. Labour abstained, with their health spokeswoman Catriona Dunbar telling MSPs that the party supported the principle but could not back the uncosted proposal as it stood.

The Wiener Konzerthaus will host a three-night residency by the Norwegian chamber ensemble Arktis Quartet beginning on 14 March, with programmes drawn entirely from Nordic composers of the twentieth century — Sibelius, Grieg, and the lesser-known Fartein Valen among them. Tickets are priced at €28 per performance, and the series is presented in partnership with the Nordic Cultural Fund. The concerts are expected to draw a combined audience of roughly 2,400 listeners across the three evenings.

Beim hart umkämpften Stadtderby in der 3. Liga trennten sich der FC Ingolstadt 04 und der TSV 1860 München am Samstag im Audi Sportpark mit einem torlosen Unentschieden – trotz 11.240 Zuschauern, die bis zur letzten Minute auf eine Entscheidung gehofft hatten. Ingolstadts Kapitän Moritz Haberland vergab in der 88. Minute die größte Chance der Partie, als sein Kopfball knapp über die Latte strich. Für beide Klubs bleibt die Lage im Tabellenmittelfeld damit angespannt.

Fenerbahçe ground out a hard-fought 2–1 victory over Trabzonspor at Şükrü Saracoğlu Stadium on Saturday evening, with striker Emre Kılıçoğlu netting the decisive header in the 83rd minute to send the home faithful into raptures. The result lifts Fenerbahçe to second place in the Süper Lig standings, three points behind leaders Galatasaray, with ten matches remaining in the season. An attendance of 41,200 was recorded, the highest at the ground this calendar year.

Miroslava Horáčková delivered a masterclass in short-track speed skating at the Štvanice Winter Arena in Prague on Saturday, powering through the 1,500-metre final in a personal-best time of 2:16.83 to claim gold at the Czech National Winter Championships. The 23-year-old from Brno edged out defending champion Petra Šimůnková by just four hundredths of a second in front of a sold-out crowd of 3,400 spectators, sending the home fans into raptures.

Commuters on the S-Bahn network around Stuttgart faced severe disruptions on Thursday after a signalling fault near Vaihingen brought services on lines S1, S2, and S3 to a near-standstill for roughly four hours during the morning rush, with DB Regio estimating that around 47,000 passengers were affected before normal operations resumed shortly before noon.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, agents, and literary scouts from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for five days of deals, panel discussions, and impassioned arguments about the future of print. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, whose pavilion — designed by architect Serena Dall'Olio — centres on a sprawling exhibition titled "Radici," exploring the deep roots of Italian storytelling from Dante to Elena Ferrante. Ticket prices start at €18 for a single day, with a five-day professional pass available at €220.

Commuters on the S-Bahn network in Hamburg faced severe delays on Thursday morning after a signalling fault near Harburg brought three lines to a standstill for more than four hours, leaving an estimated 38,000 passengers stranded or forced onto overcrowded bus replacements. Deutsche Bahn confirmed that engineering crews restored full service by 11:45 a.m., but urged travellers to expect residual disruption throughout the afternoon peak.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt mit einem Festakt, bei dem die österreichische Schriftstellerin Lena Gruber ihr viel erwartetes Romandebut vorstellt. Rund 4.200 Aussteller aus über 90 Ländern haben sich für die fünftägige Veranstaltung angemeldet, die bis zum 19. Oktober dauert und unter dem diesjährigen Ehrengastland Norwegen steht.

Helsinki Regional Transport Authority announced on Monday that tram lines 3 and 9 will be suspended for three weeks beginning 14 April while crews replace a corroded overhead wire gantry network near the Central Railway Station, leaving an estimated 47,000 daily passengers reliant on replacement bus services operated by Nobina Finland.

Hibernian came from behind to defeat Dundee United 3–2 in a breathless Scottish Premiership encounter at Easter Road on Saturday, with striker Tomasz Wielecki netting twice in the final quarter-hour to seal all three points in front of a sold-out crowd of 20,421.

Bohemian FC edged out Shelbourne 2–1 in a tense Dublin derby at Dalymount Park on Friday evening, with striker Ciarán Murtagh netting the decisive goal in the 83rd minute to keep Bohemian's promotion push alive in the League of Ireland First Division. A crowd of 4,200 packed the north Dublin ground, producing an atmosphere belying the division's modest billing. Shelbourne goalkeeper Aoife Brennan had kept her side in contention with a string of first-half saves, but could do little about Murtagh's clinical near-post finish.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its 76th edition on Wednesday, welcoming more than 4,200 exhibitors from 95 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds — a figure that organisers say marks the highest international participation in over a decade. Guest of honour this year is the Republic of Slovenia, whose pavilion, curated by literary scholar Maja Kovačič, will showcase translations of Slovenian poetry and prose spanning five centuries. Tickets for the public days, running from Saturday through Sunday, are priced at €18.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its 76th edition on Wednesday, with publishers, agents, and literary scouts from more than 100 countries descending on the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for what remains the world's largest trade gathering dedicated to books. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by the Istituto per il Commercio Estero — promises a sweeping retrospective of Italian literature spanning five centuries. Tickets for public days are priced at €18, and organisers expect upwards of 300,000 visitors by the time the fair closes on Sunday.

Commuters on the Piccadilly line faced severe delays for the third consecutive morning on Wednesday after a signalling fault near Hammersmith brought services to a near-standstill during the peak rush hour, with Transport for London estimating that roughly 85,000 passengers were affected. Engineers from TfL's infrastructure division worked through the night to isolate the fault, but as of midday the line was still operating at reduced frequency between Heathrow Airport and King's Cross St. Pancras. A spokesperson confirmed that full service was not expected to resume before Thursday.

Josefine Brandt held off a determined challenge from compatriot Maren Solberg in the final kilometre to claim the women's title at the Bergen City Marathon on Sunday, crossing the line in 2 hours 28 minutes before a crowd of 14,200 spectators gathered along the rain-soaked waterfront course. It was Brandt's second consecutive victory at the event, and race director Håkon Vesterås confirmed she would be invited to defend her title in 2026.

Leinster Rugby secured a commanding 34–12 victory over Ulster at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Saturday evening, with centre Ciarán Molloy crossing the line twice and fly-half Declan Forde contributing 14 points from the tee in what was a thoroughly one-sided United Rugby Championship clash before an attendance of 48,600.

Hosts Rosenborg BK came from a goal down to defeat Molde FK 3–1 at Lerkendal Stadion on Saturday evening, with striker Tobias Nygård bagging a second-half brace to seal a commanding victory in front of 18,432 partisan supporters and lift the Trondheim club to second place in the Eliteserien table.

Trailing by two sets and seemingly on the brink of elimination, Tomáš Brejcha staged a breathtaking fightback at the Rothenbaum Stadium in Hamburg on Saturday to defeat third-seeded Matteo Calvanese of Italy 3–6, 4–6, 6–3, 6–4, 7–5, booking his place in the Hamburg Open quarterfinals and leaving the Centre Court crowd of 8,200 on its feet.

Copenhagen's city council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a €340 million expansion of the Metro Cityringen, extending the line by four new stations into the northern suburbs of Bispebjerg and Brønshøj — a decision that came after months of fractious debate between the ruling Social Democrats and the centre-right Venstre bloc. The final tally was 31 votes in favour and 24 against, with 2 abstentions. Københavns Metro, the line's operator, confirmed that construction is expected to begin in early 2026 and that the extension will add roughly 87,000 daily passengers to the network once it opens.

Ronan Castleigh's brace in the final twelve minutes rescued Galway United from what had looked like a certain defeat at Eamonn Deacy Park on Saturday evening, as they fought back from two goals down to draw 2–2 with Bohemian FC in a breathless League of Ireland Premier Division encounter watched by 4,150 supporters.

Henrietta Voss delivered a commanding performance at the Women's European Rowing Championships on Saturday, steering her single scull to victory on the Rotsee in Lucerne with a final time that left her nearest rival — Denmark's Sofie Brandt — trailing by nearly three seconds. The gold secured Voss's third consecutive continental title, and the crowd of 11,400 roared as she crossed the finish line in a championship-record 7 minutes 18 seconds.

Leinster Rugby claimed a commanding 34–17 victory over Ulster at the Aviva Stadium in Dublin on Saturday evening, with flanker Ciarán Mossé crossing for two tries and fly-half Petra Wulff contributing 14 points off the boot in what proved a decisive interprovincial derby. A crowd of 48,200 turned out under floodlights for the United Rugby Championship clash, leaving Ulster's title hopes in serious jeopardy with only three rounds remaining.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, literary agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by the Rome-based cultural body Istituto per il Commercio Estero — occupies an expanded wing of Hall 4.1. Among the headlining authors are the Milanese novelist Carla Ferretti and the Neapolitan essayist Domenico Ruggeri, both of whom will take part in ticketed readings priced at €18. The fair runs through Sunday, 20 October.

Leverkusen fell to a stunning 3–1 defeat at the Allianz Arena on Saturday evening as Bayern München's Tomáš Hrubý scored twice in the second half to end the visitors' eight-game unbeaten run in the Bundesliga, with an attendance of 75,024 roaring the hosts home.

Edinburgh's Usher Hall will host the three-day Nordic Sounds Festival beginning Friday, 14 March, bringing together ensembles from across Scandinavia in a programme spanning folk, contemporary classical, and experimental electronica — but concertgoers arriving by rail should plan ahead after ScotRail announced a partial suspension of services on the Waverley Route between Edinburgh and Galashiels starting the same weekend, with an estimated 22,000 passengers affected during the closure, which is scheduled to last until Sunday evening while engineers replace ageing signal gantries near Newtongrange.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect to draw more than 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with this year's guest of honour being Norway — a choice that has already generated considerable excitement among publishers and literary agents across Europe. Headline events include a reading by the novelist Ingrid Solberg-Haug, whose debut collection has been shortlisted for the Nordic Council's Literature Prize, and a panel discussion on translation rights moderated by the Frankfurt-based literary scholar Dr. Ralf Ostermeyer.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, October 15th, welcoming publishers, agents, and literary luminaries from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for what organisers are billing as the most globally connected edition in the fair's history. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, with a sprawling programme of readings, panel discussions, and installations curated by the Istituto per il Commercio Estero designed to showcase the breadth of contemporary Italian letters. Ticket prices for day passes have been set at €18, while a full five-day professional accreditation will cost €310.

Tens of thousands of supporters are expected to descend on Düsseldorf this Saturday for the Bundesliga derby between Fortuna Düsseldorf and 1. FC Köln at Merkur Spiel-Arena, with city transport authority Rheinbahn already warning of severe overcrowding on tram and U-Bahn lines serving the stadium district. Rheinbahn announced on Thursday that lines U78 and U79 will operate at doubled frequency from 14:00 until midnight, while road closures along Straße des 17. Juni will take effect from 12:00 and are expected to affect an estimated 38,000 road users. "Anyone driving to the match simply will not reach it in time," said Rheinbahn spokeswoman Ines Barkow, urging fans to use public transit.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt mit einem Festakt, bei dem die österreichische Autorin Maren Soltau die Eröffnungsrede halten wird. Erwartet werden in diesem Jahr rund 95.000 Fachbesucher aus über 100 Ländern; der Ehrengast ist Norwegen. Neben dem Publikumsprogramm im großen Lesezelt kuratiert die Literaturwissenschaftlerin Prof. Ingrid Hassel eine neue Reihe zu zeitgenössischer skandinavischer Prosa, die täglich um 11 Uhr im Forum der Halle 3.1 stattfindet.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its 76th edition on Wednesday, October 16, drawing publishers, agents, and literary scouts from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, with a sprawling programme of readings, panel discussions, and installations curated by Chiara Veronesi and her team at the Istituto Italiano di Cultura. Ticket prices start at €18 for a single-day admission, and organisers expect upwards of 300,000 visitors across the five-day fair.

Die Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe (BVG) haben ab Montag die Tarife für alle S-Bahn- und U-Bahn-Linien um durchschnittlich 4,3 Prozent angehoben — die stärkste Preissteigerung seit über einem Jahrzehnt. Betroffen sind nach Schätzungen rund 1,4 Millionen Fahrgäste täglich. BVG-Sprecherin Nadine Hellkamp begründete den Schritt mit gestiegenen Energie- und Personalkosten sowie notwendigen Investitionen in die Modernisierung der Flotte. Einzeltickets im Tarifbereich AB kosten nun 3,50 Euro, während das Monatsabo auf 98 Euro steigt.

The Scottish Parliament voted on Thursday to approve a landmark arts funding bill championed by Culture Secretary Fiona Drummond, securing a majority of 74 votes to 41 with six abstentions — a result hailed by SNP backbenchers as a turning point for publicly supported creativity. The legislation unlocks £18 million annually for regional arts bodies across Scotland, and the first beneficiary is already in place: the Glasgow International Festival of Visual Art, which opens its twelfth edition at the Tramway arts centre on 9 May, featuring commissions from over thirty artists drawn from six continents.

The Scottish Parliament narrowly approved a landmark housing reform bill on Thursday, with 67 votes in favour, 59 against, and 3 abstentions, after a fractious overnight debate that tested the patience of both government and opposition benches. First Minister Catriona Elliot, whose Scottish National Party had staked considerable political capital on the measure, called the result "a hard-won step toward affordable homes for every community." The Scottish Conservatives, led in the chamber by shadow housing spokesman Alasdair Drummond, argued that the bill's rent-control provisions would deter private investment and ultimately harm the very tenants it claimed to protect. The Scottish Greens, who supplied the decisive bloc of cross-bench support, had extracted a last-minute amendment tightening energy-efficiency requirements for all new-build properties before agreeing to vote with the government.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, agents, and literary enthusiasts from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — designed by architect Lavinia Ferretti — promises a sweeping survey of contemporary Italian fiction and poetry. Organisers from the Börsenverein des Deutschen Buchhandels expect upwards of 300,000 visitors across the five-day fair, which runs through Sunday.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstag mit 54 zu 37 Stimmen bei vier Enthaltungen einem neuen Klimaschutzpaket zugestimmt, das unter anderem eine schrittweise Dekarbonisierung des städtischen Fuhrparks bis 2032 vorsieht. SPÖ und Grüne stimmten geschlossen dafür, während die FPÖ das Vorhaben als „wirtschaftsfeindlich" ablehnte. Bürgermeister Michael Ludwig hatte das Paket zuvor als „historischen Schritt für eine lebenswerte Stadt" bezeichnet.

Beim bislang packendsten Duell der laufenden Saison bezwang der SC Freiburg den 1. FC Union Berlin am Samstagabend mit 3:1 im Schwarzwald-Stadion und festigte damit seinen dritten Tabellenplatz in der Bundesliga. Vor 24.000 Zuschauern erzielte Mittelfeldspieler Jonas Wehrle zwei Treffer in der zweiten Halbzeit, nachdem Stürmer Karim Ouédraogo mit einem Kopfball in der 18. Minute die Führung besorgt hatte. Union-Kapitän Tilo Brandt verkürzte zwischenzeitlich auf 1:2, doch die Hausherren ließen sich den Sieg nicht mehr nehmen.

Wegen des Bundesliga-Heimspiels des FC Schalke 04 gegen Borussia Dortmund am Samstag, den 18. Januar, wird die Stadtbahn-Linie U11 in Gelsenkirchen zwischen 14 und 22 Uhr außerplanmäßig verstärkt betrieben, wie die Stadtwerke Gelsenkirchen mitteilten. Auf dem Rasen der Veltins-Arena sicherte sich Schalke schließlich einen knappen 2:1-Sieg vor 61.973 Zuschauern, wobei Mittelfeldspieler Tomáš Blažek mit einem Doppelpack der entscheidende Mann war.

Der Stadtrat von Linz hat am Donnerstag mit knapper Mehrheit einen umstrittenen Beschluss zur Erhöhung der Grundsteuer um zwölf Prozent verabschiedet: 23 Stimmen votierten dafür, 19 dagegen, bei zwei Enthaltungen. Die regierende Koalition aus SPÖ und Grünen setzte sich damit gegen die ÖVP durch, die das Vorhaben als „sozial unausgewogen" bezeichnet hatte. Bürgermeisterin Karin Wallner erklärte nach der Abstimmung, die Mehreinnahmen seien unerlässlich, um den Ausbau städtischer Kinderbetreuungseinrichtungen zu finanzieren.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect to draw more than 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with Slovenia this year serving as Guest of Honour. Leading the German-language fiction programme is debut novelist Carla Nussbaum, whose first book, "Die stille Kammer," will receive its world premiere reading on the opening evening. Tickets for premium author events are priced at €18.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect to draw more than 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with Norwegian literature taking centre stage as the guest-of-honour theme. Among the headline events, debut novelist Astrid Lunde will read from her prize-shortlisted collection alongside a panel discussion moderated by cultural critic Tobias Ferencz. Tickets for individual evening readings are priced at €18.

The city of Seville buzzed with a rare double bill this past weekend: the Teatro de la Maestranza hosted the European premiere of Argentinian composer Lucía Ferrarini's choral symphony "Río Quieto" on Friday evening, drawing a near-capacity crowd of 1,740 to hear the Orquesta Sinfónica de Sevilla under conductor Marcos Albéniz, while across town the Estadio Ramón Sánchez-Pizjuán roared on Sunday afternoon as Sevilla FC edged Valencia CF 2–1 in a fiercely contested La Liga fixture, with midfielder Tomás Rueda scoring the decisive goal in the 88th minute before an attendance of 42,500.

Commuters across the greater Oslo region faced severe disruptions on Monday after Ruter called a 72-hour strike affecting all underground, tram, and bus services, leaving an estimated 340,000 daily passengers without public transport as wage negotiations with the Norwegian Transport Workers' Union collapsed for the second time in six weeks.

Commuters on the Cologne–Aachen corridor faced severe disruption on Monday after Deutsche Bahn engineers discovered stress fractures in an overhead line gantry near Düren, forcing the suspension of all RE1 and IC 132 services for at least 72 hours while emergency repair crews work around the clock. An estimated 34,000 passengers per day are expected to seek alternative travel via replacement bus services laid on between Cologne Hauptbahnhof and Aachen Hauptbahnhof, though operators warned that journey times would roughly triple. Deutsche Bahn said it hoped to restore partial services by Thursday morning, depending on the outcome of structural assessments still under way.

Beim packenden Stadtduell in der 2. Bundesliga setzte sich der Hamburger SV am Samstagabend mit 3:1 gegen den FC St. Pauli durch und festigte damit seinen zweiten Tabellenplatz. Vor ausverkauftem Volksparkstadion trafen Leandro Vásquez doppelt sowie der überragende Mikkel Brandt, während St. Paulis Anschlusstreffer durch Jonas Felber in der 74. Minute ohne weitere Wirkung blieb. Die 57.000 Zuschauer erlebten ein intensives Derby, das der HSV über weite Strecken kontrollierte.

Long before the Volksbühne became a flashpoint in Berlin's interminable debates about who the city's cultural institutions actually serve, its red facade on Rosa-Luxemburg-Platz was simply a landmark — the kind of building that appears in architecture textbooks alongside the Schaubühne and the Deutsche Oper without any particular controversy attached. Critics have spent the better part of three decades arguing about whether subsidised theatre in Germany's capital can ever truly escape its relationship with the SPD-led Senate, a question that the political scientist Dr. Hannelore Trautmann explored in her 2019 monograph, which remains quietly influential in policy circles even now.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to reject a proposed motion of no confidence in First Minister Catriona Drummond, with 65 members voting against the motion and 59 in favour, after a bruising three-hour debate in which SNP backbenchers accused opposition leaders of opportunism while Labour and the Scottish Conservatives argued that Drummond's handling of the devolved healthcare budget had become "constitutionally untenable." The Scottish Greens, whose support had been pivotal in passing last year's climate legislation, abstained en bloc, a move their co-convener Euan Gillies described as "a warning shot, not an absolution."

Olympique de Marseille came from behind to defeat Stade Rennais 3–2 in a breathless Ligue 1 encounter at the Stade Vélodrome on Saturday evening, with striker Théodore Malherbe netting a stoppage-time winner to send a crowd of 62,500 into delirium. Rennes had led twice through goals either side of half-time, but Malherbe's brace — combined with a precise low finish from midfielder Axel Kouakou — ultimately proved the difference. The result lifts Marseille to fourth in the table with eight matches remaining.

Die Kunstmesse „Vienna Contemporary" eröffnet am 18. September in der Marx Halle und versammelt in diesem Jahr erstmals über 120 Galerien aus mehr als 30 Ländern unter einem Dach. Kuratorin Veronika Sedlmayr hat den Themenschwerpunkt auf osteuropäische Gegenwartskunst gelegt und dabei besonders auf junge Positionen aus der Ukraine und Georgien gesetzt. Der Eintritt kostet 22 Euro, und die Messe läuft bis zum 22. September.

Vor 34.200 Zuschauern im Weserstadion bezwang Werder Bremen am Samstagabend den SC Freiburg mit 3:1 und festigte damit seinen dritten Tabellenplatz in der Bundesliga. Die Tore für die Gastgeber erzielten Lukas Hartenfels, Marek Sobotka und Nils Breuker, während Freiburgs Anschlusstreffer von Tomáš Vlček in der 74. Minute ohne Folgen blieb.

The Reykjavík City Council approved a sweeping new housing affordability plan late Thursday evening by a margin of thirteen votes to four, with two abstentions, after nearly five hours of often fractious debate. The measure, championed by councillor Sigríður Óskarsdóttir of the Left-Green Movement, would cap rent increases at two percent annually for properties receiving municipal subsidies and allocate 1.4 billion króna toward the construction of social housing in the Grafarholt district. Centre-right bloc leader Magnús Helgi Þórðarson argued the plan overreached local government's mandate, but his objections failed to sway the chamber's progressive majority.

The Finnish parliament narrowly passed a controversial austerity package on Thursday, with 102 votes in favour and 97 against, after weeks of fractious debate that tested the resolve of Prime Minister Petteri Orpo's coalition. The measures, which include sweeping cuts to housing benefits and a freeze on public-sector wages, were championed by the National Coalition Party and its junior partner the Finns Party, but drew fierce resistance from the Social Democrats, whose leader Annika Saarela described the vote as "a betrayal of working families." The package now moves to the Constitutional Law Committee for a final review before taking effect in early 2026.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a razor-thin margin on Thursday to reject the proposed Coastal Infrastructure Levy, a measure that would have imposed new charges on offshore energy developers operating in Scottish waters. The bill fell by 64 votes to 61, with 3 abstentions, after a bruising floor debate in which SNP backbenchers broke ranks with their own government. Scottish Labour and the Scottish Conservatives had jointly whipped their members against the legislation, while the Scottish Greens offered only tepid and ultimately insufficient support. First Minister Catriona Muirhead, who had staked considerable political capital on the bill's passage, acknowledged the defeat in a brief statement from Holyrood, pledging to bring a revised version before the chamber "within the current parliamentary term."

Der Stadtrat von Erfurt hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit den umstrittenen Haushaltsentwurf für das kommende Jahr verabschiedet: 28 Ratsmitglieder stimmten dafür, 24 dagegen, bei drei Enthaltungen. Die Abstimmung zog sich über mehrere Stunden hin, nachdem die Fraktionen von SPD und Grünen in letzter Minute noch Änderungsanträge zum Sozialwohnungsbau eingebracht hatten. Oberbürgermeisterin Karoline Veth zeigte sich nach der Sitzung erleichtert und bezeichnete das Ergebnis als „Signal der Handlungsfähigkeit".

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its 76th edition on Wednesday at the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with guest of honour status awarded to Italy this year; among the headline speakers is novelist Chiara Andreotti, whose debut in German translation has already drawn pre-fair orders exceeding 12,000 copies across the DACH region. Publishers from more than 100 countries are expected to crowd the halls through Sunday, when the prize ceremony for the Deutscher Buchpreis will close the week.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, drawing publishers, literary agents, and readers from more than ninety countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for what organisers are billing as the largest edition in seven years. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by Rome-based arts director Eleonora Gatti — features over two hundred titles in translation alongside live readings by novelists Vittoria Sereni and Marco Aulisio. Tickets for public days start at eighteen euros.

The Swedish Riksdag narrowly approved a sweeping welfare reform package on Thursday, with 176 members voting in favour and 173 against, after weeks of fractious debate that had threatened to topple the minority government of Prime Minister Tobias Wennström. The Moderaterna led coalition had staked its credibility on the bill, which would cap housing benefits for low-income households and redirect savings toward vocational training programmes. Sverigedemokraterna provided the crucial cross-aisle votes needed to push the legislation over the line, a deal that opposition leader Malin Söderberg of Socialdemokraterna condemned as a "cynical bargain at the expense of Sweden's most vulnerable families."

The Flemish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a sweeping overhaul of the region's housing subsidy programme, with the centre-right coalition securing a majority of just four seats after two members of the liberal VLD faction broke ranks to abstain. Finance spokeswoman Lieselotte Vandenberghe, who had championed the reforms for nearly eighteen months, called the outcome "a hard-won but necessary step" for working families priced out of the Ghent and Antwerp markets. The opposition Groen party, which tabled fourteen amendments — all defeated — warned that the cuts to low-income rental support would deepen inequality across Flanders.

Defending champions Malmö FF edged past IFK Göteborg 2–1 in a tightly contested Allsvenskan fixture at Eleda Stadion on Saturday evening, with midfielder Tobias Krantz netting the decisive goal in the 88th minute before a crowd of 18,340. The victory keeps Malmö four points clear at the summit ahead of a demanding run of away fixtures.

Commuters across Helsinki faced significant delays on Monday morning after a signalling fault brought services on the Ring Rail Line to a standstill for nearly four hours, with Finavia and VR Group estimating that roughly 34,000 passengers were affected before normal operations resumed shortly before midday. The disruption, which forced dozens of trains to terminate at Tikkurila station, came just weeks before a scheduled infrastructure audit that was expected to validate the line's newly upgraded relay systems.

Die Berliner S-Bahn hat ab kommendem Montag eine vollständige Sperrung der S7 zwischen Ostbahnhof und Erkner angekündigt, die voraussichtlich bis zum 14. März andauern wird. Als Grund nannte der Betreiber DB Regio dringend notwendige Erneuerungsarbeiten an der Leit- und Sicherungstechnik. Rund 38.000 Fahrgäste täglich sind laut Schätzungen von der Unterbrechung betroffen; Schienenersatzverkehr mit Bussen wird auf der gesamten Strecke eingerichtet.

Commuters across Greater Manchester faced severe disruption on Thursday after Avanti West Coast announced the suspension of all inter-city rail services between Manchester Piccadilly and London Euston, citing a signalling failure near Crewe that engineers estimated would take at least 36 hours to repair. Metrolink tram services were stretched beyond capacity as an estimated 47,000 stranded passengers sought alternative routes into the city centre, with Transport for Greater Manchester urging travellers to delay non-essential journeys until Saturday morning.

Der Stadtrat von Freiburg im Breisgau hat am Dienstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einem neuen Radverkehrskonzept zugestimmt, das bis 2030 den Anteil des Fahrrads am Gesamtverkehr auf dreißig Prozent steigern soll. Die Abstimmung endete mit 27 Ja-Stimmen gegen 19 Nein-Stimmen bei vier Enthaltungen. Bürgermeisterin Carola Wendt von den Grünen sprach von einem „historischen Signal für eine lebenswerte Innenstadt", während der Fraktionsvorsitzende der CDU, Markus Dollinger, die Kosten von rund 45 Millionen Euro als unverantwortlich bezeichnete.

London's Elizabeth line will face severe disruptions this weekend after Crossrail Ltd announced emergency engineering works between Paddington and Liverpool Street, forcing passengers to use bus replacement services from Saturday morning through to Sunday night. TfL estimates that approximately 340,000 journeys could be affected over the two-day closure, which has been triggered by the discovery of a fractured overhead line support bracket identified during routine inspection on Thursday.

The Flemish parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a sweeping overhaul of the region's housing subsidy programme, with 72 members in favour and 61 against after nearly five hours of acrimonious debate. The bill, championed by Vlaams Belang and reluctantly backed by the N-VA, would cap rent assistance for new applicants at €350 per month — a threshold critics from Vooruit and Groen called "a recipe for homelessness." Speaker Maaike Devriese declared the result valid despite procedural objections lodged by opposition benches moments before the final count.

Stockholm's public transport operator SL confirmed on Wednesday that a signalling fault on the Tunnelbana's Green Line had been fully resolved after causing severe delays lasting nearly four hours during the morning rush, with commuters on routes T17, T18, and T19 facing standstills at Fridhemsplan and Slussen. At the height of the disruption, SL estimated that roughly 85,000 passengers were affected across the inner-city network.

The Edinburgh International Festival announced on Monday that its centrepiece opening concert — a programme of Mahler and Sibelius performed by the Gothenburg Symphony Orchestra under conductor Marit Søyland — will take place at Usher Hall on 2 August, drawing an expected crowd of 2,200. The announcement coincided with a warning from Lothian Buses that services on routes 10, 11, and 24 will be suspended from 1 August through 4 August due to roadworks on Lothian Road, potentially disrupting some 18,000 daily passengers hoping to reach the venue.

Malmö FF secured a hard-fought 2–1 victory over IFK Göteborg at Eleda Stadion on Saturday evening, with midfielder Tobias Strand netting the decisive goal in the 84th minute to lift his side to the top of the Allsvenskan table. A crowd of 19,340 witnessed the tense derby, which saw IFK Göteborg reduced to ten men after a straight red card midway through the second half.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt mit über 4.000 Ausstellern aus mehr als 100 Ländern. Als Ehrengastland tritt Slowenien auf, das mit einer umfangreichen Delegation von Autoren, Verlegern und Illustratoren vertreten sein wird. Messedirektorin Klara Wendt bezeichnete das Programm als „das ambitionierteste seit einem Jahrzehnt" und verwies besonders auf die neu eingerichtete Halle für digitales Publizieren. Der Eintritt für Fachbesucher am ersten Tag beträgt 38 Euro.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt und erwartet nach Angaben des Börsenvereins des Deutschen Buchhandels in diesem Jahr rund 95.000 Besucher aus über 100 Ländern. Als Ehrengast tritt erstmals Slowenien auf, und die slowenische Autorin Maruša Krese wird bei der feierlichen Eröffnungsveranstaltung in der Festhalle eine Rede halten. Für die inhaltliche Programmgestaltung zeichnet Kuratorin Vesna Lemaić verantwortlich, die ein breit gefächertes Spektrum aus Lesungen, Podiumsdiskussionen und Ausstellungen zusammengestellt hat.

Der Stadtrat von Freiburg im Breisgau hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einem neuen Radverkehrskonzept zugestimmt, das unter anderem die Einrichtung von zwölf zusätzlichen Fahrradspuren im Innenstadtbereich vorsieht. Von den 48 anwesenden Ratsmitgliedern stimmten 26 dafür, 18 dagegen, vier enthielten sich. Bürgermeisterin Klara Svendt, die das Konzept maßgeblich vorangetrieben hatte, sprach von einem „historischen Schritt für die klimagerechte Stadtentwicklung". Die oppositionelle CDU-Fraktion kritisierte hingegen, dass die geplanten Maßnahmen den Individualverkehr unverhältnismäßig stark einschränken würden. Das Konzept soll ab dem Frühjahr 2026 schrittweise umgesetzt werden.

Bundesliga leaders Bayer Leverkusen came from behind to beat visiting RB Leipzig 3–2 at the BayArena on Saturday, with midfielder Florian Kessler netting twice in the final quarter-hour to seal a dramatic comeback before a sell-out crowd of 30,210. The win extends Leverkusen's unbeaten run in the league to seventeen matches.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect will draw upwards of 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, where publishers from more than 100 countries will exhibit titles spanning literary fiction, academic scholarship, and graphic novels. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by Chiara Morvillo and overseen by the Istituto per il Commercio Estero — promises an ambitious programme of readings, panel discussions, and live translation workshops. Tickets for the public weekend start at €18.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to pass the Housing Affordability (Emergency Measures) Bill, with 65 members backing the legislation and 58 voting against, amid fierce opposition from the Scottish Conservatives, who condemned the rent-cap provisions as economically illiterate. First Minister Catriona Dalgety, speaking from Holyrood after the result was announced, called it "a watershed moment for tenants across Scotland," while shadow housing spokesman Alasdair Munn insisted the measure would deter private investment. The Scottish Greens, whose four votes proved decisive, had extracted a last-minute guarantee that a review clause would be inserted before the bill clears the upper-chamber stage.

The Reykjavík Art Museum opens its long-anticipated retrospective of Icelandic sculptor Dagný Sigurðardóttir on Friday, gathering over two hundred bronze and basalt works spanning four decades of her career under the vast skylights of the Hafnarhús building. Curated by Jón Már Eiríksson of the Nordic Arts Council, the exhibition will run through March 9th and is expected to draw visitors from across Scandinavia and beyond. Admission is set at 1,800 króna for adults.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstag mit knapper Mehrheit einem umstrittenen Wohnbaupaket zugestimmt: 54 Stimmen entfielen auf das Ja-Lager, 45 auf die Nein-Seite, während sich vier Mandatare der Stimme enthielten. Das Paket sieht vor, bis 2030 rund 12.000 neue Sozialwohnungen zu errichten, und war vor allem von der SPÖ und den Grünen vorangetrieben worden, während die FPÖ und die ÖVP geschlossen dagegenstimmten. Bürgermeisterin Klaudia Tauber, die das Projekt als „historischen Schritt für leistbares Wohnen" bezeichnete, zeigte sich nach der Abstimmung erleichtert.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnete am Mittwoch ihre 76. Ausgabe mit einem Festakt im Römer, bei dem die Verlegerin Saoirse Brandt aus Dublin die Eröffnungsrede hielt. Rund 4.200 Aussteller aus 95 Ländern präsentieren bis zum 20. Oktober ihre Neuerscheinungen auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt. Schriftstellerin Yuki Tanimoto, deren Debütroman auf der Shortlist des Deutschen Buchpreises steht, zählt zu den meistdiskutierten Namen der diesjährigen Messe.

Commuters on the Jubilee line faced lengthy delays on Thursday morning after a signalling fault near Canary Wharf brought services to a near-standstill for more than three hours, with Transport for London estimating that roughly 85,000 passengers were affected during the peak rush. TfL engineers restored full service by 10:47 a.m., though the operator urged travellers to expect residual crowding at Stratford and Westminster stations well into the afternoon.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt und erwartet in diesem Jahr mehr als 4.000 Aussteller aus über 100 Ländern. Als Ehrengastland fungiert Kanada, dessen Verlagswesen sich in einer eigens gestalteten Halle präsentieren wird. Schriftstellerin Léa Fontaine-Roux wird die Eröffnungslesung halten, während der renommierte Verleger Tobias Schnettler die Begrüßungsrede übernimmt.

Long before the first shovel broke ground on what would become the Allianz Arena, Munich's relationship with its football clubs was already a subject of heated academic debate — a tension between civic identity and commercial spectacle that urban historians at Ludwig Maximilian University have spent the better part of three decades trying to untangle. The stadium itself, critics argue, is less a sports venue than a monument to the city's conflicted ambitions, its luminous facade shifting colours in a manner that strikes some observers as playful and others as a gaudy advertisement for modernity.

Commuters on the S-Bahn network around Frankfurt faced severe delays from Monday morning after a points failure near Sachsenhausen brought services on lines S3, S4, and S6 to a near standstill, with Deutsche Bahn estimating that roughly 47,000 passengers were affected during the peak hours alone. Repair crews worked through the night, and Deutsche Bahn confirmed that full services would not resume before Wednesday at the earliest.

The debate over whether Wembley Stadium should be sold to a private consortium has resurfaced in Westminster corridors, with several Labour backbenchers arguing that public ownership of the iconic venue remains essential to British sporting identity — a claim that the Football Association has so far declined to either endorse or rebuke. Architectural historians, meanwhile, have quietly noted that the stadium's twin towers, demolished in 2003, were among the finest examples of early-twentieth-century reinforced concrete design in England, a legacy that no amount of LED fascia on the current structure can replicate.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect will draw upwards of 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with Slovenian literature taking the spotlight as this year's Guest of Honour. Norwegian debut novelist Astrid Lövheim and Viennese essayist Karl Brenner are among the headline authors scheduled for readings in Hall 3.1, while the fair's film-rights pavilion has already registered record pre-registrations from studios across three continents.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to reject the Holyrood Infrastructure Investment Bill, with 64 MSPs opposing the measure and 59 in favour, after a fractious debate in which Scottish Labour and the Scottish Conservatives joined forces against the SNP-led government. Deputy First Minister Catriona Mhàiri Dunbar, who had championed the bill as essential to modernising the country's crumbling road and rail network, described the outcome as "a betrayal of every community waiting for investment." The Presiding Officer confirmed that three members abstained.

Der Stadtrat von Freiburg im Breisgau hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einem umstrittenen Bebauungsplan für das nördliche Industriegebiet zugestimmt: 24 Stimmen entfielen auf Ja, 19 auf Nein, bei drei Enthaltungen. Oberbürgermeisterin Katrin Ohlendorf zeigte sich erleichtert und sprach von einem „wichtigen Schritt für die wirtschaftliche Entwicklung der Stadt". Die Grünen und die SPD hatten den Plan gemeinsam eingebracht, während die CDU-Fraktion sowie die AfD-nahe Gruppierung „Freie Bürger Freiburg" geschlossen dagegenstimmten.

Defending champions Röskilde Rowing Club edged out Munich's Regatta-Verein Isar by a mere half-length on Saturday at the Henley Royal Regatta, with coxswain Teodora Bjelke steering the Danish crew to a gritty victory in front of an estimated 12,400 spectators packed along the Henley-on-Thames towpath. The final time of 6 minutes 38 seconds was the fastest recorded in the Grand Challenge Cup since 2019.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstag mit 52 zu 31 Stimmen bei vier Enthaltungen einen Fördervertrag für das Wiener Festwochen-Programm 2026 verabschiedet, der insgesamt 18,5 Millionen Euro an öffentlichen Mitteln bereitstellt. Kulturstadträtin Dagmar Holzner (SPÖ) bezeichnete die Entscheidung als „klares Bekenntnis zur kulturellen Vielfalt der Stadt". Die Wiener Festwochen 2026, die vom 8. Mai bis zum 14. Juni im Ronacher sowie an mehreren weiteren Spielstätten stattfinden werden, stehen unter der künstlerischen Leitung von Regisseur Tomáš Vrábel und umfassen Uraufführungen aus Österreich, Tschechien und der Slowakei.

Der Stadtrat von Erfurt hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einen umstrittenen Haushaltsentwurf für das kommende Jahr verabschiedet: 28 Ratsmitglieder stimmten dafür, 21 dagegen, bei vier Enthaltungen. Bürgermeisterin Lena Wollschläger von der SPD sprach von einem „schwierigen, aber notwendigen Kompromiss", während die CDU-Fraktion unter Fraktionsvorsitzendem Klaus-Dieter Preuß das Ergebnis scharf kritisierte und eine Klage vor dem Thüringer Verwaltungsgericht ankündigte. Die Grünen hatten zuvor mit ihrer Zustimmung das Zünglein an der Waage gespielt.

Der Wiener Architekt und Kulturkritiker Benedikt Schornauer hat in seinem neuen Essay für die Zeitschrift „Merkur" eine ungewöhnlich scharfe Analyse der Verkehrspolitik österreichischer Großstädte vorgelegt: Während die ÖBB seit Jahren Milliarden in den Fernverkehr pumpe, verkümmerten die städtischen U-Bahn-Netze zu bloßen Alibiprojekten, die weder den sozialen Ansprüchen eines modernen Gemeinwesens noch den klimapolitischen Zielen der Europäischen Union gerecht würden. Schornauer, der auch als Gastdozent an der Technischen Universität Wien lehrt, fordert eine grundlegende Neubewertung städtischer Mobilität — ohne jedoch konkrete Maßnahmen zu benennen.

Commuters on Frankfurt's S-Bahn network faced severe disruptions throughout the working week after a signalling failure near Hauptwache station knocked out services on the S3, S4, and S6 lines, leaving an estimated 85,000 daily passengers scrambling for alternative routes. DB Regio, which operates the network under contract from the Rhein-Main-Verkehrsverbund, said engineers worked around the clock to restore full functionality, with normal timetables expected to resume by Sunday morning. Replacement bus services were deployed along the affected corridors, though overcrowding at major interchanges drew sharp criticism from the Frankfurt city transport authority.

Copenhagen's city council voted 34 to 17 on Thursday to approve a €2.1 billion expansion of the Metro network, with the centre-left bloc led by the Socialdemokraterne pushing through the measure despite fierce opposition from the Liberal Alliance. The project, which will add nine new stations and extend Line M5 through the northern suburbs of Bispebjerg and Brønshøj, is expected to begin construction in early 2026 and relieve pressure on the heavily congested S-tog lines. Transport operator Metroselskabet confirmed that roughly 180,000 daily commuters stand to benefit once the extension opens, projected for 2031.

Der Stadtrat von Freiburg im Breisgau hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit für die Einführung einer kommunalen Wärmeplanung gestimmt, die bis 2035 eine vollständige Umstellung auf erneuerbare Energien im Fernwärmenetz vorsieht. Bei der Abstimmung entfielen 28 Stimmen auf den Antrag, 19 Stimmen dagegen, während sich vier Ratsmitglieder enthielten. Besonders die Fraktionen der Grünen und der SPD hatten den Vorstoß gemeinsam eingebracht, während die CDU-Fraktion geschlossen dagegenstimmte. „Dies ist ein wichtiger Schritt für unsere klimaneutrale Zukunft", erklärte Bürgermeisterin Klara Wenderoth nach der Sitzung im Historischen Kaufhaus.

Wegen eines Signalschadens im Bereich des Frankfurter Hauptbahnhofs kommt es seit den frühen Morgenstunden des 14. Juli zu erheblichen Verspätungen und Teilausfällen auf den S-Bahn-Linien S3, S4 und S5. Die DB Regio schätzt, dass rund 47.000 Fahrgäste von den Beeinträchtigungen betroffen sind; ein Ende der Störung war am Mittag noch nicht absehbar.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a majority of thirty-one on Thursday to pass the Housing Emergency (Rent Controls) Bill, with 72 votes in favour and 41 against, after a fractious six-hour debate in which Scottish Labour and the Scottish Greens broke with the SNP government on several key amendments. Presiding Officer Siobhán McAllister called the result "historic" before adjourning the chamber, while opposition spokespeople warned that the legislation could deter private investment in Edinburgh and Glasgow.

Borussia Dortmund hat am Samstag im Signal Iduna Park einen überzeugenden 3:1-Heimsieg gegen den FC Augsburg eingefahren und damit seinen dritten Bundesliga-Sieg in Serie gefeiert. Doppeltorschütze Miro Haslinger sowie der eingewechselte Teo Vranković sorgten für die Tore der Gastgeber, während Augsburg lediglich durch einen Elfmeter von Benedikt Oswald verkürzen konnte. Vor 81.365 Zuschauern unterstrich Dortmund seinen Anspruch auf einen Champions-League-Platz.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to back a sweeping reform of the country's social care funding system, with 68 members in favour and 55 against after a fractious four-hour debate that saw the SNP and the Scottish Greens combine forces against a united opposition of Labour, the Conservatives, and the Liberal Democrats. Deputy First Minister Catriona Drummond hailed the result as "a generational shift in how Scotland looks after its most vulnerable citizens," while Conservative health spokesman Alistair Brechin warned the plan would leave a £1.2 billion hole in local authority budgets within three years.

Im packenden Relegationsduell der 2. Bundesliga bezwang der FC Kaiserslautern den Hamburger SV am Samstagabend mit 2:1 vor ausverkauftem Haus im Fritz Walter Stadion. Den Siegtreffer erzielte Mittelfeldspieler Tobias Kreuzer in der 88. Minute, nachdem Jonas Pfeiffer für den HSV zwischenzeitlich ausgeglichen hatte. Mit diesem Ergebnis sichern sich die Roten Teufel vorerst den Klassenerhalt.

Die Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe haben ab Montag die Fahrpreise im gesamten Tarifbereich Berlin AB um durchschnittlich 6,2 Prozent angehoben — die stärkste Erhöhung seit mehr als einem Jahrzehnt. Eine Einzelfahrt in der Kernzone kostet nun 3,50 Euro, das Monatsabo steigt auf 86 Euro. Der Senat begründete den Schritt mit gestiegenen Energiekosten und dem notwendigen Ausbau der Infrastruktur; Fahrgastverbände kündigten Proteste an.

Commuters on the Overground network faced significant disruption on Thursday morning after a signalling fault near Dalston Junction brought services on the East London and Windrush lines to a near-standstill, with Transport for London estimating that roughly 47,000 passengers were affected during the peak hours between 7 a.m. and 10 a.m. TfL said engineers resolved the fault by mid-morning, though delays of up to 35 minutes persisted on the Windrush line into the early afternoon.

The Reykjavík Art Museum opens its long-anticipated retrospective of Icelandic sculptor Sigríður Magnúsdóttir on Friday, gathering more than 140 cast-iron and basalt works spanning four decades of her practice into the museum's Hafnarhús building. Curated by Einar Þórðarson, the exhibition runs through March 9 and is expected to draw audiences from across Scandinavia. Admission is set at 2,000 ISK for adults, with free entry for under-eighteens.

Croke Park was barely half-full when Connaught outsider Dáithí Ó Murchú put Roscommon ahead with a towering point in the 67th minute, but Dublin's Seán Ffrench levelled matters from a tight angle three minutes later to force extra time, before Dublin ultimately claimed the All-Ireland Senior Football Championship title with a 1–14 to 0–15 victory in front of 54,210 spectators on Sunday.

Beim packenden Halbfinale der Österreichischen Wasserball-Meisterschaft am Samstag setzte sich der ASK Linz mit 9:7 gegen den Wiener Sport-Club durch und buchte damit das Ticket für das Finale in der Wiener Stadthalle. Überragender Spieler der Partie war Tobias Kirchmair, der allein fünf Tore erzielte und damit die Hoffnungen der Gastgeber zunichte machte.

Der Stuttgarter Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstag mit 38 zu 14 Stimmen bei zwei Enthaltungen beschlossen, 340 Millionen Euro für den Ausbau der Stadtbahnlinie U12 bis zum Flughafen Stuttgart bereitzustellen. Der Abstimmung war eine mehrstündige Debatte vorausgegangen, in der CDU und Grüne geschlossen für das Projekt votierten, während die AfD-Fraktion den Antrag als „finanzpolitisch unverantwortlich" ablehnte. Oberbürgermeister Frank Hildmann sprach von einem „historischen Tag für die Mobilität der Region" und kündigte an, dass die ersten Bauarbeiten im Frühjahr 2026 beginnen sollen; die neue Strecke soll bis 2031 in Betrieb gehen und täglich rund 28.000 Fahrgäste zusätzlich befördern.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a margin of 71 to 48 on Thursday to pass the Housing Emergency (Rent Controls) Bill, handing First Minister Catriona Dreich her most significant legislative victory since taking office last spring. The Scottish Greens, whose support proved decisive, hailed the result as "a turning point for tenants across Scotland," while the Scottish Conservatives condemned the measure as a threat to investment in the private rental sector. Three Labour MSPs broke with their party whip to vote in favour, complicating the opposition's response ahead of the Holyrood recess.

Commuters on the S-Bahn network in Munich faced severe disruptions on Thursday after a signal failure near Ostbahnhof brought services on the S2 and S6 lines to a near-standstill for roughly four hours during the morning rush, with Deutsche Bahn estimating that around 85,000 passengers were affected. Replacement bus services were deployed along the corridor, though BVG München warned that delays would persist well into the early afternoon. Engineers restored full operations by 1:00 p.m., according to a spokesperson for DB Regio Bayern.

Der SV Wehen Wiesbaden hat am Samstagabend im Heimspiel gegen den 1. FC Kaiserslautern einen hart erkämpften 2:1-Sieg eingefahren und damit den Anschluss an die Aufstiegsplätze der 2. Bundesliga hergestellt. Vor 8.200 Zuschauern im BRITA-Arena erzielte Mittelfeldspieler Tobias Reindl beide Tore für die Gastgeber, während Lautems Angreifer Gregor Vaszilewski den zwischenzeitlichen Ausgleich markierte. „Wir haben heute gezeigt, was in uns steckt", sagte Wiesbadens Trainer Markus Feil nach dem Abpfiff.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that organisers expect will draw upwards of 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with Norwegian literature taking centre stage as the guest-of-honour theme. Among the most anticipated events is a live reading by debut novelist Astrid Haugvold, whose collection of interlocking short stories has already sold out its first print run in Oslo ahead of its international launch at Stand 3.1.

Sweden's Riksdag voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a landmark pension reform package championed by the governing centre-right coalition, with 176 members in favour and 173 against, after a bruising overnight debate that exposed deep rifts within the opposition Social Democrats. Finance Minister Britta Söderholm called the result "a generational commitment," while Social Democrat leader Mattias Grenvik vowed to repeal the measures if his party returns to power.

The question of whether Bratislava's ageing tram network can realistically be modernised within the next decade has preoccupied urban planners and municipal politicians alike for years, yet a coherent funding blueprint has continued to elude the city. A lengthy profile published this week in Der Standard traces the career of infrastructure economist Marta Hollová, whose research at Comenius University has shaped much of the debate, and whose scepticism about public-private partnership models sets her apart from colleagues at the European Investment Bank. The piece also touches, briefly, on how the stalled rolling-stock question has begun to affect voter sentiment ahead of regional assembly elections expected in the spring.

Josefine Mäkinen shrugged off a slow start to deliver a commanding performance at the Gothenburg Half Marathon on Sunday, crossing the line in 1:08:44 to claim her second consecutive title and edge out Rwandan rival Claudette Uwimana by just eleven seconds in front of an estimated 22,000 spectators lining the Avenyn boulevard.

Beim packenden Halbfinale der Deutschen Meisterschaft im Fechten am Samstag in der Helmut-Schön-Sporthalle in Wiesbaden setzte sich der Berliner Fechtclub Rot-Weiß mit 45:38 gegen den FC Tauberbischofsheim durch. Besonders Luisa Kempermann überzeugte mit einer makellosen Serie in der entscheidenden Phase und sicherte ihrem Club damit den Einzug ins Finale, das am Sonntag ausgetragen wird.

Defending champions Rosenborg BK suffered a stunning 3–1 defeat at the hands of Molde FK in a rain-lashed Eliteserien clash at Aker Stadion on Saturday, with Molde striker Håkon Lindstrøm bagging a brace to put the result beyond doubt before the hour mark. The loss leaves Rosenborg seven points adrift of the summit with just four matches remaining in the Norwegian top flight.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a landmark package of rent-control legislation backed by the Scottish Greens and the SNP, with 67 votes in favour, 59 against, and four abstentions — a result that opposition parties swiftly condemned as an attack on the private rental sector. Conservative MSP Fiona Drummond-Cairns described the bill as "ideologically reckless," while Labour's housing spokesperson Callum Rafferty argued it did not go far enough. Deputy First Minister Màiri McLeòd welcomed the passage, saying the legislation would bring "meaningful relief" to renters across Scotland within eighteen months.

The Reykjavík Art Museum opens its long-awaited retrospective of Icelandic sculptor Dagný Sigurðardóttir on Friday, filling the Hafnarhús building with more than ninety bronze and basalt works spanning four decades of her career. Curated by museum director Ólafur Magnússon, the show runs through March 2026 and is accompanied by a trilingual catalogue in Icelandic, English, and Danish. Admission is set at 2,400 ISK for adults.

Partizan Belgrade came from behind to beat Olimpija Ljubljana 3–2 in a tense Adriatic Basketball League clash at Štark Arena on Friday night, with guard Nikola Vranješ draining the decisive three-pointer with eleven seconds remaining to silence a visiting contingent of nearly 4,200 Slovenian supporters. The result keeps Partizan two points clear at the top of the standings heading into the winter break.

The Bavarian state parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a sweeping childcare funding reform backed by the CSU, with 97 members in favour, 89 against, and 4 abstentions — a margin that opposition leader Franziska Hollenbeck of the SPD described as "a mandate too thin to govern boldly." The €340 million package, contested fiercely during a six-hour floor debate in the Maximilianeum, would redirect subsidies away from municipal crèches toward a voucher scheme that critics argue favours wealthier families.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstag mit knapper Mehrheit einen Sonderförderungstopf von zwei Millionen Euro für zeitgenössische Bühnenkunst beschlossen, was unmittelbar den Weg für das lang erwartete Internationale Tanzfestival freimachte, das vom 14. bis 22. März im Volkstheater Wien stattfinden wird. Kulturstadträtin Miriam Holzapfel sprach von einem „historischen Signal für die freie Szene", während die FPÖ-Fraktion als einzige Oppositionsgruppe geschlossen gegen den Antrag stimmte. Das Festival, das unter der künstlerischen Leitung von Jonas Reinthaler steht, präsentiert Ensembles aus zwölf Ländern und richtet sich erstmals auch an Schulklassen mit kostenlosen Matinee-Vorstellungen.

Beim packenden Halbfinale der Deutschen Meisterschaften im Rudern auf dem Beetzsee in Brandenburg an der Havel setzte sich der Berliner Ruder-Club mit einer Zeit von 6:08 Minuten knapp gegen den Frankfurter RV Neptun durch. Vor rund 3.400 Zuschauern steuerte Steuermann Lukas Breitfeld sein Achter-Boot mit bemerkenswerter Präzision ins Ziel, während Tobin Achterberg vom unterlegenen Neptun-Team die schnellste Einzelwertung des Abends erzielte. Das Finale findet am kommenden Sonntag statt.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe mit einem umfangreichen Programm: Rund 4.200 Aussteller aus mehr als 95 Ländern werden in den Hallen der Messe Frankfurt erwartet, und die diesjährige Gastlandpräsentation übernimmt Italien. Als Eröffnungsrednerin wurde die Schriftstellerin Valentina Corradini verpflichtet, die ihren neuen Roman erstmals einem internationalen Publikum vorstellen wird. Tickets für den Publikumstag sind bereits ab 18 Euro erhältlich.

Commuters across the Swiss Mittelland faced widespread disruption on Monday after SBB announced an unplanned suspension of all InterCity services between Bern and Zürich HB, affecting an estimated 47,000 passengers. Engineers discovered a signalling fault near Olten late Sunday night; repairs are expected to take at least 36 hours, with full service restoration unlikely before Wednesday morning. Replacement bus coaches were deployed along the corridor, though officials from SBB conceded that capacity would fall well short of demand during peak hours.

Edinburgh's Usher Hall will host the world premiere of composer Siobhán Murtagh's choral symphony "The Gloaming Tide" on 14 March, drawing an expected audience of 2,200, but concertgoers travelling by rail should note that Scotrail has suspended all services on the Waverley to Haymarket corridor from 11 to 16 March due to urgent overhead line repairs, with an estimated 47,000 passengers affected and replacement bus services operating throughout the closure.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a majority of 74 to 51 on Thursday to pass the Culture Funding Protection Bill, a measure championed by Culture Secretary Fiona Drummond-Laird that ringfences £40 million annually for the arts — a direct lifeline for events such as the Edinburgh International Festival, whose artistic director, Søren Maaløe, confirmed on the same day that the 2025 edition would open on 1 August at the Usher Hall with a commissioning of new orchestral works by Scottish and Nordic composers.

Dynamo Kyiv edged out Shakhtar Donetsk 2–1 in a fiercely contested Ukrainian Premier League derby at the NSC Olimpiyskiy in Kyiv on Saturday evening, with a late header from midfielder Vasyl Kovalenko sealing all three points in front of 31,400 passionate supporters. Shakhtar's consolation goal by striker Dmytro Bilous came too little, too late, as referee decisions and two near-misses in stoppage time kept the home crowd on edge until the final whistle.

The Wiener Konzerthaus will host a rare double bill on 14 March, when the Mahler Chamber Orchestra, conducted by the Finnish maestro Erika Salminen, performs Schubert's "Winterreise" — in a new orchestral arrangement by composer Tomas Brandt — alongside Arvo Pärt's haunting "Spiegel im Spiegel," before the evening concludes with a public conversation between Salminen and cultural journalist Hanna Rosenfeld. Tickets are priced at €45 and the event is presented by the Vienna Konzerthaus Gesellschaft.

Mit einem furiosen 3:1-Sieg gegen den SC Freiburg hat sich Borussia Dortmund am Samstagabend im Signal Iduna Park an die Spitze der Bundesliga-Tabelle zurückgekämpft. Vor 81.365 Zuschauern war es vor allem der überragende Mittelfeldspieler Tomáš Červenka, der mit zwei Treffern und einer Vorlage den Unterschied ausmachte. Freiburgs Anschlusstreffer durch Kwame Asiedu in der 67. Minute konnte die Niederlage der Gäste nicht mehr abwenden.

Reigning champions Eintracht Braunschweig edged out Hannover 96 Reserves 2–1 in a tightly contested Lower Saxony Cup quarter-final at the Eintracht-Stadion on Saturday evening, with midfielder Tobias Reinholt netting the decisive goal in the 88th minute to silence a travelling contingent of roughly 3,400 Hannover supporters.

Der Stadtrat von Freiburg im Breisgau hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit beschlossen, die städtischen Kitas ab dem kommenden Jahr gebührenfrei zu stellen — ein Vorhaben, das die Grünen und die SPD seit Monaten gemeinsam vorangetrieben hatten, während CDU und FDP geschlossen dagegen stimmten. Von den 48 anwesenden Ratsmitgliedern votierten 26 dafür, 19 dagegen, drei enthielten sich. Bürgermeisterin Carolin Steffens sprach von einem „historischen Tag für Familien in unserer Stadt".

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstagabend mit 54 zu 37 Stimmen bei vier Enthaltungen einem umstrittenen Maßnahmenpaket zur Wohnungspolitik zugestimmt, das die SPÖ Wien gemeinsam mit den NEOS ausgearbeitet hatte. Bürgermeister Michael Ludwig sprach von einem „wichtigen Schritt für leistbares Wohnen in der Bundeshauptstadt", während die ÖVP Wien das Vorhaben als unzureichend und ideologisch verblendet bezeichnete. Die Abstimmung fand im Rathaus Wien statt und zog zahlreiche Zuschauer auf die Besuchergalerien.
