Riding a breathtaking second-half comeback, Hibernian FC overturned a two-goal deficit to beat Heart of Midlothian 3–2 at Easter Road on Saturday, with striker Caitríona Brennan netting a stunning 89th-minute winner in front of 16,204 roaring fans. The Edinburgh derby result leaves Hearts bottom of the Scottish Premiership's top six after six rounds of fixtures.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to reject a proposed reform of council tax bands, with 64 MSPs opposed and 59 in favour, delivering a stinging blow to First Minister Catriona Eddlewood's flagship domestic agenda. The Scottish National Party, which had championed the measure as a long-overdue correction to a system unchanged since 1991, accused the Scottish Conservatives and Scottish Labour of a "cynical cross-party stitch-up" designed to embarrass the minority government ahead of next spring's local elections. Deputy Finance Secretary Rónán MacPhail told reporters outside Holyrood that the administration would revisit the bill "in substantially revised form" before the parliamentary recess in June.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstag mit knapper Mehrheit einen Fördervertrag für das Jüdische Filmfestival Wien beschlossen, das vom 6. bis 13. November in der Urania stattfinden wird. Mit 46 Stimmen dafür und 38 dagegen bei zwei Enthaltungen setzte sich die rot-grüne Koalition aus SPÖ und Grünen gegen den Widerstand der FPÖ durch, die das Budget für „kulturpolitisch fragwürdig" hielt. Festivalleiter Benedikt Warmuth zeigte sich erleichtert und kündigte an, dass in diesem Jahr erstmals auch Produktionen aus dem frankophonen Afrika im Programm vertreten sein würden. Das neuntägige Festival zeigt rund 60 Filme in der Urania sowie im Filmcasino und rechnet mit über 8.000 Besucherinnen und Besuchern.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opened its doors on Wednesday to a record crowd of 302,000 visitors, with Colombian author Valentina Ospina Restrepo drawing the longest queues at the signing tables in Hall 3.1 after her debut novel, rendered into eleven languages, was named book of the year by a jury of European publishers. This year marks the fair's 75th edition.

Lausanne's Stade Olympique de la Pontaise hosted a tense Swiss Super League clash on Saturday evening, as FC Lausanne-Sport edged out Servette FC 2–1 before a crowd of 9,800, with midfielder Damien Corthay scoring the decisive goal in the 83rd minute to seal all three points for the hosts.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstag mit 54 zu 31 Stimmen bei 6 Enthaltungen einem umstrittenen Wohnbaupaket zugestimmt, das die Errichtung von rund 4.200 neuen Sozialwohnungen im Stadtgebiet vorsieht. Die regierende Koalition aus SPÖ und NEOS setzte sich dabei gegen den Widerstand von FPÖ und ÖVP durch. Bürgermeister Andreas Baumann sprach von einem „historischen Tag für das soziale Wien", während die Oppositionsfraktionen das Vorhaben als budgetär unverantwortlich kritisierten.

Lena Kirchhoff delivered a masterclass in front of goal as Hannover's VfL Stöcken women hammered TSG Wedemark 5–1 in a fiercely contested Lower Saxony Women's Regional League fixture at the Eilenriedestadion on Sunday afternoon, with Kirchhoff personally accounting for a hat-trick to bring her season tally to seventeen goals. The 3,200 spectators who braved a biting November wind were rewarded with the home side's most convincing performance of the campaign.

Commuters across the Brussels metropolitan area faced severe disruptions on Monday after STIB-MIVB drivers walked off the job in a 24-hour strike over stalled contract negotiations, bringing tram lines 3, 7, and 25 as well as metro lines 1 and 5 to a near-complete standstill and stranding an estimated 340,000 passengers. The operator warned that service would not fully normalise until Tuesday morning at the earliest, urging affected travellers to consider cycling or carpooling where possible.

Wegen umfangreicher Gleiserneuerungsarbeiten im Bereich des Hauptbahnhofs sperrt die S-Bahn München die Stammstrecke zwischen Ostbahnhof und Pasing vom 14. bis 21. März vollständig — ein Schienenersatzverkehr mit rund 120 Bussen soll die geschätzten 480.000 betroffenen Fahrgäste auffangen, wie der Betreiber DB Regio Bayern am Donnerstag mitteilte.

The Reykjavík City Council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a sweeping rezoning plan for the Grafarholt district, with 11 councillors in favour, 8 against, and 2 abstentions, following a heated two-hour debate in which opposition members from the Left-Green Movement accused the ruling Independence Party of prioritising developers over residents. Council leader Sigríður Björk Ásgeirsdóttir defended the measure, arguing that the city's chronic housing shortage left officials with little choice but to open new land for residential construction.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre diesjährige Ausgabe auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt mit über 4.200 Ausstellern aus 95 Ländern. Als Ehrengast tritt in diesem Jahr Norwegen auf, das mit einem umfangreichen Programm aus Lesungen, Podiumsgesprächen und Konzerten vertreten sein wird. Schriftstellerin Ingrid Solberg-Hauge hält am Eröffnungsabend die Hauptrede, bevor der norwegische Autor Kristoffer Dahl aus seinem jüngsten Roman liest. Bis zum 19. Oktober präsentieren Verlage und Agenten aus aller Welt ihre Neuerscheinungen im Zeichen der internationalen Literatur.

The Wiener Festwochen opened its 72nd edition on Friday evening with a sold-out performance at the Burgtheater, where Polish director Maja Kleczewska staged a ferociously inventive production of Ibsen's "Hedda Gabler" that drew nearly 1,400 spectators and left the Viennese audience visibly shaken by its closing tableau.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by Letizia Morandi and designed to evoke the layered textures of medieval manuscripts — occupies a full wing of Hall 4. Ticket prices start at €18 for a day pass, and organisers expect upwards of 300,000 visitors over the five-day fair.

Die Kunstmesse Wien Contemporary eröffnet am Donnerstag ihre zwölfte Ausgabe in der Marx Halle und zeigt bis Sonntag Arbeiten von mehr als 180 Galerien aus 34 Ländern. Kuratorin Mirela Vuković hat in diesem Jahr einen Schwerpunkt auf osteuropäische Positionen gelegt, darunter erstmals eine eigene Sektion für ukrainische Gegenwartskunst. Der Eintritt kostet 22 Euro, ermäßigt 14 Euro.

Commuters on the S-Bahn München network faced widespread delays on Thursday morning after a signalling fault near Ostbahnhof brought services on lines S2, S4, and S8 to a near-standstill for roughly four hours, stranding an estimated 47,000 passengers during the peak rush. DB Regio Bayern, which operates the network, said engineers identified a software fault in the interlocking system installed during last autumn's infrastructure overhaul and that full services were restored by 10:15 a.m. Replacement bus services were deployed along the S4 corridor, though capacity proved insufficient given the scale of the disruption.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opened its doors on Wednesday for what organisers are billing as its most internationally diverse edition yet, with publishers and literary agents from more than 100 countries descending on the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. Guest of honour this year is Norway, whose pavilion — curated by bibliographer and critic Astrid Nygaard-Holm — centres on the theme of wilderness and belonging. The fair runs through Sunday, with a keynote lecture by novelist Erlend Vassvik scheduled for Thursday evening at the Festhalle.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse öffnet am 15. Oktober ihre Tore für das Fachpublikum und feiert in diesem Jahr ihre 76. Ausgabe. Unter dem Gastlandthema steht diesmal Norwegen im Mittelpunkt, vertreten durch namhafte Verlage und Autorinnen wie die Osloer Schriftstellerin Ingrid Vesterås, deren neuer Roman im Suhrkamp Verlag erschienen ist. Rund 4.200 Aussteller aus mehr als 95 Ländern haben sich auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt eingefunden, und die Veranstalter rechnen bis zum Abschlusstag am 19. Oktober mit bis zu 300.000 Besucherinnen und Besuchern.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to reject the Holyrood Infrastructure Devolution Bill, with 64 members voting against and 59 in favour, after a fractious three-hour debate in which Scottish National Party leader Catriona Muirhead accused the Scottish Conservatives of "deliberately stalling a generation's worth of progress." Scottish Labour and the Liberal Democrats both abstained, leaving the SNP to face defeat without cross-party support.

Am Samstag eröffnete die Kunsthalle Mannheim ihre neue Gruppenausstellung „Farben der Stille", die Werke von zwölf zeitgenössischen Malern aus Deutschland und Österreich vereint und bis zum 14. März 2026 zu sehen sein wird – just an jenem Nachmittag, als der SV Waldhof Mannheim im Carl-Benz-Stadion vor 12.400 Zuschauern mit 2:1 gegen den 1. FC Kaiserslautern gewann und damit die Tabellenführung in der 3. Liga übernahm.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opened its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing some 4,200 exhibitors from 95 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose publishers and authors are showcasing a broad sweep of contemporary fiction and poetry across dedicated pavilions. Cornelia Fröhlich, the fair's newly appointed director, described the programme as "the most ambitious in a decade," with headline events including a conversation between Nobel laureate Alice Munro's literary estate and leading Italian novelist Paola Ricci Serrano. Tickets for individual evening readings are priced at €18.

Commuters on Stockholm's southern commuter rail corridor faced severe delays for the third consecutive morning on Wednesday after a points failure near Flemingsberg station forced Mälartåg to reduce services to a single-track operation, affecting an estimated 34,000 passengers during the morning rush. SJ AB, which manages several overlapping services on the same corridor, warned that knock-on disruptions could persist through Friday as engineering teams work to replace the faulty switching mechanism. Passengers travelling between Uppsala and Södertälje were advised to use SL's pendeltåg services as an alternative, though those trains were already operating at full capacity.

The ageing grandeur of Vienna's Ringstraße has long drawn architects, historians, and tourists alike, but the question of how the boulevard's iconic tram corridor should evolve over the coming decades remains stubbornly unresolved — a tangle of competing visions involving the Wien Museum, the city's transport authority Wiener Linien, and several heritage preservation bodies whose mandates frequently overlap and occasionally contradict one another.

Brendan Osei-Mensah scored twice in the final twelve minutes to hand Harrogate Town a dramatic 3–2 victory over Carlisle United at Wetherby Road on Saturday, keeping the hosts' League Two promotion hopes firmly alive with only six games remaining in the season.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a razor-thin margin on Thursday to pass the Holyrood Housing Emergency Bill, with 65 members backing the legislation against 62 opponents and three abstentions — a result that leaves First Minister Catriona Dreich scrambling to reassure coalition partners in the Scottish Greens that rent controls will be tightened further before the bill receives royal assent. The SNP, which had pushed the measure through committee stage after months of acrimonious debate, welcomed the outcome as "an historic day for tenants across Scotland," while Scottish Conservative leader Alistair Frew called the vote "reckless and economically illiterate."

The Swedish parliament voted on Thursday to approve a sweeping cultural heritage bill championed by the ruling Social Democrats, allocating 280 million kronor over four years to preserve historic sites and fund regional arts programmes — a move that Culture Minister Britta Söderström hailed as "a generational commitment to Swedish identity." The legislation passed by 187 votes to 142, with the Moderate Party leading the opposition. Riding the wave of renewed public interest in the arts, the Gothenburg International Film Festival announced the same day that its 2025 edition would open with the world premiere of Karolina Vretemark's debut feature, "Vinterljus", at the Draken cinema on 24 January.

Beim Stadtderby im Frauen-Handball trennten sich der TSV Hannover-Burgdorf II und der SC Langenhagen am Samstagabend mit einem 27:27-Unentschieden – ein Ergebnis, das beide Trainer gleichermaßen zufrieden und enttäuscht zurückließ. Vor 1.140 Zuschauern in der Eilenriedehalle lieferten sich die Teams einen packenden Kampf, wobei Hannover-Burgdorfs Rückraumspielerin Svenja Pöhlmann mit neun Treffern zur herausragenden Akteurin des Abends avancierte. In der Tabelle der Regionsoberliga Niedersachsen ändert sich durch das Remis wenig – beide Klubs verharren im gesicherten Mittelfeld.

Der Stadtrat von Freiburg im Breisgau hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit für die Einführung eines kostenlosen Nahverkehrstickets für alle Auszubildenden im Stadtgebiet gestimmt. 34 Ratsmitglieder votierten dafür, 29 dagegen, bei vier Enthaltungen. Die treibenden Kräfte hinter dem Antrag waren die Grünen und die SPD, während die CDU-Fraktion geschlossen ablehnte. Bürgermeisterin Katrin Söllner-Brandt sprach von einem „sozialpolitischen Meilenstein", der jungen Menschen den Einstieg ins Berufsleben erleichtern solle.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opened its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, agents, and literary luminaries from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairground. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by the novelist and cultural diplomat Serena Castellucci — stretches across an entire hall and showcases more than 200 Italian titles in translation. Organisers expect upwards of 300,000 visitors before the fair closes on Sunday.

The Swedish Riksdag passed a sweeping overhaul of the country's housing subsidy framework on Thursday by a margin of 187 votes to 162, with 11 abstentions, after a bruising overnight debate in which the centre-right Tidö bloc outmanoeuvred opposition calls for an independent review. Finance Minister Britta Söderholm hailed the outcome as "a decisive step toward addressing Sweden's chronic shortage of affordable homes," while Social Democrat spokesperson Lennart Öqvist warned that the cuts to municipal construction grants would hit mid-sized cities hardest.

Commuters on the Jubilee line faced severe disruptions on Thursday morning after a signalling fault near Waterloo station brought services to a standstill for nearly four hours, with Transport for London estimating that some 85,000 passengers were affected. Engineers from TfL's Network Operations Centre restored full service by 11:47 a.m., though residual delays persisted well into the afternoon peak.

The Scottish Parliament voted on Thursday by 73 votes to 52 to approve the Edinburgh Tram Network Expansion Bill, handing the Scottish National Party a significant legislative win ahead of next year's Holyrood elections. The bill, championed by Transport Minister Catriona Dunbar, authorises a £340 million extension of the existing tram line from York Place northward to Granton Harbour, adding seven new stops and an estimated 28,000 daily passengers to the network once services begin in late 2027. Opposition parties, including Scottish Labour and the Scottish Conservatives, had argued the projected costs were understated, but ultimately failed to muster enough votes to block the measure.

The city of Salzburg marked an unusually festive weekend when the Salzburg Philharmonic, under the baton of guest conductor Mirela Voss, opened its autumn season at the Felsenreitschule with a sold-out programme of Bruckner and Mahler on Friday evening — drawing an audience of 2,340 — before the entire city's attention shifted the following afternoon to the Red Bull Arena, where FC Red Bull Salzburg edged out SK Sturm Graz 2–1 in a tightly contested Austrian Bundesliga fixture that attracted 29,500 spectators, with midfielder Tomáš Benček widely credited as the decisive figure after his 88th-minute winner.

Borussia Dortmund edged out RB Leipzig 2–1 at Signal Iduna Park on Saturday evening in a tightly contested Bundesliga encounter that kept 81,365 fans on their feet until the final whistle, with a late header from striker Tomáš Večeřa sealing all three points for the hosts.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to approve a sweeping new housing affordability bill, with 67 members backing the legislation against 59 opposed and four abstentions, in a debate that exposed deep fault lines between the SNP-led government and a fractious Conservative opposition. The bill, championed by Housing Minister Catriona Dreich and fiercely contested by Tory spokesperson Fraser Ogilvie, would cap private rental increases at three per cent annually across all 32 local authority areas. Labour MSPs proved decisive, lending their support to the government benches at the eleventh hour after securing a last-minute amendment on social housing targets.

Commuters on the Overground faced significant delays on Monday morning after a signalling failure between Highbury & Islington and Dalston Junction brought services on the East London line to a near-standstill for roughly four hours, affecting an estimated 34,000 passengers during the peak rush. Transport for London confirmed that engineering crews worked to isolate the fault by mid-morning, with a full timetable restored shortly before noon. A TfL spokesperson apologised for the disruption and said a full technical review would be completed within the week.

Commuters on Sydney's T1 North Shore and Western Line faced severe disruptions on Thursday after a signalling fault near Strathfield station brought morning peak services to a near standstill, with delays stretching beyond 90 minutes at their worst. Sydney Trains confirmed that approximately 85,000 passengers were affected before engineers restored full operations shortly after 11 a.m., and the operator has promised a formal review of the ageing signalling infrastructure.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, with Norwegian literature taking centre stage as the Guest of Honour. Publishers from more than 100 countries are expected to descend on the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, and this year's programme includes a keynote lecture by celebrated Norwegian novelist Ingrid Vaaland, whose debut in translation has already drawn considerable pre-fair buzz. Organisers anticipate roughly 300,000 visitors over the five-day run.

Commuters on the Northern and Jubilee lines faced severe delays on Friday morning after a signalling fault near London Bridge brought large sections of both routes to a near-standstill for almost three hours, with Transport for London estimating that roughly 85,000 passengers were affected before normal service was gradually restored shortly before noon.

The lakeside city of Lugano had reason to celebrate twice over this past weekend: the Lugano Jazz Festival opened its three-day run at the LAC – Lugano Arte e Cultura on Friday evening to a sold-out crowd of 2,400, headlined by pianist Marta Selvaggini and her quintet, while just a few kilometres away, FC Lugano edged Servette FC 2–1 in a tightly contested Super League fixture at the Cornaredo Stadium on Saturday afternoon, with striker Danilo Ferreira scoring the decisive goal in the eighty-ninth minute before 7,600 supporters.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a narrow margin on Thursday to pass the Housing Emergency (Temporary Measures) Bill, with 68 members in favour, 55 against, and 4 abstaining — a result that the SNP hailed as a landmark step toward addressing the country's acute rental crisis, even as Scottish Labour's housing spokeswoman Catriona Meiklejohn warned that the bill's rent-cap provisions were "too blunt an instrument" and would deter private investment across Glasgow, Edinburgh, and smaller commuter towns alike.

Commuters on the S-Bahn network in Munich faced severe delays on Thursday morning after a signalling fault near Ostbahnhof blocked all eastbound services for nearly four hours, with Deutsche Bahn estimating that roughly 85,000 passengers were affected before normal operations resumed shortly before noon.

The Swedish Riksdag narrowly approved a landmark immigration reform package on Thursday, with 176 votes in favour and 173 against, after weeks of fractious debate that exposed deep rifts within the ruling coalition. Prime Minister-designate Britta Söderholm, whose Moderate Party had staked its credibility on the measure, called the outcome "a difficult but necessary step for Sweden." The Social Democrats and the Greens voted unanimously against the bill, arguing it would undermine the country's humanitarian obligations, while the Sweden Democrats provided the decisive margin of support.

The Reykjavík Art Museum opened its long-awaited retrospective of Icelandic sculptor Birta Magnúsdóttir on Friday, drawing an opening-night crowd of roughly 2,400 visitors to Hafnarhús — the converted harbour warehouse that remains the city's most atmospheric exhibition space. Curated by Þórður Einarsson of the Nordic Arts Council, the show spans four decades of Magnúsdóttir's work in basalt and cast aluminium, and will run through 14 September.

Die ÖBB hat angekündigt, dass die Weststrecke zwischen Wien Hauptbahnhof und Salzburg Hauptbahnhof ab dem 14. März für voraussichtlich drei Wochen wegen umfangreicher Gleissanierungsarbeiten vollständig gesperrt wird; rund 28.000 Reisende täglich sind davon betroffen. Als Ersatz werden Schienenersatzbusse eingesetzt, die jedoch mit deutlichen Fahrzeitverlängerungen von bis zu zwei Stunden rechnen müssen.

Brøndby IF claimed a hard-fought 2–1 victory over FC Midtjylland at Brøndby Stadion on Saturday, with striker Mikkel Thøgersen netting a late winner in the 88th minute to keep the hosts' Superliga title hopes alive. The attendance of 19,340 made it the loudest the ground had been all season, according to club officials.

Die Berliner Verkehrsbetriebe haben ab kommendem Montag eine weitreichende Streckensperrung auf der U-Bahnlinie U8 zwischen den Stationen Gesundbrunnen und Hermannstraße angekündigt: Wegen dringender Gleiserneuerungsarbeiten wird der Abschnitt für voraussichtlich drei Wochen vollständig gesperrt, ein Ersatzverkehr mit Bussen wird eingerichtet. Täglich sind rund 85.000 Fahrgäste betroffen.

Der Gemeinderat von Innsbruck hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit für den neuen Bebauungsplan im Stadtteil Pradl gestimmt: 23 Räte votierten dafür, 19 dagegen, bei vier Enthaltungen. Die ÖVP und die Grünen trugen den Plan gemeinsam, während die FPÖ sowie die SPÖ geschlossen ablehnten. Bürgermeisterin Claudia Wörndle erklärte nach der Abstimmung, der Beschluss sei „ein wichtiger Schritt für leistbares Wohnen in Innsbruck".

Dinamo Tbilisi edged Levski Sofia 2–1 in a tense Europa Conference League qualifier at the Mikheil Meskhi Stadium on Thursday evening, with midfielder Lasha Kvaratskhelia's stoppage-time header proving decisive in front of 14,200 supporters.

Die ÖBB hat am Donnerstag bekanntgegeben, dass die Weststrecke zwischen Salzburg und Linz vom 14. bis zum 21. Februar wegen umfangreicher Gleiserneuerungsarbeiten vollständig gesperrt wird. Rund 38.000 Fahrgäste täglich sind von der Sperrung betroffen; als Ersatz werden Schienenersatzbusse auf der gesamten Strecke eingerichtet. „Wir bitten alle Reisenden um Verständnis und empfehlen, auf Fernzüge über Wien auszuweichen", erklärte ÖBB-Sprecherin Margarethe Grünwald.

The Reykjavik City Council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a sweeping housing affordability ordinance, with 9 councillors in favour, 6 against, and 2 abstentions, after nearly four hours of heated debate in which Independence Party representatives accused the ruling Left-Green coalition of overreaching into private property rights. Council speaker Sigríður Magnúsdóttir called the vote "a historic step toward making this city liveable for ordinary families," while opposition bloc leader Árni Þórsson vowed to seek a legal review of the measure before it takes effect in January 2026.

Stockholm's public transport authority, SL, confirmed on Thursday that a series of unplanned signal failures along the Tunnelbana's Green Line will suspend all service between Fridhemsplan and Skärmarbrink from Friday evening through Sunday midnight, leaving an estimated 340,000 commuters reliant on a hastily arranged replacement bus network. Engineers cited a cascading fault in ageing track-circuit hardware installed in the early 1990s as the primary cause, and SL warned that repair works could overrun into Monday morning if spare parts sourced from a supplier in Malmö are delayed.

The Scottish Parliament narrowly approved a sweeping housing-reform bill on Thursday after three hours of fractious debate, with 67 members voting in favour, 59 against, and 4 abstaining — a margin that left opposition benches visibly shaken. The legislation, championed by Housing Secretary Fiona Dunbar of the SNP and bitterly contested by Scottish Conservative leader Alasdair Murchie, introduces rent caps for the private sector across all 32 council areas. Labour MSPs, led by Catriona Osei, ultimately backed the measure, providing the government with the slim majority it needed.

Kristóf Vásárhelyi delivered a masterclass at Laugardalsvöllur on Saturday evening, converting twice in the second half as Fram Reykjavik overcame Breiðablik 3–1 to move into second place in the Úrvalsdeild table. A crowd of 4,200 watched Breiðablik equalise through Gunnar Sigurðsson before Vásárhelyi restored the lead eight minutes later, with substitute Þórður Helgason sealing the win deep into stoppage time.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to pass the Renewable Heating Transition Bill, with 67 members backing the legislation against 59 opposed and four abstentions, handing the Scottish National Party a fragile but significant win after weeks of bruising cross-party negotiations. The bill, championed by Energy Minister Catriona Erskine and opposed most vocally by Scottish Conservative leader Hamish Dunbar, will oblige local authorities to phase out oil-fired boilers in public buildings by 2031. Labour MSPs ultimately split their votes, leaving the chamber's final tally closer than the SNP had anticipated.

The Flemish regional parliament in Brussels voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a controversial nitrogen reduction bill, with 72 members in favour, 49 against, and 6 abstentions — a result that drew immediate condemnation from agricultural lobby groups but was hailed by the governing coalition of N-VA, Vooruit, and cd&v as a long-overdue step toward cleaner waterways and protected nature reserves across Belgium.

The Swedish Riksdag voted by a margin of 213 to 136, with 14 abstentions, on Thursday to approve a sweeping overhaul of the country's asylum and immigration policy, handing Prime Minister Tobias Wennerström's centre-right coalition its most significant legislative victory since taking office in autumn 2022. The Moderaterna and Sverigedemokraterna jointly backed the bill, while the Socialdemokraterna led the opposition against it, arguing that several provisions violated EU human rights frameworks. Observers noted that the vote, held in the Riksdag chamber in Stockholm, marks a decisive shift in Swedish political alignments that few had anticipated as recently as last spring.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day celebration of the written word, with Norwegian literature taking centre stage as the guest-of-honour nation for the first time in over two decades. This year's edition, the seventy-seventh, will feature more than 4,000 exhibitors from 95 countries spread across the sprawling Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. Curator-in-chief Ingrid Halvorsen-Bjørnstad has assembled an ambitious programme that includes headline readings by novelist Petter Ramstad-Lie and essayist Camille Deschênes-Vautrin, alongside a landmark retrospective on postwar Scandinavian publishing. Tickets are priced from €18 for a single-day pass.

Thousands of visitors are expected to descend on Edinburgh's Leith Walk this weekend for the opening of "Northern Palette," a sprawling open-air painting festival showcasing over sixty Scottish and Scandinavian artists, but commuters and festivalgoers alike should brace for significant disruption: Lothian Buses has announced that services on routes 7, 10, and 14 will be suspended from Friday evening through Sunday midnight as resurfacing works along Leith Walk get under way, affecting an estimated 34,000 passengers over the three-day period.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt mit über 4.000 Ausstellern aus mehr als 100 Ländern. Als Ehrengast tritt in diesem Jahr Norwegen auf, und die norwegische Autorin Sigrid Helland wird die Eröffnungsrede halten. Veranstalter des weltweit größten Buchmarkts ist der Börsenverein des Deutschen Buchhandels, der das Programm unter das Motto „Stimmen der Stille" gestellt hat. Die Messe läuft bis zum 19. Oktober und richtet sich sowohl an Fachbesucher als auch an das breite Publikum.

The Dáil narrowly passed a motion of no confidence in the coalition government late on Thursday, with 83 votes in favour and 79 against, after Tánaiste Síle Ó Brádaigh's announcement that the junior partners had withdrawn their support following a bitter dispute over proposed cuts to rural healthcare spending. Sinn Féin, leading the opposition bloc, hailed the result as a mandate for change, while Fine Gael insisted the margin was too slim to justify the collapse of a functioning administration. Talks on forming a new government are expected to begin as early as next week.

The Swedish Riksdag narrowly approved a sweeping overhaul of the country's housing subsidy framework on Thursday, with 176 members voting in favour and 173 against, after weeks of fractious negotiations that had threatened to collapse the fragile coalition between the Moderate Party and the Sweden Democrats. Finance Minister Britta Söderström, who had championed the reform since assuming office, called the outcome "a necessary correction to decades of market distortion," while opposition leader Gunnar Hjelm of the Social Democrats vowed to reverse the legislation if his party returned to power following the next general election.

Grasshopper Club Zürich fell to a bruising 3–1 defeat against FC Lugano at the Stadio di Cornaredo on Saturday evening, a result that leaves the Zurich side rooted in the relegation zone with only six rounds of the Super League season remaining. Midfielder Tomas Ferreira opened the scoring for Lugano in the 18th minute before a brace from substitute Elias Bucher put the hosts out of reach; a late consolation from Grasshopper's Finnish winger Paavo Mäkinen did little to alter the mood of some 6,200 sodden but still vocal travelling supporters.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, welcoming publishers, authors, and literary agents from over ninety countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairground for five days of panels, signings, and rights negotiations. This year's guest of honour is Italy, and the pavilion curated by the Associazione Italiana Editori promises a sweeping programme of readings by contemporary Italian voices, including debut novelist Serena Cattaneo and veteran essayist Marco Pellegrini. Tickets for the public days are priced at €18, with organisers expecting upwards of 300,000 visitors by Sunday.

Commuters on the S-Bahn München network faced significant delays on Thursday morning after a points failure near Ostbahnhof brought services on lines S2, S4, and S8 to a near standstill for more than three hours, affecting an estimated 47,000 passengers during the peak rush. DB Regio Bayern, which operates the network, urged travellers to use U-Bahn services as an alternative and said engineering crews had restored full operations by 10:15 a.m. No replacement bus service was deployed, drawing criticism from the Münchner Verkehrsgesellschaft passenger advisory board.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, drawing publishers, agents, and literary luminaries from more than ninety countries to the Messe Frankfurt exhibition grounds for what organisers have billed as the largest edition in the fair's post-pandemic history. This year's Guest of Honour is Slovenia, whose pavilion — curated by Maja Vidmar and designed around the theme of translation as cultural bridge-building — occupies a sweeping 1,200-square-metre hall in Hall 4.1. Tickets are priced from €18 for a single day, with the public programme running through Sunday.

Commuters on the Merseyrail network faced severe disruption on Thursday morning after a signalling fault near Lime Street station forced the suspension of all services on the Northern and Wirral lines for nearly four hours, with Merseytravel estimating that around 47,000 passengers were affected before partial services resumed shortly after midday.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its 76th edition on Wednesday, drawing publishers, agents, and literary scouts from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for five days of rights negotiations, panel discussions, and public readings. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by the Rome-based cultural foundation Istituto per il Commercio Estero — promises an expansive programme of contemporary Italian fiction, poetry, and graphic novels. Admission to the public days runs €18 per adult.

The Finnish parliament passed a sweeping overhaul of the country's asylum legislation on Thursday by a margin of 117 votes to 64, with 18 abstentions, after a fractious overnight debate that laid bare the deepening rifts within the ruling coalition. Prime Minister Aleksi Mäkinen hailed the result as "a necessary modernisation," while opposition leader Siiri Korhonen condemned the reforms as cruel and legally dubious. The National Coalition Party and the Finns Party, both partners in the government, drove the bill through over fierce resistance from the Social Democrats and the Greens.

The Swedish Riksdag narrowly approved a sweeping pension reform package on Thursday, with 176 votes in favour and 173 against, after weeks of fractious debate that exposed deep rifts within the ruling coalition. Finance Minister Britta Söderholm hailed the result as "a generational compact," while the opposition Sweden Democrats and Left Party condemned the measure as an austerity measure dressed up in the language of solidarity. The vote is expected to take effect from 1 January 2026.

Rosenborg BK came from behind to defeat Molde FK 3–2 in a breathless Eliteserien encounter at Lerkendal Stadion on Sunday evening, with midfielder Håkon Sveberg netting the decisive goal in the 88th minute to send the home faithful into raptures. The win pulls Rosenborg to within three points of the league summit with just four fixtures remaining.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, October 15, drawing publishers, literary agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt for what organisers describe as the most ambitious edition in a decade. Guest of honour this year is Norway, whose pavilion — designed by architect Solvei Ørnsrud — features a sweeping installation of floor-to-ceiling hand-illustrated panels celebrating Nordic storytelling traditions. Harald Kjærnli, Norway's minister for culture, will deliver the opening address alongside Juergen Boos, director of the fair, at 10 a.m. in Hall 4.1.

Commuters on the suburban rail network around Frankfurt faced severe disruptions on Thursday after Deutsche Bahn engineers discovered a signalling fault near Darmstadt that forced the suspension of services on the S3 and S4 lines for at least six hours. An estimated 47,000 passengers were affected during the morning rush, with replacement bus services laid on between Darmstadt Hauptbahnhof and Frankfurt Süd. DB spokeswoman Lena Wörthmann said engineers were working to restore full service before the evening peak, though she warned that delays of up to forty minutes could persist throughout the day.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, agents, and literary tastemakers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by Chiara Benedetti and Luca Ferrante — promises an ambitious programme of readings, panel discussions, and live translations exploring the full breadth of contemporary Italian letters. Tickets for the public days are priced at €18.

Commuters across greater Copenhagen faced mounting disruption on Thursday after DSB suspended all S-Tog services on lines A and E for roughly six hours, citing a signalling fault detected near Vanløse station that engineers said could not be safely bypassed. An estimated 85,000 passengers were affected during the morning and early-afternoon peak, with the national rail operator deploying replacement buses on both corridors while repair crews worked to isolate the defective relay unit. Normal services resumed by 14:30, DSB confirmed in an evening statement.

When the new cycle lane along Copenhagen's Nørrebrogade was first proposed three years ago, it was dismissed by critics as an expensive indulgence; today, urban planners from as far afield as Melbourne and São Paulo cite it as a benchmark for integrating cycling infrastructure into dense residential corridors without strangling bus routes operated by Movia. Whether such lessons can be transplanted to cities whose political cultures are far more car-dependent remains, as one recent Transport Research Laboratory report drily noted, an open question.

Wegen eines Signalanlagendefekts im Bereich des Hauptbahnhofs Hannover kommt es seit Donnerstagmorgen zu erheblichen Verspätungen und Teilausfällen auf den S-Bahn-Linien S1, S2 und S5. Die DB Regio teilte mit, dass rund 47.000 Fahrgäste täglich von den Beeinträchtigungen betroffen seien; ein Ende der Störung war bis Redaktionsschluss nicht absehbar.

The debate over whether to extend the Jubilee line to Thamesmead has resurfaced in planning circles, with Transport for London acknowledging in its latest infrastructure review that the southeastern corridor remains chronically underserved — yet no funding commitment has been made, and Labour-controlled Greenwich Council has so far declined to take a formal position ahead of the next mayoral budget cycle.

Die Österreichischen Bundesbahnen (ÖBB) haben ab Montag auf der Strecke zwischen Salzburg und Linz die Fahrpreise um durchschnittlich 4,9 Prozent angehoben, was nach Angaben des Unternehmens auf gestiegene Energiekosten und Infrastrukturinvestitionen zurückzuführen ist. Schätzungsweise 38.000 Pendlerinnen und Pendler sind täglich von der Erhöhung betroffen. Der Fahrgastverband „Pro Bahn Österreich" kündigte an, die Entscheidung gemeinsam mit der Arbeiterkammer rechtlich prüfen zu lassen.

The Reykjavík Art Museum opens its long-awaited retrospective of Icelandic sculptor Björn Halldórsson on Friday, drawing together more than 140 works spanning four decades of the artist's career — from brooding early bronzes to the luminous glass installations that made his international reputation. Curator Sigríður Magnúsdóttir has arranged the show across all three of the museum's buildings, with the centrepiece, a towering steel-and-obsidian triptych commissioned specifically for the occasion, installed in the Hafnarhús wing overlooking the harbour. Tickets are priced at 2,500 ISK for adults, and the exhibition runs through 14 September.

The Scottish Parliament voted on Thursday to extend free prescriptions to all residents regardless of age or income, with 81 members backing the measure, 42 opposing it, and 3 abstaining — a comfortable majority for the Scottish National Party, which had championed the policy as a cornerstone of its spring legislative agenda. Conservative MSPs argued the move would strain an already stretched NHS Scotland budget, but Health Secretary Catriona Dunbar dismissed those concerns as "scaremongering without substance." Labour declined to whip its members, resulting in a split delegation that analysts said reflected persistent internal tensions over the party's devolution platform.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, October 15, welcoming publishers, authors, and literary agents from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for five days of readings, panel discussions, and rights negotiations. This year's Guest of Honour is Italy, with the Associazione Italiana Editori curating a sprawling pavilion dedicated to Italian writing across the centuries, from Renaissance manuscripts to contemporary crime fiction. Organisers expect upward of 300,000 visitors over the course of the fair, which runs through Sunday, October 19.

Linfield FC edged out Glentoran 2–1 at Windsor Park on Saturday evening in a fiercely contested Irish Premiership derby, with midfielder Ciarán Mooney netting the decisive goal in the 88th minute to keep Linfield top of the table. A crowd of 9,800 packed the north Belfast ground, making it one of the best-attended local fixtures of the season.

Commuters on the Merseyrail network faced severe delays on Wednesday morning after a signalling failure near Lime Street Station brought services on the Northern and Wirral lines to a near-standstill for roughly four hours, leaving an estimated 34,000 passengers stranded or forced onto replacement bus services. Merseyrail engineers restored full operations by midday, though the operator cautioned that residual knock-on delays could persist into the evening peak.

Midfielder Cosima Brandt scored twice in the final twelve minutes to hand Eintracht Frankfurt a dramatic 3–2 victory over Bayern München at Deutsche Bank Park on Saturday, keeping Frankfurt's Frauen-Bundesliga title hopes very much alive heading into the winter break.

Commuters across Greater Manchester faced significant disruption on Thursday after Avanti West Coast and Northern Rail suspended all services between Manchester Piccadilly and Liverpool Lime Street following an overnight signalling failure near Warrington Bank Quay. Network Rail engineers, who arrived on site shortly after 03:00, warned that repairs could take the better part of the day, leaving an estimated 47,000 passengers to seek alternative travel arrangements. Replacement bus services were deployed on the corridor, though Transport for Greater Manchester acknowledged that capacity would fall well short of demand during morning peak hours.

Riding a fierce second-half comeback, Ferencváros TC defeated Debreceni VSC 3–1 at Groupama Aréna on Saturday evening to extend their lead at the top of the OTP Bank Liga table. Midfielder Bálint Oroszi, who had been quietly outstanding all season, scored twice in the final twenty minutes to seal the points in front of a roaring crowd of 22,400. The result leaves Debreceni VSC without a win in five league outings.

Grasshopper Club Zürich came from behind to defeat FC Winterthur 3–2 in a tense Super League fixture at the Letzigrund on Saturday evening, with midfielder Luca Ferrante scoring the decisive goal in the 87th minute to send a crowd of 11,400 into raptures. The result lifts Grasshopper out of the relegation zone with just four rounds of the season remaining.

Beim packenden Nachbarschaftsduell in der Regionalliga Südwest bezwang der SV Waldhof Mannheim den FC-Astoria Walldorf vor 8.450 Zuschauern im Carl-Benz-Stadion mit 3:1. Die Tore für den Gastgeber erzielten Lukas Fendt (18.), Benedikt Ohlrogge (54.) und Marvin Quispe (87.), während Walldorfs Olu Adewunmi den zwischenzeitlichen Ausgleich besorgte. Mit dem Sieg kletterte Waldhof auf den dritten Tabellenplatz der Regionalliga Südwest.

The Reykjavík City Council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a sweeping new housing affordability ordinance, with councillors backing the measure 11 votes to 8, after nearly four hours of fractious debate. The motion, championed by the Left-Green Movement and supported by the Social Democratic Alliance, would cap annual rent increases at 3.5 percent across all residential properties in the capital. Centre-right councillors from the Independence Party led the opposition, arguing the policy would deter investment in the private rental market. Council chair Sigríður Magnúsdóttir declared the result binding and said implementation guidance would be issued before the end of the year.

The Swedish Riksdag narrowly passed a landmark housing reform bill on Wednesday, with 176 votes in favour and 173 against, after weeks of fractious debate that nearly collapsed the minority government of Prime Minister Stellan Bromark. The Socialdemokraterna, propped up by tacit support from the Vänsterpartiet, managed to push the legislation through despite fierce opposition from the Moderaterna and Sverigedemokraterna, who jointly condemned the measure as fiscally reckless. The bill, which strips municipal councils of their right to cap private rental increases beyond a nationally set index, is expected to take effect by 1 January 2026.

Commuters on the S-Bahn network in Munich face significant disruptions this week after Deutsche Bahn announced emergency trackwork on the City Tunnel between Hauptbahnhof and Ostbahnhof, forcing all S-Bahn lines to terminate at either end of the tunnel rather than pass through. The works, which began on Monday and are scheduled to last until Friday evening, are necessary to replace deteriorating overhead-line equipment that engineers say could otherwise fail before year's end. Deutsche Bahn estimates that roughly 840,000 passengers will be affected over the five-day closure, and has arranged replacement bus services on twelve corridors across the inner city.

Wegen des Bundesliga-Heimspiels des FC St. Pauli gegen Bayer 04 Leverkusen am Samstag, den 14. September, sperrt die Hamburger Hochbahn ab 16 Uhr die U3-Haltestelle Feldstraße für den regulären Fahrgastbetrieb und richtet Sonderpendelbuse zwischen Sternschanze und Schlump ein. Das Spiel im Millerntor-Stadion, das um 18:30 Uhr angepfiffen wird, verzeichnete mit 29.546 Zuschauern eine ausverkaufte Kulisse; Torjäger Mikkel Aaronsen erzielte in der 74. Minute den einzigen Treffer zum 1:0-Sieg der Gastgeber.

Commuters on the Øresund Line faced severe delays on Thursday morning after a signalling fault between Malmö Central and Copenhagen Airport Kastrup forced Swedish rail operator SJ to run a reduced timetable for more than six hours, leaving an estimated 34,000 passengers stranded or significantly late. Repair crews worked through the disruption, and full services were restored by early afternoon, though SJ warned that knock-on delays could persist into the evening peak.

Ferencváros came from behind to defeat Újpest FC 3–2 in a bruising Budapest derby at Groupama Aréna on Saturday evening, with striker Benedek Oláh netting a decisive 87th-minute header to seal all three points in front of a roaring crowd of 22,400. The result keeps Ferencváros top of the OTP Bank Liga with a seven-point cushion heading into the winter break.

Commuters on the Overground faced severe delays on Tuesday morning after a signalling fault between Highbury & Islington and Dalston Kingsland brought services on the Windrush Line to a near-standstill for roughly four hours, with Transport for London estimating that around 38,000 passengers were affected before engineers restored full operation shortly before noon.

Commuters on the Jubilee line faced severe delays for the third consecutive morning on Wednesday after a points failure near Stratford station forced Transport for London to run a reduced service between Stanmore and Canada Water, leaving an estimated 47,000 passengers scrambling for alternative routes. A TfL spokesperson said engineers were working to resolve the fault but could not confirm when full service would resume.

The Reykjavík City Council narrowly approved a sweeping social housing expansion on Thursday evening, with councillors voting 13 to 8 in favour after a fractious three-hour debate that exposed deep rifts within the ruling coalition. Deputy Mayor Sigríður Óskarsdóttir, who championed the measure, said the scheme would deliver 2,400 new affordable units across the capital's outer districts by 2031, while opposition leader Gunnar Þórsson of the Independence Party warned that construction costs had been "dangerously underestimated." Two councillors abstained, reflecting the unease of centrists who supported the policy's aims but questioned its financing model.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a razor-thin margin on Thursday to advance a bill tightening rent controls across all major urban areas, with 65 members backing the measure against 60 opposed and three abstentions. Deputy First Minister Catriona Ogilvy, who steered the legislation through a bruising committee stage, called the result "a historic commitment to tenants who have been priced out of their own cities." The Scottish Conservatives, led in the chamber by Alistair Drummond, argued the bill would deter investment and worsen housing supply, while the Scottish Greens threw their support behind the SNP-led government to secure the majority.

The Flemish parliament narrowly approved a controversial housing reform bill on Thursday, with 72 votes in favour and 63 against, after a bitter overnight debate that exposed deep fractures within the ruling coalition. The New Flemish Alliance and the Christian People's Party backed the measure, while the Socialists and Greens voted in opposition, warning that the legislation would accelerate the privatisation of social housing stock across Belgium. Minister-President Liesbet Vandenberghe called the outcome "a hard-fought but necessary step," though critics from her own benches abstained in a pointed display of dissent.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for what organisers are billing as the most ambitious edition in a decade, with the United States serving as Guest of Honour and more than 4,000 exhibitors from 95 countries expected to fill the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds through Sunday. Lena Hoffstedt, the fair's newly appointed director, said she hoped the programme — which includes panels on artificial intelligence in publishing, a live translation marathon, and a sprawling children's literature pavilion — would draw upward of 300,000 visitors over the five-day run.

Der Stadtrat von Freiburg im Breisgau hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit für die Einführung einer kommunalen Wärmeplanung gestimmt: 28 Ratsmitglieder votierten dafür, 19 dagegen, bei vier Enthaltungen. Die Abstimmung gilt als wegweisend für die Klimaschutzpolitik der Stadt; Bürgermeisterin Karoline Seifert sprach von einem „historischen Schritt in Richtung Energiegerechtigkeit". Die Grünen und die SPD hatten den Antrag gemeinsam eingebracht, während CDU und Freie Wähler geschlossen dagegenstimmten.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe in der Messe Frankfurt und erwartet in diesem Jahr rund 95.000 Fachbesucher sowie ein breites Publikum aus aller Welt. Als Ehrengast tritt Slowenien auf, dessen Verlage und Autoren — darunter die Lyrikerin Vesna Pušić und der Romancier Bojan Krstič — das Herz des internationalen Literaturprogramms bilden werden. Messedirektorin Claudia Reimann kündigte an, der Schwerpunkt liege in diesem Jahr auf Übersetzungsliteratur und digitalen Leseformaten. Die Messe läuft bis zum 19. Oktober.

The Scottish Parliament voted by 74 votes to 49 on Thursday to approve a £2.3 billion funding package for the long-delayed Edinburgh–Glasgow rail upgrade, handing Transport Minister Catriona Dempsey her first major legislative win since taking office in May. ScotRail has confirmed that construction on the electrified corridor will begin in earnest by March 2026, with full completion targeted for 2031, eventually allowing journey times between the two cities to be cut to under 30 minutes and serving an estimated 18 million passengers annually.

The Flemish Parliament voted on Thursday to ratify the coalition agreement between the N-VA, the Vlaams Belang, and the cd&v, formalising a right-leaning governing majority in Brussels after weeks of fraught negotiation. The motion passed by 71 votes in favour, with 34 against and 9 abstentions, as coalition architect Lieselot Vandenberghe hailed the deal as "a turning point for Flanders." The agreement is expected to anchor sweeping cuts to regional public-sector spending and a tightening of immigration policy over the next five years.

Der Stadtrat von Erfurt hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einem umstrittenen Wohnungsbaupaket zugestimmt, das den Bau von rund 1.200 Sozialwohnungen im Stadtgebiet vorsieht. Bei der namentlichen Abstimmung votierten 28 Ratsmitglieder dafür, 21 dagegen und vier enthielten sich. Oberbürgermeisterin Carola Wendt, die das Paket maßgeblich vorangetrieben hatte, sprach von einem „historischen Schritt für bezahlbares Wohnen in unserer Stadt". Die CDU-Fraktion, die das Vorhaben als finanziell unverantwortlich bezeichnet hatte, kündigte an, die Beschlüsse rechtlich prüfen zu lassen; die Linke und die SPD begrüßten das Ergebnis hingegen ausdrücklich.

Commuters on the Overground faced severe disruption on Thursday morning after a signalling fault near Highbury & Islington brought services on the Mildmay line to a standstill for nearly four hours, with Transport for London estimating that approximately 47,000 passengers were affected before normal operations resumed shortly before midday.

Commuters on the U6 and U3 lines in Vienna faced severe disruptions on Friday evening after a signalling fault near Westbahnhof brought services to a near-standstill for roughly four hours, stranding an estimated 47,000 passengers. Wiener Linien engineers worked through the night to isolate the fault, and full services resumed by 1:15 a.m. on Saturday. The operator urged affected travellers to seek alternative routes via tram lines D and O, though platform overcrowding at Karlsplatz was reported throughout the incident.

The Reykjavík City Council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a controversial rezoning measure that would open formerly protected green-belt land along the city's northern fringe to mixed-use residential development, with 11 councillors in favour, 8 opposed, and 2 abstentions. The motion, championed by the centre-right Independence Party and fiercely resisted by the Left-Green Movement, passed despite a packed public gallery and a last-minute petition bearing more than 14,000 signatures. "This is a pragmatic answer to a housing crisis that has left families with nowhere to turn," said Councillor Björn Sigurðsson, who led the pro-development bloc, while opposition spokesperson Lára Eiríksdóttir warned that the decision would prove deeply unpopular at the next municipal elections.

Commuters on the Northern and Jubilee lines faced severe disruptions on Thursday morning after a signalling failure at London Bridge brought both routes to a standstill for nearly three hours, with Transport for London estimating that around 47,000 passengers were affected during the peak rush. TfL engineers restored full service by 10:15 a.m., though residual delays persisted well into the afternoon.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to pass the Housing Emergency (Temporary Rent Controls) Bill, with 67 members in favour, 59 against, and 4 abstentions, after a fractious three-hour debate in which SNP housing spokesperson Fiona Drummond accused the Scottish Conservatives of "deliberately conflating supply-side failures with tenants' rights." The Greens backed the SNP administration to secure the slim majority, while Labour abstained on procedural grounds, leaving Holyrood observers to wonder whether the coalition of convenience would survive the forthcoming budget discussions.

The ongoing debate over whether to expand the Tate Modern's permanent collection to include more works from Southeast Asian artists has reignited familiar tensions between curators who favour broad geographic representation and trustees concerned about acquisition budgets that have already been stretched thin in recent years. Critics like art historian Priya Nambiar argue that the gallery's purchasing philosophy has long lagged behind its stated commitments to global cultural equity, while the museum's director, Frederik Holst, has repeatedly pointed to the institution's record on touring exhibitions as evidence of genuine engagement beyond the Western canon.

Beim packenden Stadtderby in der Regionalliga Südwest bezwang der FC Astoria Walldorf den SV Sandhausen II am Samstagabend mit 3:1 vor 2.840 Zuschauern im Astoria-Stadion. Die Tore für die Gastgeber erzielten Tobias Reinhardt (zweimal) und der überragende Mittelfeldspieler Luca Ferreira, während Leon Metzger für den Anschlusstreffer der Gäste sorgte. Mit diesem Sieg klettert Walldorf auf den dritten Tabellenplatz der Regionalliga Südwest und schickt den Rivalen aus Sandhausen tiefer in die Krise.

Brendan Okafor's brace in the 67th and 82nd minutes sealed a hard-fought 2–1 victory for Galway United over Cork City at Eamonn Deacy Park on Friday evening, pulling the home side to within three points of the League of Ireland First Division summit with just four fixtures remaining.

Die ÖBB hat am Mittwoch bekanntgegeben, dass die Weststrecke zwischen Salzburg und Wien vom 14. bis zum 21. März wegen umfangreicher Gleiserneuerungsarbeiten vollständig gesperrt wird. Rund 38.000 Fahrgäste täglich sind von der Maßnahme betroffen; als Ersatz werden Schienenersatzbusse auf der gesamten Strecke eingesetzt. „Wir bitten alle Reisenden um Verständnis und empfehlen, die Reisezeiten großzügig einzuplanen", erklärte ÖBB-Sprecher Markus Haidinger.

The architectural debate surrounding Camp Nou's ongoing redevelopment has renewed questions about whether Barcelona's obsession with sporting infrastructure comes at the expense of its historic cultural institutions, several of which — including the Gran Teatre del Liceu — have lobbied the city council for increased public funding since at least 2019. Writing in the weekend edition of El País, urban critic Marta Solivelles argued that European cities from Vienna to Amsterdam have long grappled with the same tension, yet rarely produce a coherent long-term strategy that satisfies both transit planners and arts administrators.

Commuters in Gothenburg faced severe disruptions on Monday after Västtrafik suspended all tram services on lines 3, 6, and 11 following the discovery of a critical fault in the overhead power infrastructure near Centralstationen. Engineers estimate repairs will take at least four days, with replacement bus services operating on the affected corridors in the meantime. Around 74,000 daily passengers are expected to be impacted during the outage.

The Flemish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to ratify the coalition agreement struck between the N-VA, the Vlaams Belang, and the cd&v, with 71 members backing the deal, 62 opposing it, and 4 abstaining — a majority that coalition architects say is historically thin but sufficient to govern through the full term. Parliamentary speaker Lieselotte Vandenberghe called the result "a mandate to act, not to stall," while opposition leader Joris Crombez warned that the agreement's austerity provisions would fall disproportionately on Flemish municipalities already stretched by rising social costs. The accord grants N-VA the finance portfolio and establishes a joint working group on energy transition policy to report within eighteen months.

The Stuttgart city council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a €2.3 billion extension of the U-Bahn network, connecting the outlying district of Vaihingen to the main interchange at Stadtmitte, after a fractious three-hour debate in which the SPD and the Grüne outmanoeuvred a sceptical CDU bloc. The vote passed 29 to 21, with four abstentions, and the project — overseen by Stuttgarter Straßenbahnen AG — is expected to break ground in early 2027, adding seven new stations along a 9.4-kilometre corridor that transport planners say will serve an estimated 85,000 daily passengers by the time of its projected opening in 2031.

Heidelberg Ruder Klub edged out Mainzer RV by a single length in the men's coxed four final at the Neckar Regatta on Saturday, with a capacity crowd of 4,200 lining the riverbanks in sweltering mid-July heat. Club captain Tobias Fenrich steered the winning crew home in a time of 6 minutes 48 seconds, prompting jubilant scenes on the Heidelberg waterfront. Mainzer RV lodged a formal protest over a late steering infringement, but race officials dismissed it within the hour.

The Reykjavik City Council voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a sweeping new housing affordability plan, with nineteen councillors in favour, fourteen against, and three abstentions — a margin that surprised even the plan's architects inside the ruling Left-Green alliance. Deputy Mayor Sigríður Björk Magnúsdóttir, who shepherded the proposal through two months of fractious committee hearings, called the result "a hard-won step toward a city where ordinary families can afford to stay." The opposition Independence Party had sought to delay the vote pending an independent fiscal review, but the motion to defer was itself defeated.

A late header from striker Teodor Mânzatu settled a tense Carpathian Derby on Friday evening, as CFR Cluj edged Rapid București 2–1 at the Dr. Constantin Rădulescu Stadium before a crowd of 18,450. The visitors had levelled through Andrei Florea just past the hour mark, but Mânzatu's towering effort in the 84th minute proved decisive, lifting Cluj to the top of the Liga I table ahead of the winter break.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opened its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — designed by Milan-based architect Serena Cattaneo — occupies a striking 2,400-square-metre space in Hall 4.1. Organizers at the Börsenverein des Deutschen Buchhandels expect attendance to exceed 300,000 visitors before the fair closes on Sunday.

Der Stadtrat von Freiburg im Breisgau hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einen umstrittenen Bebauungsplan für das Rieselfeld-Nord-Erweiterungsgebiet verabschiedet: 27 Stimmen entfielen auf Ja, 19 auf Nein, bei vier Enthaltungen. Bürgermeisterin Saskia Wehrle (Grüne) sprach von einem „wichtigen Schritt für bezahlbaren Wohnraum", während der Fraktionsvorsitzende der CDU, Konrad Pfisterer, die Entscheidung scharf kritisierte und vor einer Überlastung der städtischen Infrastruktur warnte.

The Scottish Parliament voted on Thursday to allocate £4.2 million in emergency arts funding, a measure championed by Culture Secretary Fiona Kellacher that passed with 74 votes in favour and 41 against, with 8 abstentions. The grant is set to underwrite the Edinburgh International Festival's expanded 2025 edition, which will open on 1 August at the Usher Hall and run for three weeks, featuring conductors and performers drawn from over thirty countries.

Rail passengers travelling between Salzburg and Munich face significant disruption this week after ÖBB and Deutsche Bahn jointly announced that the cross-border Salzburg–Munich corridor will be closed for engineering works from Monday 14 July through Sunday 20 July, with an estimated 38,000 daily travellers affected. Replacement bus services have been arranged along the route, though journey times are expected to increase by up to ninety minutes. The closure, which centres on upgrades to the signalling infrastructure near Freilassing, is part of a broader €240 million modernisation programme targeting the southern Bavarian network.

Defending champions Rosenborg BK were held to a tense 1–1 draw by Lillestrøm SK at Lerkendal Stadion in Trondheim on Saturday evening, a result that leaves both sides level on points at the top of the Eliteserien table with just four rounds remaining. Håkon Melvær broke the deadlock in the 34th minute for the hosts before Jonas Elstad levelled with a coolly dispatched penalty twelve minutes from time, sending the 18,240 supporters inside the ground home in stunned silence.

Der Wiener Gemeinderat hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einen umstrittenen Beschluss zur Ausweitung der kommunalen Wohnbauförderung verabschiedet: 52 Abgeordnete stimmten dafür, 41 dagegen, bei drei Enthaltungen. SPÖ-Stadtrat Gregor Falkenbach bezeichnete die Reform als „längst überfälligen Schritt zur sozialen Gerechtigkeit", während die ÖVP-Fraktionsvorsitzende Miriam Stöcklhuber von einem „verantwortungslosen Griff in die Stadtkasse" sprach und eine Sondersitzung des Stadtparlaments forderte. Die Grünen, die den Antrag gemeinsam mit der SPÖ eingebracht hatten, zeigten sich zufrieden mit dem Ergebnis.

Wegen des Bundesliga-Derbys zwischen dem FC St. Pauli und dem HSV am Samstag, dem 14. September, sperrt die Hamburger Hochbahn ab 13 Uhr mehrere U-Bahn-Stationen rund um das Millerntor-Stadion weiträumig für den regulären Fahrgastverkehr; betroffen sind die Linien U2 und U3, und die Behörde rechnet mit bis zu 62.000 beeinträchtigten Fahrgästen. Das Spiel, das erste Stadtduell der Saison in der 1. Bundesliga, endete vor ausverkauftem Haus mit 2:1 für St. Pauli, wobei Stürmer Tomáš Krejčí in der 88. Minute den Siegtreffer erzielte.

The Scottish Parliament voted by a razor-thin majority on Thursday to pass the Housing Emergency (Rent Stabilisation) Bill, with 65 members supporting the measure against 59 opposed and 4 abstentions, delivering a significant if fragile victory for the SNP-led government after weeks of fractious cross-party negotiations. Labour MSPs voted in a bloc against the bill, warning that rent caps would deter new development and deepen the very crisis the legislation claimed to address. First Minister Catriona Dreich, who had staked considerable personal capital on the vote, thanked Green co-operation for securing the margin.

The Reykjavík Chamber Music Festival, which opens at Harpa Concert Hall on 14 March and runs through 22 March, is drawing unusual attention this year — not only for its programme of Nordic premieres conducted by festival director Sigríður Ólafsdóttir, but because Strætó, the city's public bus operator, has announced a targeted service expansion on routes 1, 6, and 14 linking the Old Harbour district to Harpa, effective for the entire festival duration, in order to accommodate the expected surge of some 18,000 concertgoers travelling without private vehicles.

Der Stadtrat von Graz hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit einen umstrittenen Beschluss zur Neugestaltung der städtischen Wohnbauförderung verabschiedet: 28 Stimmen votierten dafür, 24 dagegen, bei drei Enthaltungen. Die regierende Koalition aus ÖVP und SPÖ setzte sich damit gegen die oppositionellen Fraktionen von FPÖ und Grünen durch. Stadtrat Benedikt Lerchenthaler, der das Vorhaben federführend verhandelt hatte, sprach von einem „notwendigen Schritt zur Sicherung bezahlbaren Wohnraums für alle Grazerinnen und Grazer".

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for a five-day run that is expected to draw upwards of 300,000 visitors to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds, with Norwegian literature taking centre stage as the guest-of-honour nation this year. Publisher representatives from more than 90 countries will present new titles across every conceivable genre, while a headline evening lecture series — curated by veteran literary critic Marlene Schöttler — will unfold nightly in Hall 4.1. Tickets for individual evening events are priced at €18, though the full trade pass remains considerably steeper.

Benedikt Szymański's brace in the final twelve minutes salvaged a dramatic 2–2 draw for Górnik Zabrze against visiting Raków Częstochowa at the Stadion im. Ernesta Pohla on Saturday evening, a result that leaves both clubs locked on 34 points in the PKO BP Ekstraklasa table with six rounds remaining.

Commuters on Frankfurt's S-Bahn network faced fresh disruption on Wednesday after a signalling fault near Konstablerwache brought three lines to a standstill for nearly four hours, stranding an estimated 47,000 passengers during the morning rush. DB Regio, which operates the service under contract to the Rhein-Main-Verkehrsverbund, dispatched replacement buses along the affected corridors but warned that delays were likely to persist into the early afternoon. Engineers traced the fault to ageing relay infrastructure installed in the early 1980s, and RMV confirmed it is accelerating a planned upgrade of the Konstablerwache interlocking system, a project valued at roughly €34 million and tentatively scheduled for completion by mid-2027.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse öffnet am 15. Oktober ihre Tore für das Fachpublikum und präsentiert in diesem Jahr mit Norwegen einen besonders literaturaffinen Gastlandauftritt. Die Schriftstellerin Ingrid Valebrokk, einer der bekanntesten Stimmen der norwegischen Gegenwartsliteratur, wird gemeinsam mit dem Suhrkamp Verlag ihren neuen Roman „Die stille Küste" vorstellen. Erwartet werden rund 86.000 Fachbesucher aus über 100 Ländern; der Eintritt für Branchenteilnehmer kostet 78 Euro pro Tag.

The Scottish Parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to reject a proposed amendment to the Renters' Rights Bill that would have extended tenant protections to short-term holiday lets, with 63 members voting against and 58 in favour, while the Scottish National Party accused the Conservatives of "cynical procedural obstruction" after three SNP members were briefly barred from the chamber floor ahead of the division.

The Flemish parliament voted narrowly on Thursday to approve a contentious housing reform bill championed by the N-VA, with 71 votes in favour and 64 against and 3 abstentions, after a debate that stretched past midnight. The bill, which strips municipal councils of certain planning override powers and centralises zoning decisions in Brussels, was fiercely opposed by the Groen and Vooruit parties, whose spokespersons warned it would devastate affordable-housing provision in smaller communes. N-VA deputy floor leader Lieselotte Vandenberghe hailed the outcome as "a generational correction to decades of planning paralysis," while Groen parliamentarian Bastiaan Claerhout vowed to challenge the legislation before the Council of State within a fortnight.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, literary agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, which will present a sprawling programme of readings, panel discussions, and installations exploring contemporary Italian writing across the fairground's central Hall 4.1. Organizers expect upward of 300,000 visitors over the five-day run, with tickets available from €18 per day.

Der Stadtrat von Erfurt hat am Donnerstagabend mit knapper Mehrheit den Haushaltsentwurf für das kommende Jahr verabschiedet: 28 Stimmen entfielen auf Ja, 21 auf Nein, bei drei Enthaltungen. Die rot-grüne Koalition unter Oberbürgermeisterin Carolin Wettig setzte sich damit gegen die Fraktion der CDU und die erstarkten Freien Wähler durch, die gemeinsam eine Ablehnung des Etats gefordert hatten. Wettig sprach anschließend von einem „Signal der Handlungsfähigkeit" für die Landeshauptstadt.

The Scottish Parliament voted on Thursday by 74 votes to 51 to approve a landmark cultural funding bill championed by Culture Secretary Fiona Drummond, which will inject £18 million annually into regional arts programmes — a decision that comes just days before the Edinburgh International Festival opens its 78th edition at the Usher Hall and venues across the capital, with artistic director Callum Strachan describing the timing as "a rare alignment of political will and artistic ambition."

Rowers from across Scandinavia converged on Oslo's Frognerkilen bay on Saturday for the 41st Holmenkollen Regatta, where the Norwegian national squad edged out a dominant Swedish crew by a mere half-length in the men's coxless four final to claim the gold pennant. A crowd of 6,200 lined the banks in crisp autumn sunshine, watching Erlend Vassvik steer his team through a blistering last 500 metres to seal victory in a race time of 6 minutes 14 seconds.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, drawing publishers, agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt for five days of deals, debates, and readings. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — designed by architect Serena Cattaneo — sprawls across two halls and features works by over sixty Italian authors translated into a dozen languages. Organisers expect upwards of 300,000 visitors before the fair closes on Sunday.

Braga clinched a dramatic 2–1 victory over Benfica at the Estádio Municipal de Braga on Saturday, with Tomás Ferreira's stoppage-time header proving the decisive moment in one of the Primeira Liga's most fiercely contested derbies of the season. A crowd of 28,400 roared throughout, and midfielder Cláudio Neves was named man of the match after an industrious performance that unsettled Benfica's backline from the first whistle.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, drawing publishers, agents, and literary enthusiasts from more than ninety countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for five days of readings, panel discussions, and rights negotiations. This year's guest of honour is Slovenia, whose pavilion — designed by architect Teja Remic — foregrounds a generation of writers largely unknown to German-language audiences. Organising director Hannelore Voss described the programme as "the most ambitious in a decade," with over four thousand exhibitors registered and single-day tickets priced at eighteen euros.

Wegen umfangreicher Gleisbauarbeiten auf der S-Bahn-Linie S3 zwischen Darmstadt und Frankfurt Hauptbahnhof, die vom 14. bis zum 21. Juli andauern werden, empfiehlt die DB Regio betroffenen Fahrgästen die Nutzung von Schienenersatzverkehr — just zu jenem Zeitpunkt, da das Internationale Jazzfestival Darmstadt in der Centralstation seine diesjährige Ausgabe eröffnet. Festivalleiter Moritz Schellhaas zeigte sich gleichwohl optimistisch: „Unsere Besucher aus Frankfurt und dem Rhein-Main-Gebiet sind eingefleischte Jazzfans, die auch einen Umweg in Kauf nehmen." Das Festival, das von 15. bis 20. Juli läuft, erwartet laut Veranstalter rund 4.200 Gäste und präsentiert unter anderem das Kölner Saxophon-Quartett sowie die amerikanische Pianistin Delara Nouri.

The Flemish parliament narrowly approved a controversial austerity package on Thursday, with 72 votes in favour and 68 against, after nearly fourteen hours of fractious debate that tested the resolve of the ruling coalition. The agreement, brokered jointly by N-VA and the cd&v, imposes a three-year freeze on public-sector wages and cuts subsidies to municipal cultural centres across the region. Opposition leader Sofie Vandenberghe of Vooruit accused the government of "governing against ordinary working people," while Flemish Minister-President Lasse De Coninck defended the measures as fiscally unavoidable. No abstentions were recorded.

Hoffenheim claimed a gritty 2–1 victory over Werder Bremen at PreZero Arena on Saturday evening, a result that lifts them to sixth place in the Bundesliga table with eight matches remaining. Marius Steinfeld opened the scoring in the 23rd minute before Werder's Tomasz Krawczyk levelled just after the break, only for substitute Devante Achampong to nod home a 78th-minute winner to send the home crowd into raptures. The attendance was recorded at 24,302.

Die Frankfurter Buchmesse eröffnet am 15. Oktober ihre 76. Ausgabe auf dem Messegelände Frankfurt und erwartet in diesem Jahr erneut über 4.000 Aussteller aus mehr als 100 Ländern. Als Gastland wurde Spanien ausgewählt, und die spanische Schriftstellerin Pilar Montoya wird am Eröffnungsabend aus ihrem neuen Roman lesen. Veranstalter ist der Börsenverein des Deutschen Buchhandels, der das Programm unter das Motto „Lesen verbindet" gestellt hat.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opened its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — curated by Chiara Nardelli and designed around the theme of contemporary migration narratives — has already attracted long queues on the opening morning. Organisers expect upwards of 300,000 visitors over the five-day fair.

The Reykjavík Arts Festival opens its 48th edition on Friday at Harpa Concert Hall, with an opening night programme curated by Sigríður Björnsdóttir that spans electroacoustic performance, contemporary dance, and a rare staging of Icelandic composer Hjálmar Sigurðsson's chamber opera "Askur." Festival director Einar Magnússon said organisers expect more than 12,000 visitors over the eleven-day run, with tickets priced from 2,500 Icelandic króna for individual events.

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opened its doors on Wednesday for its 76th edition, drawing publishers, agents, and literary luminaries from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds. This year's guest of honour is Italy, whose pavilion — designed by architect Serena Calvi — sprawls across an entire hall and showcases more than two hundred titles in translation. Organisers expect some 300,000 visitors over the five-day fair, which runs through Sunday.

The Flemish parliament narrowly approved a contentious housing reform bill on Thursday, with 72 members voting in favour and 61 against, after a bruising overnight debate in which N-VA and Vlaams Belang clashed repeatedly over rent-control provisions. The Grüne-affiliated Groen faction abstained on the final tally, depriving the coalition of a more comfortable margin. Social Affairs Minister Lieselotte Vandenberghe, who shepherded the legislation through committee, called the result "a foundation for affordable housing across the region."

The Frankfurter Buchmesse opens its doors on Wednesday, welcoming publishers, agents, and readers from more than 100 countries to the Messe Frankfurt fairgrounds for what organisers have billed as the largest gathering of the international book trade since the pandemic. This year's Guest of Honour is Slovenia, and the Slovenian pavilion — designed by architect Maja Oblak — occupies a prominent position in Hall 4. The fair runs until Sunday, with free admission for school groups on Thursday morning.

Wegen umfangreicher Gleissanierungsarbeiten auf der S-Bahn-Stammstrecke wird die Münchner S1 zwischen Ostbahnhof und Pasing vom 14. bis zum 28. Juli vollständig gesperrt; die Bayerische Eisenbahngesellschaft schätzt, dass täglich rund 87.000 Fahrgäste auf Ersatzbusse oder die U-Bahn umsteigen müssen.
